review_text: UPDATE below: Original review - I have longed to try one of these of many different brands. After research and reading dozens and dozens of reviews, I landed on the Meater Plus. I opened it up and found it to be in a beautiful wooden box which is actually it's charging station. Comes with a AA battery for charging. I downloaded the app. I am 60 - so not a tech wizard. I was able to sync with app very easily. It did take a few minutes (maybe updating as well). I just used it to cook a beef roast and it worked perfectly. One thing I would note - I was going for a medium rare - and "upped" the suggested temp of 135 to 140 because I was nervous... the Meater Plus counts the resting time in the finished temp! So, I ended up with a little to the medium than to the medium rare. I am going to trust the Meater Plus next time. It notifies you of when to take your food out and then reminds you when the resting is done. You can follow the progress on the app on your phone. Has a lovely dial that shows where you are in the cooking progress. I am very, very impressed. I love it. I am eager to try it in my all natural turkey for thanksgiving! It's just a real handy tool with a modern twist. It's a little bit of an investment, but I think it's worth it. Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful. UPDATED review 4/1/2021.... The more I use this thermometer the more I love it. I have learned to "trust" the resting time - I have read other reviews that report overcooked food and I wonder if they might not be trusting the process. However, could also be faulty items. I am grateful that my thermometer has worked perfectly each time and I could not be happier. It has taken so much stress out of my cooking life. I won't roast without it. Or cook a thick steak without it. Pretty much anything you need temp on. I am not compensated in ANY way for my reviews and I am sharing my honest experience and opinions. UPDATE 2022; Therms will NOT stay connected to device. NO tech support. Takes WEEKS to get a reply via email and then it is truly worthless. I am so disappointed because they (I have two pluses and a block) for about 4 or 5 months and then just will NOT stay linked. SUPER frustrating both in lack of support they 'say' is there and then that they lasted just a few months. NOT a cheap lesson either. I invested over $450.00 at this point. I will sadly say I can no longer recommend these in any way.

I had high hopes for this meat probe after my Inkbird wireless probe wire died. I was watching Guga on YouTube endorsing this probe. I thought it would be a good probe to buy. I do a lot of steaks on the grill, oven/stove, and BBQ on the smoker. Red flag #1 - I purchase before Thanksgiving for my turkey. I should have noticed something was wrong when it would loose connection through the oven door. I have a cheap Frigidaire. I would need to set the base on the oven handle or on the floor right next to the door for connection. Even with the distance so short, it would still intermittently loose connection. I tried a few reverse sear steaks in the oven at 250 degrees. It has been wintertime, so I wrote the performance off as maybe just an issue with an oven door. Red flag#2-I decide to do some steaks on indirect heat on my Weber Kettle. You know the kind, the one that has been around for 70 years. The think black material one. Well, I put in a new battery in the receiver just in case. I put the probe in my 1 1/2 inch ribeye. Inside the house, right next to the receiver, I could read the base temperature of the raw steak. I moved the steak to the outside grill. As soon as I put the steak on the indirect heat side, I could see the internal temperature and ambient temperature on the app. As soon as I put the lid on the kettle grill. I lost connection within a minute or two. I opened up the lid and it connected. I closed the lid again and went inside 25 feet away. Within a minute or two I lost connection again. I went outside again, I opened the lid, with the receiver on the handle of the grill. The receiver was blinking green for connected, but I could not connect through the app. I tried for several minutes to get connection, but it continued to work intermittently. I gave up and found my old gauge thermometer and about cried when it said 135 degrees. Red Flag#3- I contacted Meater support (Apption Labs) for help. They advised me my app permissions may be blocked, which they were not. Told me some cooking appliances are good at blocking signals. They told me to keep the base close to the probe. I guess 1-2 feet is too far. They sent weblinks on range expectations and using Meater Cloud. Maybe that would work it the product worked more then 1 ft apart. No offer to warranty an exchange. Conclusion: Don't waste your money. Stick to brands that standby their products. I will stay with Inkbird and ThermoWorks ThermoPen. I appreciate the prompt response from their support. But they do not warranty and stand by their product. I am glad I found a deal on this one for a bit off. It was $79.99 for the Meater Plus with a list price of $99.99. So at least I only threw $79.99 in the trash instead of $99.99. I guess the $20 I saved there will pay for a new ThermoPen. Good luck grillers and BBQ enthusiasts. If you still buy one and it performs as well as mind did, well I told you so!!

I've had this thing for nearly a year and tried to use it most weeks but unfortunately it's almost always a terrible experience. I'm going to list the issues I can remember: Sometimes even though the probe has been in the base station, the contacts haven't quite been touching properly and so the battery on the probe is dead and unable to be used when you need it. Nothing happens to alert you to this, you just find out when you need to start cooking and have to grab a better thermometer instead. Sometimes for no reason the base station will disconnect from the probe mid cook and tell you to move it nearer to the probe. Even putting the base station on the grill itself doesn't remedy this, it will just refuse to reconnect until you physically put the probe back in the base station. Which means potentially taking the very hot probe out of whatever you are cooking and then contaminating the base station with uncooked meat contact from the probe. Despite the range being advertised, the phone will often fail to connect to the base station if it is on the other side of the window. Sometimes I want to smoke something outdoors while I am myself indoors for the cook, but this is often not possible without losing connection. I ended up using a spare second phone to act as a bridge which sits outside with the base station but this work around is pretty ridiculous for an $80 thermometer. Sometimes the thermometer disconnects mid cook and doesn't notify you. I have once found a tri-tip that got to 140 before I noticed the thermometer had disconnected so the alert never told me to take it out. The app is a real nuissance to use. Often I want to pull out a brisket at say 195°f knowing it will climb to 203°f, but the app will try to outsmart me, so if I set the desired cook temp to 195°f it will tell me to pull the meat out below that so it will climb to 195°f. I don't need the app to try to do this for me and it cannot be disabled. What I end up doing is setting a cook temp of 225°f and then setting up a custom alarm to ring when it goes above 195°f. This work around gets the desired result but it shouldn't be a constant battle with to get it to work how you need it to. On some occasions I have been ready to cook but the app wouldn't allow me to proceed with the cook until performing software updates. If it isn't a safety issue the user should have the option to update later, as I have had cooks I was late to get started due to having to wait for the Meater app to update. Sure it only takes 5 or so minutes but that time matters if you are cooking lots of courses that all need to have pretty precision timing. I ultimately always end up using my cheaper thermopro because it never messes me around like the meater does.

There is nothing more important when smoking meat than the ability to maintain a steady temperature at the desired level for the Cook. Because pellet smokers do not give an accurate ambient reading due to the placement of their sensors, this sounds like the perfect product as it reads both the internal temperature and the ambient temperature, which is key to a proper smoke. Unfortunately, the ambient temperature reading with this device is wildly inaccurate. After smoking ribs for four hours I wrapped them in heavy duty foil to finish the smoke at 250° in my oven. My oven is dead accurate, as confirmed by the placement of two separate oven thermometers inside. While the ambient temperature in the oven was 250°, the meter read 223°. I phoned and they told me that this would’ve been the accurate reading at the point of the meat where the MEATER was sticking out and that cold bubbles coming out of the meat would lower the temperature. Cold bubbles after I’ve been smoking for four hours? Well, I asked, how then can I test to see that this device gives an accurate ambient reading? There’s no way you can test it to see if it’s accurate, I was told. Can I just put it in an oven by itself, I asked? Yes you can, but we wouldn’t accept that as a test of accuracy, even if other thermometers in the oven read a different temperature. And they told me that the ambient reading doesn’t matter anyway-the only thing that really matters is the temperature of the meat, but if it doesn’t read the ambient accurately, how do I know it reads the meat accurately? Can I do a Cook using both this and a Thermopro T20, the very highly regarded wired meat thermometer to trust the accuracy of the internal meat reading? No I was told, we wouldn’t accept that as a valid test either. In summary, this device appears to be very inaccurate, and according to the company, there is no way you can test it to see if it is. Caveat Emptor.

review_title: Ambient temperature can't be used to control cooking temp (i.e. Offset Smoke)
review_text: The ambient temp probe reads what Meater refers to as a "micro-climate" around the meat which is created by the cooler meat temp mixing with the actual heated air in the cooking environment. In my experience, on an offset smoker, this temp is often 30-50F cooler than the actual cooking temp inside the smoker. If you're expecting to control your fueling of the smoker based on the ambient temp readings, you're going to struggle. As the meat warms, the ambient temp gets closer to an accurate temp so you can't simply add 50 degrees or 30 degrees because it's going to vary. It simply can't be used to control cooking temp. Frankly, I'm not sure what situation it is useful in. Who cares what that microclimate is? If you use the probe in an environment where there's high enough airflow to disrupt that micro-climate (like a convection oven where a fan is moving the air) then it reads accurately. In a low and slow cooking situation where the air flow is pretty light it's not going to be useful. Again I'm not really sure what situation it is useful in. The other issue with this whole micro-climate situation is during a low and slow cook where you're trying to hold the smoker around 225 and this ambient probe is reading 175-200 and your expected finishing temp is somewhere between 200 and 210, it really seems to struggle with the expected cooking time. I don't know what their algorithm is for calculating that but I expect an ambient temp, which falls below your finishing temp, is going to drastically affect the ability to get an accurate finish time. In my experience, I spent a lot of time with an "Estimating" rather than an actual finish time and even when I did get a finish time, it was very inconsistent and often very unrealistic. Meater does have documentation on this micro-climate situation, but it's not clear up front. If you're like me you'll buy the thing thinking, "Hey this is great, two probes in one with a wireless option and a phone app." Just to find out it's not really useful. I asked Meater for a refund and was told it's working as expected, which I suppose it is, once you realize they've created a probe with a faulty design that will accurately read a temperature in a "micro-climate" which is useless to the user.

review_title: These are garbage, and customer service is a joke. Here’s what happened.
review_text: I ordered two of these two years ago and tried a few cooks. I could never really get it to work, so I stuck one in the drawer and gave one to a buddy hoping he could get it work. I don’t know if he ever did. I recently got it out to try it again and smoked a brisket. The temperature showed different than my other thermometers so before my next brisket cook, I wanted to test it. I couldn’t get the ambient temperature to show, so I called customer service. After a half hour of trying an ice bath and other things, the rep wasn’t able to help me. I called the next day, the day of the cook, to try again. I spent an hour and 15 minutes on the phone with customer service. In the end, she determined my prob was broken and wanted me to buy a new probe, since I’d purchased it two years prior. She said that it was out of warranty.I explained that I’m not a fool - so far 0% have worked, The Amazon reviews that I read said the same thing about problems with the ambient temperature reading. So the company knows about this major problem. I told her that I’m not going to waste my money buying another probe. She reached out to her boss and they said there’s nothing they could do. I told her the only way I was going to buy a new one is if, when the new probe doesn’t work, I’ll return it. She once again checked with her boss and told me no, they wouldn’t accept a return when it doesn’t work. That tells me that there is no warranty at all that they honor. This seems absurd to me. In my experience, Meater is an absolutely terrible company.

review_title: Once the sell you do NOT expect t to be reliable and do not expect the support to care one bit.
review_text: Originally I loved this product and even wrote a glowing review about the functionality! I also mentioned in this review the great customer support I received when it lost connection the second time I tried to use it.. the rep person got me up amd running again and explained that the product will sometime “inadvertently go offline” and explained how to delete the app and start over with a couple of extra steps. After two more uses my product did this again, and despite my attempts, it would not reconnect so I called support again. After 30 minutes on the call as the rep tried various instructions to reset it, she determined that my device was faulty and , after a long hold, she came back to report that a new one is on the way, She also apologized for the inconvenience .(I was having a dinner party that evening and was serving a prime filet of tenderloin dry aged roast of which I spent $197). I asked if I should send mine back to them and she said that in this situation it was unnecessary. I then tossed it in the trash amd awaited my new one. What transpired since the has been the worst customer service I’ve ever had to listen to. In short, I was sent a probe. That’s it. It took two days to get a person on the phone to ask for this situation to be rectified, and today I was told that if I wanted the charger block with the probe, the best they could do is offer me 50% off for the device! This is no joke. I have only had this product since beginning of January. I have have no idea where to go from here and I’m venting right now until I figure out my next step. Huge disappointment. Don’t do business with this company.

review_title: This product does not provide an accurate temperature for y
review_text: I have absolutely no idea how this product is rated so high. The Good: - The wooden charging case is a nice touch. It looks and feels rustic with a modern touch. - The Meater itself, looks and feels sleek and sturdy. The Bad: - The internal temps are all over the place. Just now, I set the cook for a NY strip - 130° - lowest of the medium-rare in the app. I pulled it within 10 seconds of the alert going off and the temp read 138° (wasn't paying attention to the app, as I was cooking the rest of dinner). I rested it on a wire rack, elevated from the pan, and watched the temp rise to 145 - fine.. It's the top of mid-rare, and the bottom of medium, I can deal with that. What came out was top of medium (at best) though was mostly mid-well. All this to say, that the first time I used the product, I set it at 145 and I pulled it off to reveal a rare (maaaaybe low threshold of mid-rare) steak - same cut and quality. The temps have been consistently, and very much in contrast to the final product. - Much less of a concern, but annoying - The charging case functions on a AAA battery.. Dwight D Eisenhower was using this same charging dock. Figure it out, Meater. tl;dr - I would absolutely never purchase this again. At the price point, bells and whistles aren't necessary, but if I'm buying a plug-and-play product, I want it to function as it was intended. This product does not do that.

review_title: Great idea but not accurate at all.
review_text: I really wanted this probe to be good but unfortunately I got to say it is far from worth the money you pay. I bbq probably every weekend and spend a lot of money on meat. Good meat is not cheap and temperature monitoring is obviously a key element in producing a good pice of bbq. I’m usually not one for writing reviews but I have had my MEATER for over a year now and here’s why I gave a negative rating. My last cook I used my MEATER on was for a 17 pound brisket. I like to smoke my briskets overnight and did so. In the morning I wrapped my meat and stuck the MEATER in the flat side and my Traeger prob in the point side and back in the smoker it goes. Brisket is made up of two muscles that cook in different ways so you want to monitor them independently if possible. After about 2 hours or so I noticed my Traeger prob ( Point) reading at about 176 and my MEATER ( Flat )hitting at about 152. I have cooked many Briskets in my day and immediately new something was up when I saw these so far apart in temperature. At this point I have quit a bit of issues with my MEATER probe as far as accuracy goes but I decided to give it on last benefit of the doubt. I thought maybe the flat side stalled for some reason (thermal stall happens at about 155/170) so I flipped it around and waited an hour. No luck. They were now reading 153 and 177. I flipped the brisket back around pulled pulled the MEATER probe out of the flat, pulled the Traeger prob out of the point, inserted the Traeger probe back into the flat and now my flat is reading at 168. The difference in temperature is usually about 10 degrees or less, if it goes any further you end up with one side overcooked or you have to separate them which I’m my opinion can cause issues. I also used a Thermapen MKII in both spots to verify that the MEATER was giving an inaccurate reading and indeed my Thermapen read exactly what my Traeger probe was reading. In the end this product is a great idea but if you are serious about BBq and spend good money on meat I would not recommend this product. Just get yourself a Thermapen and call it a day.

After purchasing the Meater + I had such high hopes for it. The reviews were generally positive, and I thought it would be great to have so that I did not need to camp out near my grill, and I could use while cooking steaks, roasts, tri-tip, etc... I only used it a few times, but there was a different problem each time. At first, I was my own fault that I did not realize that the base needed to be kept near the Meater. I put the thermometer in my steak, but left the base stuck to the fridge. That led to a "connection error" when I would get more than about 10 feet away from the grill. Easy enough to fix. The next issue was not so simple. This time I made sure that the Meater was inserted properly, the base was stuck to the outside of the grill, and I was able to go in the house, yet within minutes, it said that my steak was over 200 degrees! I must have charcoal by now... fortunately, I knew there was no way it cooked that fast and I had a cheap instant-read thermometer that accurately read the IT at around 130, almost ready for a perfect medium rare... I decided to try again, and this time the ambient temperature inside the grill was way off! It quickly got up over 500 degrees and gave me a Warning that the Meater was over heating. It eventually climbed to over 800 degrees!... the max temp on my Rec Teq RT-1250 is 500 degrees, so that seemed a bit excessive. Especially, given that the reading on the grill was pretty stable between 500-506 during the entire cook. By this point, I was convinced I bought a dud. It happens. When companies start to mass produce things, inevitably there is going to be one with a defect, and I was unlucky to get it. So I contacted their support team. It took 2 days to get back to me. They asked questions about the probe, but by they time they finally determined it was faulty and sent me a return label to exchange for a new one, it had been a week, and I was already at my 30 days with Amazon, so I returned with Amazon and got my money back. Pretty disappointing all the way around. I really wanted to enjoy this product.

review_title: UPDATE: Don't waste you money! Doesn’t Last Long…the Meater or the Warranty!
review_text: UPDATE: I finally getting rid of the Meater Plus I have, because of the connection issue, but because the trustworthy of the temp when I leave my phone outside and it can read the temp for awhile. I have two, they both did the same thing. Everything seems to be disposable any more, apparently the Meater is right in there. I have purchased two Meater and both stopped working properly. Yesterday I tried to smoke a pork roast for pulled port and the Meater seemed to be working fine. I have to leave my cell phone on a table on the patio so it stays connected. So, from what I had researched, my roast should have taken 2-1/2 hours to smoke, this was confirmed by the Meater, so I felt comfortable & happy. I checked on the hour and at the point it should have been ready, the Meater read more time. It was a cold day so I knew this would happen. By the time I took the meat off of the Traeger, the Meater was telling me 2 more hours!! I took the meat off and I had a tough, dry and overcooked pork roast. This is the second time I had a ruined roast because of the Meater, the first one was from my other Meater. I tried the newer plus because it said it had a greater range, I still had to leave my cell phone outside. So sad because I had bragged about how amazing it was and encouraged family & friends to purchase one. So money down the drain from the 2 Meaters and 2 very nice cuts of meat! The warranty is only 30 days on mine, I checked!!

review_title: you will be tempted to buy but read my review first
review_text: I purchased not only this Meater product but some of their other products like Meater Block. Seemed conceptually the perfect product for smoking, especially wireless ability. Now the reality. The product is not accurate. Had probes next to each other spinning of not only massive differences in temperature but not even showing at all temperatures on 1 or more. Next and worse, notice this company has no customer service number - there is a reason, it is a farce. You have have wait for days to get a response. Aside from a front store/warehouse in the USA, there is no American representatives who you can call live. When you do get through with their online form, they are nasty and constantly insistent their product is perfect and you are to blame (I am a master griller and not taking about the retail products). They string you along and do not honor until after the period is over the 30 day money back period. So I ask you to be patient until other products who have real customer service come along or you will regret for this overpriced product. Never have I seen a company in decades of my existence act the way they have. I know, there is a tendency not to read the 1 stars but there is a story there. Tread carefully. If they try this game on you too, remember to call your credit card company and complain they are provided you a defective product and it is at their cost they must come to get. If they refuse, tell credit card company what the company is trying to do and they will block monies of going to them. Sad to have something with right concept just have attitude customer is to be played with, especially for the price point they have this out.

review_title: Works great....when it works. :-(  SUPPORT IS HORRIBLE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  DON'T BUY!!!!!!!!!!
review_text: My Meater worked great for the first 8 months. Since then every time I would pick it up to use it the battery would be dead (as in the AAA battery) in the charging block. After changing that battery for the third or fourth time, I watched the charging block for a week and the LED would go from flashing green, to flashing red, to off -- and after doing this for a week the battery would be dead. I have religiously cleaned the probe after every use and there can be nothing left on it, I have also cleaned the contacts on the charging block and ..... nothing. I reached out to support and I've just heard crickets chirping...... EDIT: I heard back from support!!! It only took them three days to get back to me and told me I had to setup a call with a support person -- which there were no scheduled openings for two days. So, I did that -- all they did was say "YUP, sounds like it's broken. Send it back to us and if we verify it is broken, we will send you a new one". Well, I send it to them -- gets there in TWO DAYS (this is important). After two days they finally say "YUP, it's broken, we'll send you a new one. You'll get information when it ships." After three days I still have received no notification, I reach back out to support....crickets again for three days. Finally hear back from support that there was a screwup on their end and it was supposed to be shipped, but didn't (and they still have not told me why it didn't). So, they setup an other one to ship to me and are sending me a bottle opener, oooo, wow, for my troubles. So they sent this A WEEK AGO and it still is not there. Remember I sent it and they had it in two days!!! STAY AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY AND PRODUCT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

review_title: App is Poorly Designed, Difficult to Use
review_text: I really like the convenience of being able to connect my phone to a Bluetooth thermometer to gauge how well a smoke is coming along, but the app that they use to connect the phone to the thermometer is one of the worst I have ever seen. It frequently (like every couple minutes) annoys me with notifications when I'm already paying attention to it. The interface itself is counterintuitive, functionalities are either missing, dont work or not where I would expect them to be. The top is all off, I just got thrown an error right before a smoke that I was unable to connect to their MEATER cloud, which completely blocked me from using my device. Something like this shouldn't be necessary to use something as simple as a thermometer. Poor app design that causes me significant headache on a regular basis. I will be looking elsewhere in the next time I'm in the market for something like this and I suggest you do the same.

review_title: Warning: Very lengthy setup before you can use it.
review_text: I had used meater for a while. After a couple of months when starting to use it I got the message that it had a low charge. I went ahead anyway and got most of the way through cooking the fish I was cooking. I replaced the battery in the charger. Usually once I put the probe back into the charger the red meater icon on my phone will go out. But after this incident it never went out and is still on. I tried various things: restarting the phone, deleting and reinstalling the app, buying a new meater. Nothing worked. Having bought a new meater I thought I was set. But when I had put the fish in the oven and opened the meter app it insisted on going through a whole series of instructions-which I didn’t need because I already used it. Then it insisted on my setting up a cloud account, it insisted on my registering the product, all before I could use the meter to monitor the cooking of my fish. I tried to bypass these things so I could get on with monitoring my fish but it wouldn’t let me. I finally reconciled myself to having to give my personal information to them – why? I already paid for it, why do you need my personal information to sell to marketers? There was no option for not setting up a cloud account. Why are you shoving this down my throat? Why do you give no warning that someone has to go through all this rigmarole before they can use the app? In the middle of my pissed off state I realize that my fish was cooking. I went to the oven to take it out and it was slightly burnt. To add insult to injury after I thought I had the app ready to use it informed me that I had to download an updated version of the app. Why? I just downloaded the app from their website. Apparently they don’t bother to give you the latest version.

review_title: You don't always get what you pay for.
review_text: I purchased this after extensive review and figured with the price point and the improvements I could count on this to be a reliable product. I was wrong. It all started very well. I setup the probe, fully charged it and set up my first cook. It would be a relatively long 5 hr cook. Everything went well for about 3.5 hours. The app was working, the probe appeared to be giving accurate data. At the 3.5 hour point, it went south...fast. The base and probe wouldn't stay connected. The base was about 5 ft. from the probe. It couldn't have been closer without being inside the grill. Then when that failed, the probe refused to stay connected to my phone via BT or WiFi. The ambient and food temp also began to show incorrectly and from using an instant read was at least 15 degrees off on the meat and probably 30 on the ambient. I was only able to get it to reconnect by removing the probe from the meat, cleaning it and putting it back in the base. Once it reconnected, I removed it and put it back in the meat, only to find I'd lost all my cook information from the original setup. That's not even the worst part. I was already in contact with MEATER+'s customer support for something unrelated. When I mentioned the problems I was having and was strongly considering returning the item, their response was..."We definitely recommend the MEATER+ for use with grills and smokers. The ambient reads from a small area and factors in the cold air coming off the meat and uses that to calculate cook time. It's reading the overall appliance temp, just from a small area. But we understand our products aren't for everyone so thanks for giving it a try. - Haley" Yep, I can tell you appreciate my business with that stellar effort. Will never buy another product from this company again and will recommend that no one does.

review_title: Hot garbage, threw it in the trash and got an RFX instead
review_text: Friend had a Meater, thought it was neat, borrowed it. Constant drop out issues. Got a Meater+ for myself, drop outs improved but were still a major problem. This thing eats batteries, and doesn't last long enough for a single long smoke, despite it's diameter being quite large. Eventually it just stopped working after using it a few dozen times, the base station wouldn't connect to it anymore at all. Replaced it with a 4 probe RFX set from Thermaworks. Actually designed to work with a thick wall smoker, no drop-outs now, and the base station connects to WiFi. Threw my Meater+ in the e-waste bin at my local recycling center and never looked back. Have seen some horrible reports from others about their Meater being 25 degrees or more off from what it should read as well, verified by tossing it in a pot of lightly boiling water. Should read 212f but i've seen various readings from 185f to 250f swinging in either direction. Not worth the risk IMO, and the app feature that tells you when to pull your steak is garbage as well. I cooked many a medium well steak using that thing's guidance for when to pull for medium rare, carry over cooking is real and apparently this thing just doens't know how to account for it at all.

If i could give this a 0 i would. Right out of the box, and a full 24 hours of charging and the probe will not pair, I called tech support and they were unsuccessful getting to pair. They sent me another probe, and of course that one didn't pair up either. Two probe thermometers unable to pair. Stay far away from this product. Why can't companies make a quality wireless meat thermometer. So disappointed!

I had this product for about a year. I used it less than 10 times and each time, it worked really well. However, after about 14 months, it stopped charging and I was unable to use it. I contacted customer support who after several back and forths, asked me to send them photos of the charger and the unit itself. I sent them several pictures, close ups, different angles. There was no damage to the casing, the charger or the device. The asked me to try several different trouble shooting maneuvers, which I did to no avail. They then asked me for my receipt so they could send me a replacement charger which I did. I then received an email informing me that because my device was over a year old, they would not replace the charger. I explained that I had only used it a handful of times and asked if they could make an exception and they responded by saying no. I explained again that I felt ripped off and it would go a long way if they would simply replace the charger so I could see if this was the issue ( I was not asking for a new device). They responded with an unfortunate NO again. I felt like I was in an episode of White Lotus battling the ego of Armond. It was like a line was drawn in the sand and that was it. No escalation to a supervisor, No empathy, no coloring outside the lines of policy, and no happy customer. Anyway, when the product works its great. Customer service was not what I look for. The durability of the product no good. Will not rebuy or recommend.

My husband is a computer engineer so he knows how to make things work. This Meater has never worked like it should've. If you dont use it everyday, then you have to start all over with charging it for a min of 2 hrs, then bluetoothing along with setting it up for the cook. We could never have an impromptu grilling bc this thing had to be charged first, then set up and it never was easy bluetoothing it to the app on my Samsung android Ultra 24 phone. We never knew how long it held a charge bc everytime we went to use it, it had no charge. Its never been EZ. Its one frustrating effort after another. We finally stopped trying to use it. It was on sale for $70 which is not a good deal if the themometer isnt user friendly. Maybe by now the Company has a better one out but I wont ever waste my time like we have done, trying to use this smart (lol) themometer. Alls not lost, tho. It makes a nice expensive magnate for our frig.

I love this product, but only when it works! I've had it for probably 2 years, maybe more, and want to use it at every Christmas, Thanksgiving, and a few other occasions. However, the majority of those times in the last 2 years when I pull out the probe and am ready to BBQ I can't get the stupid thing to connect! This is beyond frustrating when I'm ready to go and then I spend a fruitless hour trying to make the probe work and then just proceed without it. I can always get the dock to connect to my phone but not the probe to the dock. Ive spent many hours troubleshooting and with customer service and they weren't able to fix it. They sent me a new probe which worked the very first time I used it and then lo and behold today I want to use it and can't! Also of note, the customer service is 100% email based and you can never EVER talk to anyone on the phone, which is also frustrating. And if you don't respond to an email within 5 days they will close your ticket and have to reopen it. Ridiculous hassle just to try and get some help with their product. Also, I should note, I am not a Luddite, I am quite tech savvy and have tried all the help tutorials and everything they told me to do online. This is not user error. Maybe my dock is the problem, idk? So the product gets a 1 star unfortunately since it is so unreliable. Really sad because when it works it's great!

review_title: If I Could Give It Negative Stars, I Would! Worst Meat Thermometer of All Time!
review_text: Complete waste of $99! First, the probe itself needs to be charged, and it never holds a charge long enough for a cook. It constantly disconnects during a cook, and you have to move everything - my phone, and the charger box - ridiculously close to the grill where the probe is being used. And it STILL disconnects. Another really annoying point is the probe is like a giant, 4" nail, and it has to be buried into the meat, but for the very top / last 1/4", or so, of the probe. So, unless you are doing some massive roast or something, good luck getting the probe properly placed in your meat! I was doing 1" thick pork steaks today, and had a heck of a time getting the probe properly inserted, as it is so large! And of course, it disconnected while using it, meaning it was a waste of time even inserting it in the meat! I wound-up reverting back to my trusted ThermoPro wireless, which ALWAYS works well. The probes on the ThermaPro are thin, and easily insert into the meat (there are two of them, and they are connected by thin wires to the base transmitter unit. The base unit remains outside and talks to the unit I have in the house!). The ThermaPro wireless unit works flawlessly, and has never failed me. I won't be attempting to use the Meater again - it's complete junk, and a waste of money. You want something that works? Get a ThermaPro wireless meat thermometer. And the ThermaPro wireless digital thermometers are at least $40 - $60 cheaper than the Meater! Follow-up on 12/19: I threw the Meater in the trash, where it belongs! Meater was the only bad Amazon purchase I have ever made! Worst product of all time!

review_title: Expensive piece of useless gadget. Worst customer service.
review_text: Ordered in July of this year. I had it in my kitchen drawer until my first use in September. It kept losing connection, despite me being only a few feet away. This meter is supposed to have a range of up to 1000 ft, which is why I don’t understand how it loses connection within 30 feet. I had all done what customer support instructed me to do. They seem to never run out of excuses and “possible” scenarios of why the connection issues. None of the possible reasons applied. I had forgotten to respond to one of their many follow-up troubleshoot. At that point, there was a lot of back-and-forth useless and redundant communication. I am a very busy person so many times, emails fall through. In fact, I had forgotten all about the issue until it was time to use it yesterday on Thanksgiving dinner. I was using it for my standing rib roast and another time for my Cornish game hens, which were both roasted in the oven. It kept losing connection, especially when it came to the hens. I almost overcooked them because of constant lost connection. By the time I had reconnected, the app was flashing red to remove the meat from the heat. I got back to my communication with customer support but they communicated that my request had been resolved due to not getting back with them within 48 hrs of their last communication. DO NOT BUY THIS ITEM OR ANYTHING FROM THIS BRAND! Their customer service will give you the run around and frustrate you beyond measure only to leave you high and dry. I have an expensive piece of you-know-what now.

Purchased a second MEATER+ about 10 months ago. I love the product and how it works, however……. My experience in warranty support was spending about 90 minutes on the phone with a tech who seemed to be trying every way he could to blame the issue I was having on various “issues”. My probe quit working and would be “dead” every time I got it out to use. I replaced the battery each time and again pulled out a dead probe. Support had me send multiple pictures of my probe, the base, etc. Finally after telling me that my probe had a excessive build up (didn’t), my base battery compartment was dirty (wasn’t) etc, the last picture that he had me send, in the picture you could see that the black end of the probe was “cracked.” The tech was able to look at my account and verify that it had never been exposed to excessive heat temps. Bottom line, after finding the crack, advised me that “cracks” are not covered with warranty…….. I expressed my amazement because I cannot think of anything that would crack the probe other than temperatures, and if the probe was never exposed to excessive temps, then it should be defective. Tech finally offered to sell me a replacement for 10% off….. I passed on the offer. There are now many wireless probes not he market and many of them have great ratings. I will try other brands.

I was really excited to get this thermometer. I cook a LOT and I use a very accurate and very inexpensive instant read thermometer, but I figured the Meater would save me the hassle of pulling food out of the oven to check on it and MOST importantly it is so sad when you insert an instant read thermometer (no matter how slim) only to withdraw it and now you have a stream of juice running out of your meat! This product seemed perfect for me. Upon receipt I thought the packaging was great and really appreciated the minimalistic design. While the unit was charging up I installed the app, set a ??password?? For my ??cloud account?? and I’m like wtf I’m just cooking some meat! I did watch several videos to familiarize myself with how to use the probe. So, a few hours later I was excited for my first cook. Wah wah,,,I started with some really fat chicken breasts, inserted the probe into the middle of the biggest one, gave them a quick sear, then into a 350° oven. That’s when the fun started. Within a few minutes the app was reading 185° - way overdone. But just by pressing with my index finger I could tell the chicken was medium rare at best, so I pulled out my instant read and got 130°. Yanked the Meater and set it aside for another day. I really wanted this to work, but chicken on the grill was a fail as well - the probe was inaccurate again and the range was barely 30’. I’m returning this item and buying a traditional corded unit for my oven, I’ll keep my little instant read for grilling.

just got the Meater + read all the reviews Arrived quickly Used it on a brisket in a smokey mountain smoker App loaded quickly and set for Brisket Smoking Connected quickly to to the Meater put the meat in the smoker and then it all fell apart the base charging unit does not go 10 feet I had to have it within 1 foot of the smoker to get any kind of reading Connected to the application and gave me an accurate reading on external temp and meat temp verified with the smoker temp gauge walked 10 feet away lost signal and I got the 165 foot model! Will not give an accurate reading for how long it takes to cook told me 2 hours for a brisket! then kept adjusting and could not give me any indication of time I let the smoker work overnight and left my phone with the app no further then 10 feet away as I could not move it. woke up in the AM the application lost all connect and stopped the cook! I love the concept but the execution of the entire system is not ready for prime time Don't waste your money until they come out a new model that can do what it claims. I will be returning this expensive paper weight.

I initially enjoyed two excellent smoked pork shoulders with the Meater plus, but sadly, this device is no longer measuring the temperature accurately after my last two cooks. In my last cook (picture attached), it was 15 degrees below the temperature of my standard Traeger probe. In addition, when I tested which probe was more accurate with my meat thermometer, the Meater plus was still off by around 15 degrees. I tried calling customer service after my first poor cook, and they had me try an ice bath test. It passed the ice bath test that time. Thus, they told me to do another cook and to contact them again if I still have problems. When I did my next cook (today), the temperature gap still persisted. They had me do an ice bath test again, which it passed. Thus, in their minds, my probe is working fine. This is extremely frustrating. It is one thing to pass an ice bath test, and it is another thing to work in a real cook. Thus, according to their procedures, there is nothing I can do in this situation to prove that this product is defective, and I am stuck with a useless $100 probe. I am frustrated that I have a poor product which is useless to me, but more so frustrated by a company unwilling to stand behind their products and make the situation right.

I dont often leave a bad review, because by and large there are factors that go into all negative products consumption. I will start by saying this is a super cool tool for the smoker or kitchen, SO LONG as you never have an issue with it and have to deal with customer service. I have a Meater Plus that I use multiple times a week... and about a month ago it started having connectivity issues with the docking station. No charge, no light, no nothing... Got in touch with Meater to try and resolve the issue, walked through all the trouble shooting stages muiltiple times (there customer service must be in India or something, because you wont get a response for 24-48 hours and it will be at night or early morning). Finally got them to agree after about 2 weeks of going back and forth to replace the dock. Product is under warranty and i still have the original box and recipt... They sent the docking station about a week ago and was supposed to arrive today. Open the package which seemed way to small and what was it? Probe clips... the recipt and tacking number reflect a docking station and the i got probe clips which is going to be super helpful for my inoperable Meater Plus... Customer service is pathetic. When you spend nearly $100 on a thermometer, you generally expect a solid product, and at least decent customer service. This has been pathetic, highly disappointed, will certinlay recommend other products to friends and family.

I have had a Meater Plus for a few years, and it is good when it works. However, on several ocassions after I had finished preparing my food for cooking the device failed to make the connection to my iphone. Needless to say this is extremely frustrating so I cannot recommend this device.

I have bought two thinking one wss a flaw, at the end of the day both probes struggle to connect to the base for a reading. Even when sitting 6 inches apart on my kitchen counter. Would not reccomend or purchase again.

review_title: Not practical for BBQ - too delicate with temps
review_text: I wanted to use this for bbq grilling so bought it for $50 on Prime Day. Regretted the purchase from the first use and haven’t used it since. The first (only) time I used it was on a thick ribeye on a bbq. The problem occurred when I closed the bbq lid after searing (for indirect cooking). Within seconds I got an overheat alert. I opened the lid and removed the device and just finished it using a standard external temp probe, which worked fine and the steak was great. The manual says the device maxes out at 500F and is no longer warranties if overheated. But I assumed it is made for bbq, so why such a low max? BBQs get very hot, well over 500F when fired up and the lid is closed - much harder to control temps than in an indoor oven (where I don’t need this). BBQ is where I really needed this. Now, apparently the accuracy has likely been compromised from the high heat warning (according to the manual). So, for me this device is completely useless and I wasted my money.

Unless I’m standing right beside it, I can’t connect to it. So it’s pretty much useless if I can’t walk away. I have to reconnect every time through the app. It just doesn’t stay connected. Half the time he can’t find my probe. Save your money.

Have owned this since Sept 2021. Frequent, “semi-pro” griller. World famous, actually. Meater device is really awesome. When it works. Which is rare. First use, flawless. Actually made me look pro. Second time, oops, must update firmware. Problem, I’m camping 30 minutes from a cell signal. No option to disregard update prompt. This MUST be done to continue (really? Worked fine a couple weeks ago). Drive away. Update (20 minute download). Return to camp. Wants another update. Give up. Useless waste of 90 minutes. Third try, back at home, fine. Fourth try, device not charged (huh? The AA battery is like 2 months old and only 4 charges). Replace battery. Re-charge. Next say, works fine. Next try, no charge (new batteries!). Scrub a minute amount of smoke accumulation on the tip. Recharge 48 hours. Works again. Today, nope. Can’t pair it. Delete it. Re-pairs fine. Connected. Put on grill. Walk away. Can’t see device. Re-pair. Sees it. Nope. Connects but doesn’t see it. Fiddle around another 20 minutes of deleting- re-pairing, sees, doesnt see. Give up again. Not giving this tool any more batteries. Heading to garbage if it doesnt work again. Waste of time and $. The software developers should be canned. Too many infinite loops, firmware updates that cannot be deferred, simple but clunky and unintuitive navigation (connect and disconnect devices > there is no forget or disconnect button, come on). Says 165 ft range but when your meat is inside a stainless steel grill the range is about 24”. On and on. Save yourself some time and disappointment and wait for a copycat product with superior engineering.

I used my thermometer once and it was great. I went to use it a second time, and thought the battery was dead, so I changed it. No luck. It is out of warranty, but I still tried Amazon to see if they would help. They contacted the company, but no response. I rarely use a meat thermometer other than holidays, so I had no idea it would only last for one use. I'm disappointed the company did not respond.

review_title: I didn't have a good experience with this device.
review_text: This device will not pair with my iPhone. I've been charging it for more than an hour, my phone detects the Meater+, but it keeps telling me to 'charge the device for at least 2 hours.' Tech support was non-existent, and I figure that trying this same procedure over and over again isn't worth it. No offer to replace the device or alternative paths to pairing... I've gone back to using my wired meat therm...just don't bother with this thing.

I've been making my Thanksgiving turkey for the past 14 years, and I'm very consistent. I have my recipe and roasting times down to a science. I thought that it might be time to change out my old probe thermometer for this wireless one with the great reviews. Thanksgiving arrived and not wanting to chance anything, I used both thermometers. At first, they were reading similar. But, as the cooking progressed, the Meater+ was reading almost at the target temp at only 45 minutes in the oven, whereas, my old probe was no where near - still reading under 100 degrees internal. The Meater+ was hours early, and was screaming for me to remove the turkey from the heat after only 1 hour 15 minutes, while my old probe was still reading not quite ready. I thankfully, went with the my old probe and waited until it alarmed at my target temp. Perhaps I didn't have the Meater+ probe in far enough? I didn't go past the line as per the instructions. Does it need calibration? I don't know. I'm just glad I used my old aging thermometer as well... or this would have been my first Thanksgiving in 15 years with a trip to the hospital for everyone, not that I would have served it that raw, but I can only imagine if folks using the Meater+ for the first time, never having used any thermometers before and it gave the readings I got sooner than it was actually ready. I'll need to experiment more. Until then... not a good first outing with the Meater+.

review_title: Disappointed – Could Never Get It to Work
review_text: I purchased the Meater Plus as a Father's Day gift, and unfortunately it has been nothing but frustrating. We have spent the last week trying to get it to connect and stay connected with three different devices. We followed all of the recommended troubleshooting steps, including fully charging it, resetting it, replacing the battery in the charger, and testing it at different distances, but nothing worked. At this point, we still have a probe that won't reliably connect, making it completely unusable. I had high hopes based on the reviews, but our experience has been very disappointing. As it stands, this Father's Day gift has been a dud!

Would give 0 stars if I could. I've had my MEATER + for a little over a year and the item was always well taken care of. I'm not a guy who smokes/grills a ton and therefore the MEATER has seen limited use. With that being said, the thing just DIED! Will not charge, will not respond, nothing. I changed the battery numerous times with no luck. Contact MEATER support to find out the only option they will give me is a small discount on a new unit.....seriously?! I'm not sure what sales were running for Black Friday but I would assume I'm getting no special treatment than someone who hasn't even bought into their products. I've bought one for my dad and was even looking to buying a dual probe unit for myself in the near future. The warranty is pathetic and exactly why there's no brand loyalty with customers anymore. This is a blatant manufacturing defect that the company won't even back up their own product. You've lost a customer. BUYER BEWARE! SAVE YOUR MONEY AND BUY A DIFFERENT PROBE!

review_title: One Star is Too Generous – Total Waste of Money
review_text: I recently purchased the Meater Pro Plus wireless thermometer for around $80 (shipping included), and honestly, I would’ve been better off taking four $20 bills and wiping my *** with them. That would’ve at least saved me the headache. The Meater Pro Plus advertises a 165 ft range, but in reality? It only works if you’re standing right next to the grill. First time using it, I lost connection just 10 feet away. Thought maybe it was a fluke, so I gave it another try. This time, it wouldn’t connect at all—no matter what I did. I followed every step in the manual, watched tutorial videos, and still nothing. I’m no rookie when it comes to meat thermometers. I’ve used plenty before and never had issues like this. If you want a reliable, tried-and-true thermometer, go with a ThermoPro. Sure, the model I have doesn’t display ambient temperature, but at least it actually connects—and stays connected. I can sit inside my home and monitor the cook without constantly babysitting the device. The Meater Pro Plus promises all this fancy wireless accessibility, but it simply doesn’t deliver. I’ll never buy another product from this brand again. Ever. Absolute trash. Thanks for nothing. Hallelujah and pass the Tylenol.

Cool product if it works. Mine came in defective. Contacted customer service and the send me Pro probe that doesn’t work with the Plus box. Only to get sent a Plus probe that also doesn’t connect with the box because not the box and probe were defective. I wish all the best talking to incompetent customer service.

I have had this for just over a year. I had to have the probe replaced as it stopped working. Having issues again. They are able to track everything you do via the app (what you are cooking, the temp of your device (oven or ?). It most definitely read a high temp in error and now they won’t honor the warranty. I will have to find another brand.

review_title: Metaer used to be a fine product and now is unreliable. Do not buy
review_text: This product has become unreliable. I have had bought three of at least for myself and bought two engraved for gifts for close friends. I used to think this was a terrific product however in the past two weeks two models won a replacement and one that I purchased in March have failed. I think that the product which used to be terrific and it's a fine design and a good app it's getting cheaper and they don't care. They pretend to care but I purchase one it failed I asked for a replacement which they sent me and that replacement failed to pair or to connect. They've refused to replace it a third time. Again this used to be a good product and now it is unreliable do not buy purchase some other brand
I definitely would not recommend the meater thermometer. I have owned it for a few years now, and it has been 50/50 on the bluetooth connection. Not worth the hassle.

review_title: I used it once and… here let Monty Python explain.
review_text: Customer: ’Scuse me, I wish to make a complaint! Shopkeeper: We’re closing for lunch. Customer: Never mind your lunch, my lad. I’ve got a dead probe on my hands. Shopkeeper: No, no, no… it’s not dead. It’s uh… thinking. Deeply. Probably communing with the roast. Customer: LOOK, MATE. I know a dead probe when I see one, and I’m looking at one right now. This MEATER Plus has passed on! Shopkeeper: It’s stunned. Customer: STUNNED?? I tapped it on the counter! I reseated it! I polished its charging rings! I reset the cradle! If it was stunned, it’d be broadcasting temperatures by now! This probe is no longer among the connectable! It has ceased to be! It’s expired and gone to meet its manufacturer! This is a late probe! It is a probe that will probe no more! It has shuffled off its mortal Bluetooth, run down its internal battery, and joined the choir invisible of defective kitchen gadgets! THIS… IS… AN EX-PROBE!

Works fine, until it doesn't. The first 5 or 6 times I was able to perfectly cook chicken or steak in my air fryer. But now, tonight, it will not connect to my phone app via bluetooth... It's a freakin meat thermometer and I am hungry! But now I have to google search for possible remedies!!! Did I mention I was hungry, well yea, just make that 'HANGRY' ! UPDATE: I got it to connect a few times after my last review, but tonight, no deal. So I ground it up in my garbage disposal. Seriously now, I'm supposed to contact tech support with my issues as I'm preparing dinner? Sorry, no go. I'm cooking a chicken breast in the air fryer but now it is most likely burning up in my air fryer, as I have diverted my attention to researching debug and consequently, publishing this gripe. DO NOT BUY!!!

I wanted to like the Meater and it comes in a slick design with a nice case. I wanted something wireless rather than use the wired thermostats I already have, but that was a mistake. This thing just does not work in some grills. I have a PitBoss and the moment you close the lid you lose connection to the Meater. I’ve put the magnetic case practically as close as possible without wondering if it’d catch fire and it still doesn’t stay connected. Lid open? No issues. Lid closed? No connection. I went to Reddit and saw that I’m very much not alone in this issue. Now I have a useless probe laying around. If it does work in your grill or oven, the app experience is decent. I had to silence the app notifications though, which kind of defeats the whole point, because even with no cook going on and the Meater disconnected the app will whine whenever I turn off Bluetooth because it’s worried I might need to use my Meater still. It’s a slick product, but if they didn’t discover the connection issues in testing (with one of the most common smokers) I don’t know what else they probably missed. It’s definitely not worth the cost.

Worked great for about one year then....stopped working. Pulling it out of roast at about month 9 it started to come apart (see image). Still kinda worked for the next 3 months but stopped recharging so now dead.

I purchased a Meater Plus last year and after using it the first time, the temperature of the meat and ambient temperature were way off compared to other probes I used to check if the Meater Plus was working correctly. Because of a huge difference in temperature, I returned that thermometer. The new one I bought has the exact same issue. Having placed a thermometer probe directly next to the Meater Plus, the Meater Plus read 12-15 degrees higher. To check, I used my $100+ instant read thermometer and the Meater Plus was confirmed to be 12 degrees higher. Also, the Meater Plus measured the ambient temperature to be 80-85 degrees lower than my oven and additional ambient probe I used. Way too many issues to want to use this thermometer ever again. Extremely disappointed in this product and can’t believe all of the positive reviews. If you don’t double check with other thermometers/probes, you may think the Meater Plus is working just fine. Huge mistake. The warranty makes you pay shipping back and forth so very annoying. A business should stand behind their product during the warranty period and should handle the costs of shipping and return shipping if there is truly an issue with their product.
Terrible, spent forever trying over and over to connect to phone and it wouldn't. Not much online support, tried everything stated and wouldn't work. Returned
It's great when it works. I bought a second one because it didn't connect to my phone and the second one did the same thing after a few uses. Not worth the money.
Dead after 2 years. Won’t charge.
Lasted 5 months and stopped working. On phone with support for about a half hour and then they disconnected me.
Not good. Doesn’t connect to WiFi. This should be a problem in 2026. No customer support. Do not buy.
Rarely works!

Avoid! I purchased 21 months ago. Consistently off temperature by several degrees. The prediction timing is very poor and takes very long into the cook. Product can’t even be used for any medium to high heat cooks so extremely limited utility. My probe stopped connecting to Bluetooth after less than a year. I got a replacement from meager but tonight that failed to connect to Bluetooth as well making the product not function. Two broken products is unacceptable, especially at this price point. Stay away. Im a bbq cook and judge and this is consistently let me down. Troubleshooting is frustrating. Told to charge clean charge clean charge clean… the probe just don’t work
Most overpriced piece of **** on the market. Save yourself a huge headache and go with the Tempspike Plus.
Would not bind to my phone. Beware!
I have had two meager temp. gauges and they both guide working after about six uses each. I believe these are rip off and I suggest DO NOT BUY!!!!

review_title: Don't go... 2 yrs and the battery won't hold a charge... run around from support... no real support.
review_text: About two years into the Meater journey, the probe won't hold a charge past 15 min. The help desk isn't helpful. I offered to pay for another probe, they made noises about a link to purchase that never showed. A reasonable company would've send a new probe. An ok company would've let me purchase a new one. Neither happened. There are too many competitors to live with drama. Off to try ThermoMaven (Gemini recommendation). Bottom line for Meater: Inferior range and technology, horrible customer support, only thing they seem to do well is work the run around and ghosting.
Totally unreliable!! I have the MEATER and the MEATER +. Every time I use it, it loses connection- NO MATTER HOW CLOSE I AM TO THE MEATER PROBE ON MY PHONE. I can’t trust it.
Absolute garbage, used about 3 times and the charger stopped working and giving a charge. Don’t waste your time, not worth paying premium price for junk.

review_title: Range too short and temperature wrong
review_text: I have given up on my Meater Plus. It cannot keep a connection between the thermometer and my phone, and the reported temperature was 20° higher than the actual temperature
It’s great when it actually works. . .which is rarely. Constantly loses connection in the middle of cooks. Nearly impossible to make it all the way through without some kind of technical problem.

Has anyone else heard the new ‘Overheating’ notification? ‘Cause apparently Meater is now hiring 6 yr old programmers. I’d switch to the competition, but after one visit to their website, I’m now gonna get spammed for all eternity
Worked great but only used a handful of times and then completely stopped working after about 1.5 years, outside of its 1 year warranty.
I don’t use the thermometer often but connectivity with my phone and iPad is spotty and it now won’t connect at all. This is after only 3 1/2 years. 1 star for lack of reliability.
Its not good. It has disconnected on 100% of my grills. I have a charcoal weber, i do not use it over coals or direct hear. The signal has to go maybe 6-12 feet through cheap trailer walls
Not happy with the item. I’ve used it a few times and only once can I say the meat cooked as expected

The every 6th use where it actually works and finds the probe, it works well. More often than not I just grab my wired probe that has Bluetooth that I have never once had an issue with it finding it. I really wanted to like this more and use it more but it is so unreliable that I almost always just leave it in the drawer.

review_title: Company does not replace their faulty products
review_text: I love my Meater; however, this is the second charging case to fail. The first one to fail, they only charged me a nominal price to replace it. This time they wanted to charge me full price to replace the 2nd one. These are battery-operated and should never go bad unless you break them. I am going to try another brand. I don't like that the company's customer service policy has become overly restrictive.
Does not work with grill cover closed!
Doesn't connect to app. At least for me. The thermometer is thick/wide. Find something else.

Piece of garbage, do not buy!! I regularly experience connectivity issues and this product simple does not read correctly, set your steak to 130 for medium rare and it will prompt you at 140 degrees. Don’t waste your time. Waste of money
Doesn’t work right. Can’t connect. Very disappointed

I got this as a gift and every time I brought it out to cook it didn’t work. I troubleshot it, cleaned it, replaced the battery multiple times. When I finally got tired of trying to fix it, I contacted support but they just wanted me to buy a new probe. It’s crazy to have a premium thermometer company not support their product.

review_title: Connection lost constantly. Waste of money.
review_text: Piece of junk. Constantly losing connection even when moving the box closer to the thermometer. Then the app changes the cooking time to say it’s going to be some astronomical amount of time even though all the data from the cooking up to that point is in the app. Issue happened multiple times. Returning. Save your $60 and get something else.

It worked 1st couple times. Now it always needs to be charged ... reloaded software ... reconnect probe .... bluetooth etc etc . Not worth it get 2 battery, wire tethethered probes . More reliable than having to do backflips everytime you want to use an over priced thermometer

Temps are no where near accurate. Five minutes into cooking an inch and a half thick New York strip steak it tells me to pull it off the grill as it’s 135 degrees.
