review_title: Not worth the 100$ if you are going to be using an oven, works fine with a grill tho.
review_text: I bought this to replace a meter that stopped connecting to my phone. When it arrived, I tested it on a steak on the grill and it worked fine. I figured I had nothing to worry about. Fast forward to today. I am making meatloaf and have the meter magnetically attached to the outside of the oven door. I remove the probe and open the app. No connection. I close and reopen the app. Still no connection. I check the battery. Green light. I check the charger. Blinking red light. What does that mean? I check the app, and it says the meter is not connected to the charger. I put the meter back on the charger, count to ten, and remove it. Now a message pops up telling me to bring the charger closer to my phone. The diagram shows the meter and charger are connected, but there is a red X between my phone and the charger. I am literally standing one foot away. I slide my phone closer, and now it connects. Small victory. I slide the probe into the meatloaf dish, lining it up properly. BEEP. My phone says the meter is disconnected and to move the phone closer. I move it closer, and it reconnects. Alright, the meter shows the temps. Great. I put the pan in the oven, close the door, and walk three feet to my fridge. BEEP. The meter has no connection with the charger. Are you kidding me? It is right next to it. I open the oven, pull the pan out, and set the charger on top. After a full minute, it finally reconnects. I try again, and I do not even get the loaf in the oven before BEEP, probe lost connection to the charger. Fine, I see there is a setting to use the meter without the charging block. I go through the process to link the meter directly to my phone. It connects. Another small victory. Then I get a warning: “This probe has a low battery, are you sure you want to use it?” Seriously? It is brand new. I have used it once, a month and a half ago. I check the device information. Full battery. I say screw it and use it anyway. It is currently in the oven, and I am here venting my frustration and checking to see if I can return it. A 100 dollar wireless thermometer should not be this much of a hassle, especially since my last one worked fine with a 300-foot range. Sadly, the return window closed July 27. I will be reaching out to support to see if they can make an exception.

I've been a manual quick read probe fan for a long long time in my BBQ, Grill and stove top cooking. Then I switched to a 4 probe corded product from Weber. That one was also Bluetooth so I knew what to expect for signal range. Well the Meater added a few new things to my making of the meat duties. I lost the wires. I also lost out on using more than one probe. I didn't want to spring for the multiple probe kit so it's just a single for me, at least for now. I really like the built in ambient temp sensor on the top of the probe. Before I used a grill grate mounted probe and quite often I'd melt the thing after about a year of roaring hot coals in my 22" kettle. I guess a 500 degree probe can't handle the direct 800+ heat from a good charcoal. No big deal replacements are cheap and at the local hardware store. With the Meater that sensor is a lot further away from the coals so I don't see temps like that and with the majority of the probe in the meat there is a built in heat sink of sorts. So it should survive better. I love the app and the estimate seems to be very close to accurate. Only thing I need to learn and teach my spouse is to not pull the probe until it is in the house and rested per the app. Then you can save your cook. What I seriously dislike is the "long range" feature. There is none. The range is crap. Doesn't matter if it's in my 22" weber kettle with the lid on or not. Or in my gas grill with the lid closed or not. I have constant "out of range move the "box" closer to the remote" error. This is with the holder box a foot away from the probe. I don't mind leaving it out on the table next to my grills but to have range issues at mere single digit feet distances is really not what I call long range. Or if that long range is how far I can take my phone, iPhone 12 Pro Max, away from the cooking area well that is not really what I'd call long range either. It's less than half that of the Weber product I am attempting to replace. This isn't an interference with my surroundings as my watch, Series 8 iWatch, works fine in my house even at 70 feet from my phone. I just want to be able to work on food in my kitchen while the probe is doing it's thing and even that 20 feet line of sight is too far. But then again so was sitting at the other end patio table 8 feet away from the bbq. I figure outside has to be better than inside but that doesn't seem to be the case. Should I have purchased the wifi Meater product? Maybe. I do know I won't be buying another one of this model. I'd return it and upgrade to the more than doubly expensive other model but I'm not sure I can trust that it would be money well spent.

I have used the meater + a few times now and I feel like I can write my review. Goods: it’s very compact and feels high quality. The thermometer its self is durable and can withstand hand washing. Bad: it always discontents all the time over and over again. It is terrible with keeping the signal. I’ll have the base right on the smoker close enough that it’ll read and it’ll still disconnect. And when I wrap the meat it’ll disconnect. And when I place the meat in the oven it’ll disconnect. When you go to calibrate it will not read the meater. Is honestly very frustrating to the point I’ll use my corded monitors and put a baby camera in front of it. And it’s battery operated. So make sure you take the battery out when you don’t use it cause it dies so fast. Summery: concept is awesome. The product itself is not. Purchase at your own risk. Next time I’ll purchase a more expensive one that’ll actually work.

review_title: You Will Grow To Hate It
review_text: Be sure to look at my photos to clearly understand the problems with this product. I am done with this device. Problem #1 I own two and both have difficultly staying connected to the app. Problem #2 There's nothing to indicate when the battery is dying, so it can inconveniently die in the middle of the cook. Problem #3 It takes too long of a time for all the connections to load and randomly looses the connection. This is problematic on shorter cooks where something small such as a steak can overcook quickly. Then all you can do is patiently wait several minutes hoping it reconnects. If it doesn't reconnect on its own, you have to pull the thermometer out of the food and place it in the base station, and then reset up the cook. Problem #4 The interactions with the support department take too long to respond, and when you do hear back they have lousy excuses why the device didn't work properly, all being user errors. Problem #5 both internal food temperature and the external air temperature are consistently way off. My meat is always over done. When I test the meater temp to my instant read thermometer, the instant read is spot on and the Meater way off. The cook I did tonight, had the thermometer Meater reading at 74 and not changing. The instant read 132 (see photos in my review) . The meat overcookes. The meat went into a 500° oven, after searing on the stove for 12 minutes in the same cast iron pan it seared in. This has now ruined too many cooks to count with both Meater thermometers. I loved the concept but that's it. This thermometer is way too much work. People who are giving this device a high rating more than likely haven't used it enough times to see all its shortcomings over time and if they do find shortcomings, they forget to follow-upon their reviews. The competition has better thermometers and are less expensive. Two years ago I bought my son-in-law a thermometer that Costco had, because I couldn't even consider gifting the Meater one to him after all the frustrations I've had with it. It came with two thermometers and is considerably more sophisticated than the Meater Plus for half the cost and everything about it is better than Meater Plus. So far no calls to support for any technical issues either.

review_title: Its pretty good but not mind blowing.
review_text: Im using the device for the first time today. Im smoking a pork shoulder. Unboxing was great, excellent packaging and I really like the wood repeater box. Although why does it use alkaline batteries rather than lith ion? Connecting was easy with the app. I prepped my smoker and it is running at 225 degrees and stable. I know this as I have 2 temp probes in the smoker and have been using it for years. I've inserted the meater into the pork shoulder being sure it is not contacting the bone and is past the tiny line on the meater. Initial reading from the meater before going in was as expected, 38 deg internal and no reading from external. I put the pork in the smoker. Let it sit for about 10 minutes and checked my readings. Internal 39 and external 189. Say what? My 2 smoker probes say oven temp is 226 and 228. Ok so the meat is still cold and the meater external probe is near the meat. I guess. 1.5 hours in. Smoker says it's at 232 neater external says 198. Seems my meater external probe is off by 20 or more degrees. That's not acceptable. Now I question the accuracy of the internal probe. I will be putting another probe that I trust right next to the meater and I will report back Now, the wireless part. In the 2 hours I've used this, it has said it is disconnected at least 5 times. My house is a single story, and is only 70 feet long by 30 feet wide. My smoker is on the back porch about 10 feet from the house. So by the numbers, I should never disconnect. But it does. Now, I'm cooking a large pork shoulder for pulled pork. Im using the meater app custom cook setting. It says at my current and inaccurate abmiant temp, it will cook to 203 in about 6 hours? How could it come up with that. In fact this meat will not hit 200 for almost 10 hours. It did not ask how much weight or what I was cooking, so the estimate is flawed from the beginning. I swear I wanted to love this device. But I mearly just like it. If this changes I will update my rating. At this time the meater external probe is at 202, it has never matched my smoker probe temp, the ambiant sensor is not accurate. I have put a probe for internal temp right next to the meater. Meater says 106 and my trusted probe says 108. Totally acceptable. Internal probe seems acurate. If something changes I will edit this review. So after a 15 hour cook, here is where I stand. Do not depend on the ambiant temp sensor to monitor your oven temp, it does not give accurate readings. Meater actually knows this and trys to explain it away on their website. I put a probe right next to the meater external sensor and it showed the correct temp, the meter never did. The internal sensor seems accurate. I have the meter plus, it does not extend anywhere near 165 feet, more like 35. For some reason you need two devices to get cloud data. Why cant the repeater box connect to the wifi? This device is good in concept, lacks in execution. I'm going to return the meater, it is not for me nor does it really do what it claims. It just barely does what it sets out to do. The one real cool thing it does, the app graphs your cook, kinda cool.

review_title: I regret getting this.  Getting a signal is a big hassle (get a wired thermometer)
review_text: I've cooked 2 things with the Meater+ so far, a 20lb turkey and a pot roast. I cooked the Turkey first. I put the probe in the turkey and put the turkey in the oven and then put the base on top of the oven about 2 feet away from the probe, but through the cooktop of the stove. Apparently there was too much metal or too much distance from the probe to the base and I couldn't get a reading. The problem is, the app doesn't really tell you that. It just shows the last reading it could get when I put it in the oven. So for about half an hour, the readings didn't change and the user has no idea what is going on. For all I knew, it was working fine. When I finally realized that the temperatures weren't changing and should be by now, I thought I just had a bad unit (there were a lot of other reviews with faulty units). Finally figured out (no thanks to the App) that the base wasn't really reading the probe, so I move the base to the front of the oven door and finally got my readings. Not a huge deal but very annoying that the app doesn't even tell you that it can't sense the probe. I even went into the connection page and it looked like I was connected all the way from my phone, through the base, to the probe. Pretty ridiculous in my opinion. A loss of signal is a super easy thing to program. The second attempt at using the Meater+ was for a pot roast. Well, apparently you can't get a signal when the pot roast is in the pot either, so it was strike 2. Again the app didn't tell me this, it just stayed at the temperature of the last signal it got before I put the roast in the pot so based on the last experience from the turkey, I knew the signal wasn't getting through (the pot is a metal pot so not a giant surprise). After this last defeat, I realized that I am going to be very limited with what I can use this for and am honestly regretting buying this. Between the signal issues and the temperature limitations (can't be put on the grill in direct heat), I am regretting not getting a wired thermometer that wouldn't have either of these limitations. I haven't tried to use this on my grill yet, but based on how poorly it is able to get through metal pots and my oven, at this point I doubt it could even get through the grill to the base when it is closed. I was so excited for this and it has been a huge let down. The worst part is how much I spent on this thing and that I won't really be able to use it.

Trash - the main problem with it is the battery that recharges the probe instead of some soft of USB rechargeable option. It worked pretty well until I had to change the battery, then it'd work 1 time out of 4. I threw it in the trash - $100 lesson.

review_title: MEATER Misses the Mark: A Griller's Frustration
review_text: If you're considering the MEATER wireless thermometer, be aware of some notable limitations that may affect your grilling experience.​ I used it once and immediately returned it. I was swayed by the high number of positive reviews, but I was not a fan. 🔌 Connectivity Challenges Many users report that the MEATER's Bluetooth range is quite limited, especially when used with grills or smokers. The signal often struggles to penetrate metal lids and walls, resulting in a maximum range of about 10 feet, sometimes even less. This means you often need to stay near the grill to maintain a connection. ​ To mitigate this, MEATER suggests using a second device as a Wi-Fi bridge via their MEATER Link feature. By placing a spare phone or tablet near the grill and connecting it to the same Wi-Fi network, you can monitor your cook remotely. While this workaround can be effective, it adds complexity to the setup. ​ ⚠️ High-Temperature Warnings Another concern is the MEATER's performance at high temperatures. Users have reported that when the ambient temperature exceeds the probe's limit (approximately 527°F), the device displays a red warning and stops showing the current temperature. This can be particularly frustrating during high-heat grilling sessions, as the thermometer doesn't resume normal operation even after temperatures drop. ​ 🧼 Maintenance Requirements Proper cleaning is crucial for the MEATER's functionality. Residue on the ambient tip can interfere with charging and connectivity. Regular cleaning with hot water and a sponge is recommended, and in some cases, low-grit sandpaper may be necessary to remove stubborn buildup. ​ ✅ Potential Alternatives If these issues are concerning, you might consider alternative wireless thermometers with better range and reliability. For instance, the ThermoPro TempSpike offers a 500-foot range and robust app features, while the Combustion Predictive Thermometer provides a 330-foot range and a multi-sensor probe. ​ In summary, while the MEATER offers a sleek, wireless design, its limited Bluetooth range, sensitivity to high temperatures, and maintenance requirements may pose challenges. Evaluating these factors against your grilling needs will help determine if it's the right tool for you

review_title: Tech is unfortunately not there yet - the concept is a great one for rotisserie though
review_text: I purchased this product after following the KickStarter they had for a while. When I realized it was finally available, I was excited to purchase it and try it out, even though I had seen plenty of low star reviews and mixed feelings in general around how the BlueTooth technology actually functioned. I purchased the Meater probe with the extender to allow for 165+ feet. The first night I got it, I read through the instructions, downloaded the app, and paired the extender/probe. I started it up and began to cook a chicken on my Weber charcoal grill conventionally (so not a rotisserie). Throughout the cook, the app kept indicating that the probe connection was lost and it would try and find it and reconnect and then the cooking time would be revised. The Meater block was super close to the grill on a little table (but not so much that it would be affected by the heat) and my phone was placed on the counter inside, so from phone to probe, it was probably 6 feet max. Anyway, it did cook the chicken though. I cleaned it off per the instructions and made sure the probe was charged for the following day. The next day, I went to cook a Turkey on the grill (Thanksgiving naturally, no stress associated with cooking the turkey). I didn't even chance the rotisserie as I thought that might complicate connectivity, so I just cooked it conventionally on the grill. To start, my app could not even find the Meater block, even though I had previously paired to it the night before without issue (this shouldn't be a phone issue, i have the latest iPhone with all the software updates). It took me a solid 30 minutes of trying to pair the thing, restarting my phone, restarting the app, trying to forget the block and pair it again, all with no success. Then I tried to pair just to the probe and avoid the "range extending" block. I was finally able to pair to it directly and cook the Turkey (although it was halfway done by the time I had the probe up and running). It kept losing connection throughout the cook as it did the previous night, which was annoying. So I cleaned it and returned it to Amazon first thing possible. Meater did process the return relatively quickly, so I can't fault them for customer service as some others have. My closing thoughts are: - This is an excellent, excellent concept and I really wish it would work because it would allow you to have a probe style thermometer for a rotisserie, something that doesn't really exist but should. - The app concept is also great, as I really like having the ability to time things based on reaching a certain temperature, and most probe thermometer apps don't offer expected time to completion, instead just tracking the temperature. I'm giving an extra star here because of how good a product the app alone would be if they could get things to execute. - Unfortunately, the execution is not there yet and they probably needed even more R&D time to get this right. I really wanted this product to work as described, but unfortunately I would suggest you look elsewhere.

review_title: Great in concept, horrible in execution.
review_text: The Meater+ is a $100 thermometer that is a bold idea and continuation of their original. Jumping right into the good (short points at the bottom). The app experience is great, it makes sure whether you're a novice or, experienced, you have all the information you need to get the probe set up and working. Tracking your cooks allowing you to give feedback are all great features. The probe itself seems fairly sturdy, and we'll put together along with the base. Running off a single battery it charges seemingly quickly and easily. The ability to clean in a dishwasher (I would still never do that that's asking for trouble), is nice. The app is also intuitive as far as letting you know to pull and test your cook (important if you're not used to doing that). Now. The bad. It's silly inaccurate. So inaccurate I wouldn't trust it on a big cook. Like the numerous briskets or pork butts I do. Normally I don't care if my temp probes give me temp data for inside my cook chamber because they have their own thermometer but for a $100 it shouldn't be off by 150°F +/-. Or never actually get fully up to sensing the temp. That's just not acceptable. The same for the temp in whatever you're cooking. Speaking of. In order to work properly, you're going to need to make sure it's a hefty piece of meat. The probe itself is thicc as the kids say. Like slightly bigger diameter than a No. 2 pencil. And the line for insertion is 2/3s up the probe. On a medium medium/large chicken breast it was still hard to get it surrounded by enough of the breast to feel confident in getting a reading that is accurate and true. Finally, connectivity. They boast a 165' range. Which is fascinating because it would drop connection for no reason with everything right next to each other. Just prepping for my cook. I wouldn't trust it the less than 35' from my back porch to my kitchen if it can't stay connected on my kitchen counter. So. Over a few cooks, as I always do with my thermometers, in just my regular oven. To get a feel for how they work, their accuracy etc. My experience was, not good. Again. Dropped connection both on the counter and in the oven. Never registered the oven at it's temp. Never even got close. When I pulled the cook and checked against my instant read that is highly accurate it was a difference of 10°+/-. That's just no good. I got the same results over 3 cooks before I finally declared the Meater+ a bust. It's a good idea. Just poorly executed. And not worth anywhere near a $100. The only thing I could see this being good at would be a rotisserie but that's a fairly niche application. So I sent it back and put the purchase price towards a ThermoWorks Signals instead. I usually follow the philosophy of buy once cry once. But this time I used it in the wrong direction as the Meater is definitely not ready for primetime. Pros: Great app experience Helpful step by step instructions if needed. Seemingly solid construction Cons: Super inaccurate Actual range is suspect Connectivity is spotty at best Large diameter

I have had this for almost a year, it worked rather well except for calculation of the done time, it will intermittently lose connection then it would take quite a while to recalculate. The ambient temperature being off a little makes the done time calculation off. The worst part is for the connection to be made to the probe on a Blackstone pellet smoker, the base must be magnetically stuck to the side, it is wood and a long way from water proof, it must be to close to put in a plastic bag and so after a rain during a smoke, my connection never works anymore, cuts in and out continuously. I don't recommend this unit for outdoor use

When they work there great , the connectivity is in and out you have to be within five to ten feet of the device or it cuts out. There’s so much potential, but I feel like the people who invented this never have grilled or cooked anything in their life.

review_title: New app is ?? ..... all of a sudden my phone can't connect (update)
review_text: I bought the Meaterr+ about a year and a half ago. To be honest, I never had much love for this thing. Definitely not as accurate as a simple meat thermometer and finicky from a connection perspective. So.... for a long time, it got no use. I even went to the point of removing the battery and a shelf the thermometer sat for almost a year. A week ago, I put in a fresh battery and started the charge. Made the mistake (?) of downloading the latest app for Android. That's when progress stopped. After 8 hours I started the very much not intuitive app (for me anyway). By now, the thermometer was no longer in my prior connected list of bluetooth devices. And it stayed that way. For life of me, I can't get the d@mn thing to connect. And the app, of course, will not let me out of setup since it can't connect. And, yes, I've visited the website numerous times and watched more YouTube videos than it takes to disassemble my car and put it back together. 12/23!2023 - Quick update….I’m starting to show much needed success. I took out the old battery and deleted the app and told myself to leave it all alone for a dozen hours. Jump ahead about 8 hours and I’m back. I did a data cleanup on my phone removing all evidence that the old/refreshed app was ever installed and then reinstalled it fresh from the google Play Store. By now, my fingers were crossed that the Meater was fully charged. Bingo, paired and connected. When I returned the next day and checked, the Meater and my phone played well together and connected. I played with the menu and felt reasonably confident that we could use it in a nice roast on Christmas. So, as of this writing, we’re connected and ready (?) to go. My next update tomorrow will address accuracy. Merry Christmas! p.s. I’ve raised my rating to two stars, so there’s hope.

review_title: Save Your Money and Buy a Good Instant-read Thermometer For ¼ of the Price
review_text: I have owned my MEATER Plus - Smart Digital Wireless Meat & Food Thermometer now through two seasons of outdoor and indoor cooking. I have used it over 30 times. This product is VERY well made. Sustainable bamboo is used for the box, everything including the probe fits snugly together and looks very cool. The App is very intuitive and with functions and features that are easy to use. Its temperature readings are always within 1 degree of my two, instant-read thermometers. This is where the “Pros” end. The main feature and selling point is your ability “to monitor your cook from virtually anywhere in your home.” Sorry, NOT SO. With my roast in the oven, I lose connection in my bedroom on our second floor. Moving to my basement office, no connection. (batteries fully charged). For my outside BBQ, when I close the lid, I lose connection when I get to my porch 50 feet away. With a roast in the oven and covered with foil in a roasting pan, no connection after closing the oven door and my phone five feet away. All I got from their support was, “you’ll have to move around your house to find where you can connect.” Save your money and buy a good instant-read thermometer for ¼ of the price.

Cannot recommend. The thermometer function works fine but I have three issues. 1. The case received is defective. The metal charging points are not in line correctly in order for the probe to touch all three and charge. I have to push the probe bottom over in order to get all three points to touch but eventually it moves back slightly so it is no longer touching and will no longer charge. 2. The charging box is kind of a Bluetooth enhancer and therefore needs to be near the probe while in use. Usually this would not be an issue, but I found that as little as 3 feet away is too far and will drop the connection. The box needs to be very close so it’s just a bit annoying especially if using in a wall oven with no where to really put the box. 3. Customer support. I contacted them about the metal sensor issue. They sent a generic message back to try some trouble shooting items I had already followed from their website. I replied that the troubleshooting did not work and I needed additional support or a new box. I have not heard back since that message. Finally, just for information but a negative impact necessarily, directions are ok, but there are some really specific items that don’t make sense, for example you need to pull the probe from the charger before opening the app in order for the connection to work properly. Also, I found that the connection kept dropping and reconnecting and couldn’t figure out why. But according to the troubleshooting, your probe will always try to connect to your phone instead of the charging box if your phone is near by because the connection is stronger. Just made me worry there was a connection issue so they should clarify in the instructions.

review_title: Poor Accuracy & Only For Thick Cuts Meat
review_text: Overall disappointing I wanted to like it but it’s inaccurate and can only be used on very thick cuts of meat. 1) Temp reading is inaccurate when I compared to my wired thermometer 2) can only be used on very thick cuts of meat the Meater support people tell me that you have to insert the thermometer 2 1/2 inches to be accurate so it’s no good for burgers, chicken thighs, pork chops. 3) I've had problems with charging even though I’ve kept it very clean, the Meater support people told me that the charger station is very sensitive to grease, grime, dirt, water.

review_title: Tired of buying a new one every year
review_text: WHEN IT WORKED it was great. I’ve been through three of them in three years. They like to suddenly drop signal in the middle of a Cook. I called Service, they tried to be helpful, but every time they told me to look for something in the drop-down menu on the app it didn’t exist. I’m over it now too bad I enjoyed it while it was working.

I've had this for about a year now and I do not like it. Lots of issues connecting to my phone. Probe dies fast. Not worth the price at all. Very disappointed since this brand was supposed to be the best. When it works, great. But most of the time it does not work.

The meater plus measures two temperatures, the inside of the meat, and the ambient temperature of your grill/oven. The meater plus accuracy hits the mark dead on when it comes to the internal temperature, but it was remarkably off when it came to the ambient. If you have a good thermostat on your grill, then you could work around this, but you want what you pay for and in my case it didn't deliver. The accuracy of the ambient temp was so far off I wasn't sure that I would be able to trust the internal temperature gauge. So in the end I did use a second trusted thermostat to verify the accuracy, and the meater plus internal sensor ended up being on the mark. The features of the app are nice and it's easy to setup. You set your desired temp ( or choose a preset) and it predicts the time it takes and sends an alert to your phone when it's ready, and even has a "resting" setting after you pull the meat off the grill. The only problem is that the estimate of when the meat is done is off due to the ambient temperature sensor not being accurate (+- 50°f the entire cook). The meater plus connects to your phone via bluetooth, and the setup is simple and easy. When in use the thermometer must be in a 10ft range of its box, which then transmits to your phone, up to 130 ft, so that's nice. The only problem I could see with this particular setup is if your trying to grill in the rain, and dont have a canopy for weather protection, thus exposing your electronic charger/transmitter to the elements. One final word of note that I cannot verify, but I read a review of the meater plus from a tech source, and the writer mentioned that If the internal temp of the meat is over 210°f for longer than 10 minutes then the internal sensor will break. I'm not sure why, or when you would allow meat to get to 210°f, but it's worth noting. In the end the meater plus is simply a shiney new toy that that fails to live up to the hype. It's unfortunate, it would have been nice to watch the game, and monitor my grill temp all at the same time.

review_title: Compared to ThermoPro the range is absolutely horrible
review_text: I've been looking at the meater product for some time now but the initial reviews of the original product left me hesitant due to the issues reported on the inferior range. Now with the meater+ I see the range has been increased to 165ft (or more)!... but, in practice that's not the reality. I managed to get the meater probe connected to the base when it was about 5 feet away from my smoker... no problem because the base is what should be connecting to my phone. The problem is, that connection goes another 10 feet at best when I'm indoors. It's pretty much useless for remote monitoring in the standard configuration. On the other hand, my old-tech ThermoPro probe and monitor still operate at a much better range. I can roam around most of my house with no issues. The idea is the same, but with some wires - The probes are inserted into the meat and the wires are lead outside of the smoker to a unit that hangs off or near the smoker. This unit connects to a remote display that I carry around. I was willing to pay the considerably higher price tag for the meater+ so that I could avoid the somewhat cumbersome wires and utilize the fancy app. The bonus being I didn't need to carry a separate device, I could just use my phone. I'm going to try the "meater link" feature to see if I can get the device connected to a tablet and then use the tablet as a range extender. It basically makes the app connect to the device via my home wifi network, which in theory should increase the range. However, this is just a cumbersome bandaid to get the functionality I thought I'd be getting with the standard configuration. Regarding support: I'm having much the same experience as others have reported. It takes days to get a response. I'm not really impressed with their customer support due to this. It sounds like they don't have enough bodies to handle the workload.

review_title: The battery checking system needs a big time update.
review_text: Nice system WHEN it works. Just about every cook I click the button it shows green. Pull the thermometer out and it’s dead. Clean connection but still dead. The Bluetooth strength is very weak. The wood box needs to be externally close to the thermometer. The smoker is on my porch and I have a brick house. I have to set my iPad next to the front door so it will stay connected while I use my phone to monitor from 20’ away. If you wrap with tinfoil it will not work on the inside. You have to poke it through the tinfoil and even then for some reason that might interfere with the connection. I would not buy again unless it was the fancier model. I’d look into getting a wired version instead.

review_title: Weak signal strength does not allow you to monitor food temp more than a foot away!!!
review_text: I'm giving this 2 stars because the signal strength is absolutely awful. The only reason it's not getting a 1 star is because it does give an accurate temperature reading. But if you want to monitor the food you're cooking you have to have the charging base and your phone within a foot of the meat thermometer. So if you put your meat in the oven, smoker, or literally anything other than sitting on the counter with your phone next to it you can not monitor the temperature which makes this device completely useless in my opinion. And no, this has nothing to do with my wifi strength, I have full wifi strength and I have even tested this by leaving the thermometer and charging base right next to WIFI router (where signal is absolute strongest) and if you walk more than a foot away with your phone you can no longer monitor the temperature. Unfortunately for me, I didn't use it often enough to realize just how bad it is until I was past my window for a return. Do yourself a favor and DO NOT BUY this product, unless you're just testing the temperature of your food while it's out of the oven/grill and you're standing within a foot of it.

I loved the idea of no wires. I had been using a different brand for two years. It has wires from prongs (inside grill) to receiver (sitting next to grill). Paint to clean. But it worked. I c could go anywhere in my house, in the basement, and never lose connection. I have used the MEATER plus twice. First time, I watched it constantly, and was able to reconnect by walking right next to the grill. The second time I used this, I connected while standing next to the grill. Walked inside the door (10 feet away) still connected. Then my neighbor knocked on the front door. I walked to the front of the house and I must have lost connection. After he left, I sat down to watch tv. About 25 feet from grill. I assumed I was still connected. And my fault for not constantly checking. And hour later, I remembered the meat cooking. Checked the app and no connection. Walked to the door that flies out to the grill (5 feet from the grill) it would not connect. I opened the glass door and was able to connect. I walked back to the tv room (25 feet from grill. Less than 20 feet from the door to the grill) and no connection. This might work for grills that you don’t have to close the top. But for me, this is useless. For this to work, I literally have to stand less than 10 feet away. At least I got this on sale during prime day. I am only out $75. Back to the old wired prongs with the range anywhere in my house. Anyone want a cool looking meter with no range, I will sell mine cheap

review_title: Small issues are irritating.  But its still very good
review_text: I'm going to ignore criticism of the hole size it punches in a roast. Once sliced, nobody notices. It is remarkably accurate and, if you do what it says, when it says to, the result is perfect. I've tried it now on rotisserie roasts and poultry as well as grilled meats, poultry, and fish (swordfish), with consistently good results Problems are two, and everybody has the first one. It disconnects randomly, phone to transmitter. The transmitter/charger sits next to the box on my grill while I sit in the house, about 10 feet away, reading or entertaining. All of a sudden I get an alarm that my phone and the transmitter have disconnected. 5 seconds later it reconnects and all is well... until the next time. One roast, on the rotisserie, meater and probe connected, meter and me not 14 times in an hour and a half. All for 5 seconds or less. Having to look at the phone that many times for no apparent reason is really, really an irritation. Especially if you have company. Second, and this is programmatic: The device tells you when to remove from heat and rest the beast. This really works and a roast comes up to the right temp where upon the Meater says Ready. But. If you're delayed getting there and the temp overshoots, the rest time doesn't adjust to the higher temp. That's really not Meater's fault, so just remember to keep your eye on the readout while its resting and cut early if necessary. All that done with... I love the thing, especially when rotisserie cooking. Update: it has become irritating. Every 5minutes or so, I get a" connection problem. Move the Meater closer to the probe" Well, see photo, the probe is at the front center of the grill. Things need to get fixed? Resting now, and more msgs every minute or so - connection lost, move phone closer to meater pro. See photo two.

review_title: Unreliable and inconsistent connection. It could ruin your cook.
review_text: I have used it 4 times now in 2 months. It worked fine the first 2 times. The last 2 times it would randomly disconnect overnight. I had the charging box box about 3-4 feet away from the smoker on the kitchen table. Their is a sliding door glass between the probe and the box. The first time it happened, it was only a pork butt and I was cooking it throughout the day so, thankfully, I caught that it disconnected. I reconnected it and an hour later it disconnected again. So I went back to my wired thermometer which has a wireless receiver that I can take anywhere in the house and monitor the cook. The second time it happened was overnight as I was smoking a brisket. Went to bed and woke up 7 hrs later to see the MEATER had disconnected from my phone. Our bedroom is about 15-20 feet away from the charging box with one interior wall between my phone and the box. I went out to the kitchen table and the green like was blinking which I understood to mean it is connected. It was not, as the app was saying it was disconnected and there were no readings. Thankfully I woke up because my brisket was at 180 degrees. I normally wrap it at 170 degrees. I went back to my wired thermometer with no issues. About 3 hrs later my wired thermometer alarm went off indicating my desired temp was hit. As I got up again, I looked at my phone and the MEATER was connected to my phone again!!! WTF?? I didn't do anything. Incidentally, the alarm never went off indicating my target temp was hit but the app still showed my target temp. I don't like the wires but at least my wired thermometer is reliable and consistent. If I hadn't woken up, my brisket, which wasn't cheap, may have been ruined.

I really wanted to like this product, and given the other good reviews I am wondering if I just got a bad one. For months after using it, the ambient sensor would be +/- 30 degrees Fahrenheit off from what other temperature sensors were showing. I thought it was something that I was doing wrong, so I continued testing with placement and calibrating my other equipment. I know that there are microclimates inside of any grill, and I know that the dome thermometer is not the be-all, end-all of readings. However, even right next to the thermometer the ambient sensor would fluctuate by a total of 50 degrees or more. Even if it was consistently wrong I could still use it, but I could never trust that it was reading too high or too low during a cook, which partially defeats the purpose of this product. For what it's worth, the internal temp probe was always spot on with my other probes. In contacting support, I got the standard "it's going to read differently than other thermometers" response and the ticket was closed. I didn't see anywhere where they recommend or discourage testing or calibration, but at that point I figured why not and tested the ambient sensor in boiling water as you would a standard probe. The first test levelled off at 185F, the second test at 235F. Other probes in the water read 212F as you would expect. I'll still use it for internal temperatures and I love the app, but I'm going to have to come up with an alternate solution for remote reading the ambient temperature.
One of the worst thermometers I have used. Constantly loses connection to it's dock to the point it's nearly worthless. It'd be a great product if the connection actually worked.

review_title: When it works, it’s okay. Too bad it rarely does.
review_text: The probe itself is a nice idea, able to monitor my smoker temp and internal meat temp simultaneously. But when it’s inside the smoker, it has an effective range of almost nothing. I use a Weber Smokey Mountain, and have an attached tabletop. It loses connectivity with the base, which is literally sitting 18 inches or less away. The base loses connectivity to my phone, and I’m literally sitting on the porch 8 feet away, because it won’t reach the kitchen on the other side of that wall (my Bluetooth headphones and speakers do). The idea is sound, but the execution is bad. There are other products on the market that are better, where I can go into the house and I can still monitor the cook.

I bought two of these for Christmas in 2024. One for my husband and one for his Dad. The first cooks were awesome! It’s was such a convenient product, however, the devices constantly lose connection from the charger to the probe. I called customer support and they were helpful. It worked a few times then blitzed out on me. Changed the battery in the charger….re paired it, to no avail. The same thing happened to my father in laws unit. We were so hopeful for this product but have been left quite disappointed and they are not that cheap.

review_title: Not as good as other systems
review_text: The app never stops beeping during a cook. The ambient temp reading is way off.

review_title: Great for the app's recipes and terrible for everything else.
review_text: The device only barely works. The bluetooth connectivity is truly only accurate to approx 15-20 feet with direct and unobstructed line of sight, which defeats the purpose of a cordless/remote thermometer. As far as accuracy goes, it isn't. I'ved used my meater+ around 50 times and it has never given an accurate temperature. I kept using it because of how much I spent, but it ruining yet another pork shoulder today is the final straw: it gave a consistent read of 193 for nearly 3 hours before I finally decided to check the temp with 2 different battery thermometers to find the pork shoulder to be closer to 220. Shame on me for being tricked 50 times, but I just wanted this expensive fridge magnet to eventually work.

Used twice. First time had a hard time figuring out how to even get it to connect to the app but it eventually did and cooked the pork perfectly. Second time also struggled getting it to connect to app but also if I wasn't standing directly in front of the oven it would disconnect every time.

Constantly receive messages that the base disconnects from the probe. Sometimes it won’t work when I have the lid closed on my smoker. When it works, it is great. App is okay but not great. I wouldn’t buy again.

Worked great until it did not. I got maybe a dozen cooks out of this product. Worked as advertised. After that it lost connectivity with the app. Tried all the troubleshooting tips I could find. Don’t recommend this product until proven more reliable.

review_title: When it worked (3 times) it was amazing
review_text: They thought of everything except building a product that lasts. The app and interface are amazing and when the thermometer worked it was almost grill nirvana. With the ambient probe you set almost any alert you could think of. The ability to also monitor your cooks over the internet with an additional iOS device was also pretty sweet. Sadly though this only lasted through 3 cooks. (Turkey, Ham, and a Tri-Tip) It seems like there is an issue that if the ambient portion of the thermometer gets even the slightest bit dirty it prevents the probe from connecting to the block. I have scrubbed and scrubbed and after the last cook it will now not connect. I am including pictures so you can see how clean it actually is. Will update after my conversation with customer service. In their own words...”We are experiencing a high number of inquiries over the holiday season and may be slower to respond. Queries will be answered in the order that they are received. We aim to get back to you within 3-5 working days (Monday - Friday)” Hmmm. Wonder why?!? If they get it figured out will be great. Would just wait until the 2nd or 3rd generation

Terrible at reading temp, and the app is horrible. This thermometer will routinely read far too low or high when measured against an analog thermometer. To the tune of 10*+. Additionally, the app will tell you to “remove from heat” way too early OR late. This results in a coin flip between under or over cooked. I was cooking a New York at 425* on my Traeger today, aiming for a 130*’internal temp. The temp on the Meater skyrocketed from 100-121 and said “remove from temp”, which I promptly did at 122*. It then only proceeded to 124*, indicating that the quick temperature rise was likely lag, and the app not knowing the difference and thinking the steak was heating quickly. I took it inside and pan fried it to finish since it was now undercooked, but after waiting for the pan to heat up the steak was basically ruined. Just one example of many at this point.
Complicated to set up and use app
Worked for a while. Can’t recharge even after following all instructions.

My daughter has a meater plus and she loves it. I purchased it and I don't love it. If someone is barbecuing outside, your phone must be outside close to the thermometer. I cannot sit in my living room with my phone when the food is cooking in the kitchen. This was a bad investment for me.

review_title: I wanted to like this, but had to return it.
review_text: We really thought this was a great idea. And it is, just a poor execution in our case anyway. The unit we received had very poor wifi range. My wife could not even walk out of the kitchen without the probe disconnecting. The entire point of this is that you do not need to babysit your food in the oven. But if you can't leave the kitchen, what is the point? For what this cost, we expected it to work better, and maybe they do. But the one we received did not work well at all.

review_title: Decent when it works, but too faulty
review_text: I've been through so many crappy digital thermometers and was so stoked about this one. Great concept and really wanted to love it, but too many flaws. Used mine for close to 2 years, finally died and TBH I'll be happy to toss it in the trash and quit stressing over it. I spent 2 hrs on chat with customer service, who wanted all sorts of tests - which ended in them wanting me to close the app, kill all my connectivity to my phone (which guess what, killed our chat and my confidence in the product, warranty and service). 1) Getting it to pair with the base is one thing, getting it to pair and stay connected with the probe is problematic 2) Connection drops all the time 3) Doesn't really work if you use a Big Green Egg (BGE) with the top closed, especially at any distance, even if the base is right next to it. 4) High temp / grill flares will cause it to alert you and probably ruin it 5) First few cooks were wildly off in terms of accuracy. Seemed to get better but I still questioned it often when cooking chicken Save your money & stress.

review_title: Like standing around your oven while things cook? This is for you!
review_text: Bought this for myself for Christmas. The first time I used it was on a small turkey and we were all in the kitchen. I thought "wow, this is cool!". But.... (always a but right?) the next time I used it was on my BBQ grill. It can only take ambient temps up to 500 degrees and a BBQ grill can go way above that, especially my Infrared grill. No go on the BBQ. I had to yank it out of the tri-tip halfway through since I was getting warnings. The real kicker for the bad review is the range. It says 165 feet. i think they missed a decimal. More like 16.5 feet. I was slow-cooking ribs in the oven (since I cant use the BBQ grill). Worked great, until I went into the living room with my phone - about 40' with an open floor plan (nothing to block the signal). Started getting disconnected messages over and over. "Move the charger closer to the thermometer". Mkay... the only way to get it closer would have been to put the box in the oven with the probe. Finally found a sweet spot about 5' away on the counter. But the phone was still throwing errors that it couldn't connect. Apparently, unless you are standing in the kitchen 5 feet from the sensor... this won't work - at least for me. Looks like I am out $89.00. Going back to my wired one with the wireless sensor since that works 100' away at least. Great concept, needs more work.

review_title: Awesome idea, worked amazingly well....until it didn't.
review_text: Purchased the Meater+ in April 2020 and have used it dozens of times on various meats on various cooking devices. My initial impression when I first began using it was that it was pretty great on long, low-and-slow cooks, but it struggled on higher temp fast cooks because it seemed to take so long for the internal algorithm to figure estimate the done time. That has seemed to improve over time - perhaps a firmware update was pushed since I first started using it. It also seems to be sensitive enough that the ambient temp reading it actually affected by the temp of the meat. For example, if you put the probe in a piece of meat straight from the fridge, and then put the meat on a hot grill, the ambient temp reads quite a bit lower than expected. Again, minor quibbles. The deal breaker is that the probe stopped working all together in the middle of a cook recently. It was not a battery or charge issue, or an issue with the probe being too far from the base. The probe will disconnect from the base now when it is literally an inch away from it, and when I can get it to re-connect the probe now no longer reports ambient temp. In a hot grill (350F) it gives no ambient temp and provides a warning message that the ambient temp is too low to register. I've submitted a support request with the manufacturer, so hopefully they will make good on the 12-month warranty. I'll report back here when it's resolved one way or the other.

review_title: Started strong, but faltering of late.
review_text: When I first acquired the meter, I was pretty happy with it. However, the last two cooks have changed my mind. I tried it in a Ninja Foodi Possible cooker, and the base lost contact with the thermometer. The same thing happened when I tried to use it in my Traeger smoker grill. Not sure what’s going on with it, but I find myself going back to the wired meat thermometer and manually monitoring the temperature.

I've been using the Meater for several months now. I'm not very impressed. I grill at least once or twice a week and use it for chicken, tomahawk steaks, thick pork chops, etc., meat that takes longer and is difficult to tell when it's done enough inside. Recently, it's started losing connection with my phone and tells me to move the phone closer to the Meater. I've stood over the grill with the phone and it still won't connect or will connect but keeps losing the connection. I can't put the phone on the grill! I keep it charged so that isn't the problem. I don't think it gives an accurate temperature reading either. From the beginning, the meat is not done to what I selected. I sometimes have to put the meat back on for a little bit. I expected better. It's ok but not worth the money. The app is also not very user friendly. I would not buy it again.

Probe too thick for many cuts of meat (supermarket available). Tried for pot roast in an Allclad dutch oven with lid in regular oven - no connection. Adjusted location to get periodic connection but when liquid level rose in pot and touched the probe all connection was lost and app “blew up”. Tossed in the garbage and finished up the job with my hand held digital.

I so badly wanted to like this thermometer. A single probe, Bluetooth enabled device. Unfortunately, it very rarely stays connected, even when placing the unit on the handle of my smoker. It will stay connected for a few minutes and then lose connection. I have used it successfully on two occasions or approximately 5% of the time.

Connectivity on these suck a$$. Transmitter is literally less than a foot from the receiver and it loses connection. Same with my Weber. Otherwise, when it works, it’s kinda cool. The estimated cook time is definitely a rough estimate. If you get lucky and get one that works, the functionality is 4-5stars. Otherwise, I’d only give it one star. I’m being generous giving it two stars today.
As a chef, this product is terrible. I can't believe any positive reviews. No wonder they dropped the price.

I got ONE cook out of this $80 piece of junk. I made the mistake of purchasing it earlier than I needed to make sure it was on hand so I didn’t immediately cook with it. It won’t charge. I contacted Amazon and it can’t be returned. I was 3 days past the 30 day window. I’ll not be buying Meater again and encourage you to look at other brands.

review_title: Was gifted it and glad I didn’t buy with my own money
review_text: I was given the MEATER for a Christmas present and I’m glad I didn’t spend my own money on this thermometer. It was easy to set up, and it had a decent battery life… however, one brisket cook in my smoker at 275 and it basically killed the thing. It has to charge in just one specific angle and even then it’s 50/50. Beyond that, it wasn’t particularly accurate. I was comparing it to my tried and true kitchen thermometer that I’ve had for years and it was reading about 10 degrees lower. I also ran into connectivity problems - where it would drop out every 5-10 minutes overnight. Very stressful. I plan on buying a different wireless meat thermometer, that can actually withstand long smokes and won’t crap out after the first use.
Another solution looking for a problem. Regret the purchase, back to using standard meat thermometer.
Doesn’t connect well

review_title: Not accurate and charging/status is fiddly
review_text: This thing is definitely not accurate. I have thermopen thermometers and they all agree when this one doesn’t. It’s consistently incorrect though. Even when looking at the individual temperatures along the probe, none agree with an instant read thermometer that is right next to it. By 10 degrees F…. On top of that, leaving this in the charger, in the drawer apparently doesn’t leave this device ready to use whenever needed. You need to make sure that you’ve planned at least 15 minutes prior to putting the thermostat in the meat because this will need to recharge. Also, it won’t pair with your phone while the probe is in the charger, so you have no idea if it’s having Bluetooth pairing issues until after the charge is complete. When it works, and you know the limitations and the variance in temperature, it is helpful.

review_title: Not as good as it claims.
review_text: It is constantly disconnecting from the app, it claims it has a far range but that isn't the case for me. It's nearly unusable.
Very low range for connection, user interface is very annoying. For the price, I expected a more premium product.

review_title: Buy lots of AAA batteries, and plan on shrt lifespan.
review_text: Great product, but you have to change the battery about an hour before you use it, each time. Also, customer service is really bad. The probes go bad very quickly. Go with a different product.

Save your money, pulled it out from not using it over the winter and it registered a low battery so I replaced the battery, had the box within 3’ of the sensor and it kept dropping connection and displaying an error message that signal was lost. I confirmed that probe tip was clean and still dropping connection. Going to shop a more reliable option!
Dreadful piece of junk works poorly and dies soon.

review_title: Great features ruined by terrible range
review_text: When this thermostat is actually connected and working, it’s a nice piece of tech. The interface is clean, and the features work exactly as advertised when you're standing right next to it. ​Unfortunately, the connectivity is an absolute dealbreaker. To use the app or see data, I have to stay within 5 feet of the meter at all times. The moment I step any further away, even in the same room, it completely disconnects. Because of this incredibly weak range, the smart features are rendered absolutely useless. You shouldn't have to stand face-to-face with a wireless device just to get it to work. ​If you only plan on checking it manually or don't mind standing right next to it to sync data, it’s decent. But if you actually want a functional wireless thermometer you can monitor from across the room, let alone another part of the house, look elsewhere.

I am disappointed with the quality of the product. I had one for about 2 years and the charger stopped working, I bought another in May 2025 probably used it 10 times and the probe and the black top have pulled away from the probe housing. Time to move on.
Thermometer came apart after just a few months of use. The device separated at the plastic tip and steel intersection. Appears that the glue may have been degradated by heat. Disappointed 😞

review_title: Only OK.  Better options are out there
review_text: Good for a few cooks but then keeping it connected is next to impossible. Even when it's connected it disconnects constantly. Way overpriced for this kind and of performance. There are cheaper models that perform better out there.
Very unreliable. Worked a few times then just stopped connecting. Either the prob couldn’t connect to the base or the base couldn’t connect to my phone. Became more trouble than it’s worth.
Really cool when it works. But it has a hard time staying connected. It’s frequently disconnecting from the app which is very frustrating.

The best I can say…. It’s fine. No better, and in several cases worse, than what I already have. I grill and smoke food every weekend and enjoy buying new gadgets and tools zine this is my favorite hobby. If this item were $20, I’d give it a better rating, but for $100 it’s mediocre at best.
It would be nice to have a battery meter, so half way through cooking it informs you of a low battery then dies.
It was a great meat thermometer while it lasted. Just not long enough for a good rating.
The app keeps disconnecting from the probe at less than 100 feet

I bought this in 2022. I always had connection issues with it from day one. The charging with one AAA battery is not great. I think I used this product 40 times. Every time was an issue and not it broke completely. When it does work it is great.
The wifi and Bluetooth range on these suck!

I really love the idea of wireless. Having dogs, I didn’t want the wire for safety reasons. I also didn’t want a bunch or wires to roll up and store, and the attractiveness of the small size, self storage wooden box, no wires that could be pulled and damaged was very appealing. I read the product reviews and thought this would work as it is being used in our home, in our kitchen which isn’t large at all. After all, I’m not grilling or out on a lake in a boat where I can see connectivity being an issue, and planned on the probe, base and my phone being less than 10-12 feet from one another. Downloading the app and the instructions to get started cooking our turkey were super easy. The best part was seeing how quickly our turkey cooked to avoid dry turkey. The cooking time should have been 3.5 hours and it only took 2.25 hours. I know another 1.15 hours of cooking would have certainly resulted in a dried out bird. There are audible tones that keep you aware of what is going on as long as you maintain connectivity. The turkey was delicious; white meat was super juicy, once off the bird and plated, a knife really wasn’t necessary as a fork would do. Best turkey I’ve ever made! The probe was easy to clean, just wiped clean. Nice looking, compact wooden base to store the probe. Love the magnetic battery compartment, no more lost or broken pieces. Downfall? Connectivity. I needed spin the turkey around to have the probe closest to the cookware drawer where I needed to put the base unit directly next to the oven and keep my phone on the counter next to the stove where I was working with liquids and other items used to prepare the meal so I could keep an eye on the app because the probe, base unit and phone lost connection multiple times. Even in doing that, the probe, base unit and my phone kept disconnecting and were not communicating. I needed to manually troubleshoot and reconnect. We lost connection over 10x, which concerned me because who wants to choke on a dry turkey or one that needs to be drowned in gravy?! Because the probe, base and my phone kept losing connection, I needed to “babysit” the connection on my phone. Isn’t this why anyone would want the MeatR+ to begin with? I attempted to contact their customer service via app email for help and needed the Amazon order number, serial number, fill out the online form. On Thanksgiving, I needed to prepare the meal, not spend 15+ minutes to get the information while the probe continued glitching and not reading the turkey temp which at that point, it was cooking fast and minutes were being shaved off at a quick rate. I was going to not even bother trying to have the probe, base and my phone reconnect as it became disappointing and more of an interruption to have to watch the app very closely while trying to get other things done. Also, using the app will eat your battery life, so start with a decent charge on your phone or have a charger handy if your phone is older. I had high hopes the MeatR+ would not lose connection for me since the turkey, prove, base unit and my phone all were in our small kitchen. Playing around where the probe, unit and my phone were was critical! I ended up needing to place the probe and unit less than 3ft from one another and my phone was on the counter less than 3.5 ft from the base unit and even then we lost connection. I kept opening the oven, opening the lower cabinet and putting my phone close to regain connection. It did every time, but I wasn’t expecting connectivity issues with everything now on aces less than 3.5 fr from one another. Our counters are granite, maybe this was the issue? The turkey was roasted in a dark blue and white speckled roasting pan (thin metal) with a single layer of foil over the top of the turkey with the lid on it. Probe was placed in the breast of the turkey with the probe turned to be closest to the lower cabinet drawer that had the base unit in. It’s a great idea, would love to have it work as intended. Maybe the company has some tips? Maybe our unit was a bum one that got literally was dropped shipped somewhere along the line? (Amazon driver stacked our delivery neatly, so IDK.) While the product is easy to use, the more than expected disconnections from probe to base unit to phone and the constant need to watch my phone and then troubleshoot what went wrong and reconnect. The MeatR+ lost connectivity more times than I would have expected, it wasn’t quick to reconnect each time, or trouble free to use. Because of that, it’s losing 3 stars for “ease of use”. Sad, because my brother in law was interested in it; he does a LOT of outdoor cooking on his grill, smoker and big green egg, and was interested in the multiple probe unit.

review_title: So close to being an amazing product.
review_text: An update (April 2022) to my original review. My original post can be seen at the end. Purchased again in April of this year and the experience is much better but still needs a ton of work. This is now the 3rd time I am purchasing this product, but only 2nd time I'm actually getting to successfully use it. What I love: - The Ambient temperature sensor. This feature is crucial if you are serious about smoking / BBQ. The built-in thermometers on most grills and offset smokers are usually very poor quality, and give skewed readings. Because they are connected to the metal of the grill, and because they are located at the top of the cooking chamber they tend to read much hotter than the air/environment where your food is actually being cooked. The fact that I only need 1 probe to read both internal and ambient temperature is fantastic. What needs work? The bamboo/wooden charging case feels premium, but there's no real way to clean it. And if that thermometer isn't 100% dry when you put it back, that's just a breeding ground for mold. A major design flaw to this charging case is the fact that it doesn't have any indication of whether or not the probe is charging. Now, this may not seem like a huge deal at first, but then I ran into the same issue I had with the first unit I purchased. The first use, it works great. However, after cleaning it (I thought thoroughly enough but was proven wrong) I stored the probe back in the charging case, expecting it to be charged the next time I needed to use it. Now, a delay of needing to wait to charge this probe for a few hours can delay a BBQ project by an entire day. I woke up at 6 am this morning to start an all-day smoke to find that the probe would not power on no matter what I tried. Turned out, the probe never was charging. After contacting customer support and finding some helpful tips on Reddit, I found that even if the back charging plate looks clean, it often isn't clean enough to make a connection with the charger. The support recommended using baking soda and a coarse sponge (which I did the first 2 times I tried cleaning it). I ended up finding a post on Reddit suggesting I use fine-grit sandpaper to fully clean the back tip of the probe to ensure it would charge properly. After trying this, thankfully it was finally charging. BUT I had no way of actually knowing whether or not the probe was charging until a few hours later when I took it off the charger. I'm hoping in a future version they add a charging indicator to the case. The software has definitely improved by leaps and bounds from my first review, but still needs a ton of work. Originally, it was incredibly difficult to remove/reset a device if you were having issues. Now, it's possible but I found that the menus were sending me in circles. Since I first tried the product, the functionality of the "estimated cooking time remaining" has never worked. When the Meater+ works, it's great. But it's too inconsistent. It feels incomplete. ORIGINAL 2021 REVIEW: I was so excited about this! I had seen it on youtube and bought it immediately. It seems like a great idea, but executed poorly. In the app, there is no way to specify which phone/tablet you want to use as a base station, and which one you want to have as the "remote" device. I was leaving my iPad out by the grill, and bringing my phone inside with me so I could view the temperature from inside. But the thermometer kept defaulting to try and connect to my phone instead of the iPad that was less than 5 feet away. There is no easy way to connect a second device to the app, or to factory reset one. After one use, the thermometer would not charge or connect to any device. It just died after one use. The one time it did work, it worked fantastically (if I was close enough). I think the app UI needs some rethinking. I really wanted to keep using this, but it died after one use. When I tried to order a replacement, my order was lost, and took a few weeks to fix the issue. I don't even want to try again. Best Buy has another brand of smart thermometer and I think I will end up trying that one instead.

3/5 Stars — Disappointing Longevity for the Price I purchased my MEATER thermometer in January 2023 for approximately $100, and it has already stopped charging. While I appreciate the convenience and functionality, I expected better durability from a premium kitchen thermometer. At this price point, I would expect more than 3–4 years of reliable use. Overall, a great concept, but disappointing longevity and questionable long-term value.
Funciono perfecto hasta el 5 mes, donde se despegó la cabeza y ya no funciona bien...

review_title: Great results, user interface and cost is disappointing
review_text: I love the function and results. My unit worked Feb thru Sept the stopped working. The use interface needs to work better in bypassing the tutorial. I also disliked the “reporting use” back to the mfr. again, the results were awesome, but the user interface and cost to use less than a year is disappointing.
Unimpressed overall. The 165 foot range rating is not accurate. If the app was better and range of the Bluetooth was longer or could connect through wifi, that would be great.

review_title: When it worked, it was excellent... BUT
review_text: When it worked, it was fantastic. Real time temperature readings and accuracy were exactly what I wanted. I understand why my son raves about his more expensive dual probe model. BUT... 1. The base needed to be extremely close to the probe to pick up the signal, and when it lost signal it took significant time to get back in sync. I ended up having to place the base on top of my Weber kettle, which was not optimal. 2. It eats batteries. And there was no low battery indicator. Not fun to be replacing battery when you are needing to put the meat on the grill. 3. It quit working entirely 13 months after purchase. I estimate that I only used it about 50 times.
Had it for 5 years, finally just quit. Probe won't connect anymore.

review_title: A grilling accessory that may or may not work for you!
review_text: Like many others, it can be quite a challenge while grilling meat on our favorite grills. In my case, my wife and I was looking for something "new" which would help us to perfect the art of grilling our meat, such as chicken and steaks. After having read the reviews, we thought this might be a good option. Its meat probe recharges while in the box, the box itself has magents which one can affix to their grill (must be in a cool place, NOT hot). It's also connected to your WiFi and you can monitor the various aspects of your cooking via the app. The problem we encountered was that our probe seems to have failed us. We used it multiple times and then the last time, it kept warning us that the temperature was too high, which could result in damaging the probe. We immediately took it off the grill and tried it again the next time we used it. Experienced the same issue then. Others may have better experience with this than what we did. We ended up purchasing a ThermoPen One, to assist us in our grilling. PROS: Traeger owned, nice app for Android/iOS CONS: Wish it had lasted longer than what it did. Must say that one needs to monitor the app when it tells you that the temperature is too high, which could result in damaging the probe. This could have very well been the case for us. We DID take it off immediately after our app started "blaring" like an emergency alert but for one reason or another, it no longer seems to work properly. Caveat Emptor (buyers beware).

review_title: Not for long cooks or long range
review_text: Bought this over a year ago and tried to use it for pellet smoker cooks. One problem I noticed is I had to have the receiver with about 10 feet of the grill and then my Bluetooth connection would fail if I moved 20-30 feet away. Then it would take a minute for it to reconnect and recalculate itself. I love the idea of this thing. It does its best to take all the guesswork out of the cook by reading the meat temp, air temp, and rate of cooking to estimate when your cook should be done. It even tries to tell you when to take the meat off the heat to let it rest and have the temp rise the rest of the way during the rest. A big problem I’ve had with that is it either doesn’t calculate the end time correctly (I’m not looking for it to give me rest times, but I get why it does. I haven’t been able to disable that feature) or just doesn’t calculate them at all because it’s still trying to figure something out. The most frustrating thing about this is the battery life. If you plan to use this to cook anything longer than 7 hours, don’t start using it until 6 hours before you expect it to be done. I haven’t had it last through a pork shoulder or a brisket. Unfortunately, I’ve had it too long to return and I really don’t use it much. Shorter cooks like turkey, chicken, ribs, it’s ok. Wish the probe could be a little thinner. Again, I love the idea of this, I just don’t think it’s where it should be, yet. Temperature accuracy is a bit spotty, too, but if you can calibrate it with some ice water and boiling water, you’ll figure out your offset. Not sure if I trust the air temp end. It always reads 50 degrees hotter than the smoker is set at.

I so wanted this to work and give it a great review, but unfortunately, I can’t. I read a lot of reviews about it and the consensus was the Bluetooth connection wasn’t what the promised I purchase mine in November of 2023 and have tried different strategies to overcome the connection problems, but nothing has worked. You must be basically right next to our smoker for it to connect. Our patio table is only 13 feet (yes, the OCD in me is at work here) from our smoker and I am out of range already. Our smoker. stays connected to its app when I am in the house with a line of sight to it at almost 40 feet through our patio doors. Other that the connection problems I love it, straight forward settings on the app and the info you get is great. If they fixed the Bluetooth connection problems, it would be an awesome temperature probe

review_title: Good Range, Non-Submersible, but probe came apart after one year
review_text: I bought the Meater to replace a setup I was using that required wired probes into the meat, and then wireless to another unit to monitor just the meat temperature. I like the Meater as it is truly wireless. I did notice that if you insert the probe in far enough that not much bare metal shows, that the ambient temperature is way off. Yesterday I left about 3/8" to 1/2" below the black Ambient sensor and used my regular oven's Air Fry feature, and the ambient temperature was very close to the actual temperature inside the oven. I've been very careful with the probe, as to not submerse it in water when cleaning. I've ruined other brands probes by soaking them, and learned the hard way. Maybe in the future there will be a way to better water proof instead of just water resistant of the probes. The App is great. I really like being able to use it on my tablet or phone. I prefer the tablet for the larger display. The time remaining recalculates throughout the cook process and gets more accurate as the cook time-ending nears, as it should be. Very much an upgrade to what I was using before, and love that the probe charges itself from a AA battery in the base. The base is magnetic so I leave mine on the side of the refrigerator next to the oven. UPDATE - The Probe with my Meater pulled apart when removing from chicken breast. I purchased the Meater Pro2 directly from Meater, that provided me with a discount due to the product failure of my original Meater. The New Meater Pro2, while is supposed to be an upgraded model, frequently disconnects from my tablet. The distance is about 25 feet. The Original Meater did not have this problem, and the tablet sat in the same location. I've replaced the battery that came with the unit with a new battery and the frequent disconnects are making me not like the Pro2 version. I do like that the probe of the Pro2 is rated at a higher temperature, and dishwasher safe. But if you can't use it with your tablet at a distance of 25 feet without frequent disconnects, it starts to become useless very quickly.

review_title: Not as accurate as a hand-held meat thermometer
review_text: When I was looking for a Bluetooth thermometer, I was concerned about the software I'd be installing on my phone. I sort of doubt any of them contain malware, but I also didn't want software that hasn't been thoroughly tested or that might not work after three or four phone updates. That's why I went with a Known Brand like Meater - I figured any bugs would have been flushed by now, and they would still be around in a few years. I think that was a good call, and the software is certainly attractive and easy to use. The probe does a good job of telling me the "ambient" temperature inside a closed smoker. That's the good news. The bad news (part 1) is that the probe is REALLY hard to place with any accuracy. There's a groove 2.5 inches from the probe tip, and you must insert the probe so that groove is inside the meat, lest you damage the probe. That might be OK with a big roast, but it's quite hit or miss with a chicken breast or chicken thighs, and ribs are just out of the question. Most of the time, the temperature the Meater reports is a lot higher than what a handheld thermometer reports, probably because the actual sensor is too close to the surface.
