The bad news (part 2) is that the estimated cook time is ridiculously inaccurate in Low & Slow mode with an ambient temperature in the low 200s. The bad news (part 3) is that the range is really poor - you have to keep the charger/repeater within a few feet of the grill, and your phone within a few feet of the charger. They have something they call the Meater Cloud, but whatever it does, it sure doesn't let me keep my phone in my pocket and walk away from the smoker.
You can’t go far from it without the Bluetooth disconnecting from your phone.

I have used it a few times. Worked great. Was very happy. Find now after six months battery need replacing often. Also if put in a pan with aluminum foil to cover it looses signal. Have far to much to do to preplan the use of a device. When I test the battery it shows full. So not really sure why it doesnt keep the tool charged. I clean end after each use to maintain the clean contacts

review_title: Meh...connectivity issues limit it's use for me...
review_text: TLDR: Accurate, but connectivity issues limit its usefulness for me. Full review: So I see the reviews and read many of them before I decided to purchase. The good: I've done several cooks with it and I'm happy to say that it's a very accurate thermometer. Much better than others I own. It's solid, built well and is really a quality item. The app is a bit annoying, but decent. HOWEVER, the connectivity issues cannot be ignored. The probe constantly loses connection with the probe. I know that this connectivity relies a lot on variable factors, but how can the probe and base lose connection when the base is literally a foot away?? I smoked a chuck pot roast, and finished in the oven. I used the magnets to stick the charger/base on the oven door, with the pot inside the oven less than a foot away! It can't hold the connection!?!? Seriously?? The only way to get it closer would be to put it in the oven!!! To explain, the probe connects to the charger base, and the base is bluetoothed to my phone (more on that below). Bluetooth can also be a big drain on your battery for some devices, especially if you're moving around a lot. So be prepared to stay in the immediate area. Secondly, this CANNOT USE WIFI without a secondary device such as another phone or tablet... and the setup to get it to be wifi'ed is about as confusing as Chinese math. So unless you want to be hovering around your cook all day, this falls very short IMO. I have other thermometers that use wifi, so if I have to leave the house, I can still monitor my cook, but their accuracy isn't as good as the meater. If I could get that wifi functionality with an accurate thermometer like the meater, I'd be much happier.
Worked well for about 2 years then stopped charging. Tried cleaning probe as instructed, changed battery, cleaned base, still won't work. Works well while it lasts.

Am I missing something. Can you have wi-fi on this. Don’t like the fact if it’s only Bluetooth. I don’t want to sit at home for a 12 hour smoke and not be able to watch the temps if I decide to leave my house. Am I doing something wrong

review_title: Disconnects often, but is still pretty awesome
review_text: This thermometer is AWESOME! ...when it works. Connectivity is a huge problem, my phone will disconnect from the case (headquarters) when I'm 5 feet away. It beeps at me, then reconnects 5 to 20m later. A lot of people are having the same problem it seems. Meater needs to address this issue. Other than that, I like the interface, it is very user friendly, and the videos and tutorials are probably very helpful for beginners. Great idea

review_title: Glad it was a 1/2 price deal
review_text: Bluetooth goes in and out... range far less than stated (at least in my circumstance). I will say the probe is accurate and really like enjoyed not having wired probes to deal with.

Bought this thinking I could use it to monitor the cook in my smoker remotely while I'm out and about running errands in town. It doesn't work like that, and TBF I guess that's partially my own fault for not reading the spec sheet thoroughly. This is primarily for monitoring your cook while within bluetooth distance. Problem is the bluetooth range is absolutely terrible, the app is frequently telling me that I'm out of range and need to move closer, sometimes when I'm no more than 20ft away...cue much repositioning until the signal re-establishes. I believe there is a long-distance feature using the "Meater Cloud" option, but from what I can tell this is also pretty junky because it still requires you to have a phone/tablet local. Couldn't even get this feature to work properly but my understanding is the connection looks something like Probe -> Meater Unit -> Phone/Tablet ----INTERNET----> Phone in your pocket. It's such a convoluted way of doing things that it's just not worth the hassle. Temperature readings and estimated cook time remaining are pretty accurate when there's a stable temp, it doesn't do a good job at recalculating if you open the grill/smoker lid, adjust heat, etc (yeah, I know you shouldn't really do that anyway, but c'mon, how hard can it be to detect a consistent change in temp and recalculate?). Often times it fails to even give a time estimate and just sites there "calculating". It's not quite junk, but it's not far off. Construction is solid, aspects of the app work well, the overall package just isn't good enough though.

review_title: Two design flaws, and a suggested fix
review_text: Two design flaws: 1. It disconnects from the app when the grill cover is closed, even when I keep the charging box right next to the grill and place my cellphone in the house window about 15 feet from the grill. So, I can’t relax with friends or even be anywhere else on the property as I have to be able to get to the window to see what is going on with the food. I bought the more expensive one hoping I could get the 135 feet of connection, but I don’t even get 15 feet because my infrared grill cooks best when the cover is closed. And, I don’t have an extra cellphone to leave next to the grill as a repeater, as some suggest. 2. The ambient temperature of my infrared grill is almost always over that allowed, so I am always panicking that I am going to burn up this expensive new thermometer. I am going to take it on our upcoming camping vacation, where the RV grill cooks without the cover being closed. If it works well there, I may keep the thing. And I am going to try it in the oven tomorrow when I cook a turkey. If it does not lose connection because the oven is made of metal, then it may also be worth keeping for oven cooking. For grill cooking, it is not up to standards yet, and therefore not worth the $99 price tag to me. It should be sent back to the design lab for improvements. Simply make AN EXTENSION to the thermometer which sticks out the side or front of the grill so it both keeps the connection to the app, and keeps the brains of the thermometer cool. Duh. I bought it because the wired Maverick thermometer I use for many years has switched to a cheap cable which stops working anytime the cable gets coiled or slightly bent. I’m tired of buying new ones.

I think accurate dynamic monitoring of internal temp is key to perfect grilling. The OC side of me loves the time graph of external and internal temps on the app, you can really fine-tune a "cook," and keep notes for future reference. Quality manufacturing here, too. As for the wireless design, it's amazing that they have packed that all this into a probe. But there's a price for convenience. The probe is itself is BIG, and needs to be inserted a long ways in to work correctly. I've found burger patties and fish can fall apart around it. The initial "cold" insertion is critical, because if any part of the long probe is too close to the surface, or if the external part touches the grill surface when you flip, you can get anomalous results. Horseshoe sausages and quail are tricky for example. And once the probe is in, you can't safely mess with it. I've had wired probes, and used to yank out and re-set them on the fly with tongs, but this fatter probe is 'grabbier' and can tear up a delicate cut. And it stays hot longer. You don't want to grab it with anything metal that could scratch the end where it recharges. In short, Meater is a tool in the toolbox. It works great for thick cuts and whole birds, not so good for other configurations, or meats that you are going to manipulate further immediately after the cook (think reverse sear). As for wireless performance, YMMV but I found the connectivity is more spotty than the wired variety. The "estimated time remaining" feature is cool, but I found it necessary to stay close to the base unit and monitor it constantly, because if I walk away and signal drops it takes some time to recalculate. So, I thought we had a "holy grail" here, and I'll continue using it on large cuts, but for most grilling will stay with the wired variety, or handheld thermometers plus "eyeballing."

So far not so good. Ambient temperature is never correct, cook temp stops with inaccurate reading and will not go up even when increasing the cooking temperaturer & will not give estimated cooking time after 4 hours

review_title: A little squirrelly to connect, but once you do, it works flawlessly!
review_text: Just cooked a 25 lb turkey on the rotisserie and needed something portable. This baby worked like a champ, it told me the temp, the air temp in the grill, and the desired temp based on my choice. Since turkey was one of the options in the app, it also showed me the expected thermal performance (temp vs. time into the cook), then predicted the time remaining for the turkey. It was awesome! My first experience with a bluetooth gadget for monitoring temp remotely and it worked great! I also like that the meater+ range allows me to monitor the grill from within the house. __________ Follow on - I have tried the Meater several times after my initial success with the turkey, and get nonstop problems with connectivity. The probe isn't recognized or is recognized and then drops connection. This is too expensive a product to only get one reliable use from it. And note that I am SUPER careful about inserting it correctly and avoiding overheating. This is not a problem with me not doing it right, it seems to be something wonky with the way my Pixel 8 connects, perhaps something with the latest Android update? But I really don't want constantly monitor and troubleshoot this device. I think I might just switch back to a reliable wired thermometer, like the cavemen before me....

review_title: Very nice thermometer - but not for smoker
review_text: I really like this unit, and it has some great features that make it a breeze to use (once you figure it out the first time). The app is a little weird. You have to got to little icon at the bottom "custom cook" to put in temp. They are trying hard to get people to choose preselected temps/recipes by clicking type of protein, etc. This makes it feel amateurish. It really should just be a temp setting when you open the app without having to navigate to get to the basic function. The real problem comes with the smoker. I've used this in the smoker twice, both times with short to intermediate smoke times, but at the end of the day I have to get the sandpaper out. This unit charges on the wood unit, and the end of the probe clicks into the charger to complete the connection. So when you use this in the smoker, the probe gets coated in smoke and it won't make the connection. Try cleaning it traditionally, no dice. I had to use 200 grit sandpaper to get this to charge again. In itself, that's not really the hugest problem, I wonder how long until the probe is ruined from it? I'll keep using it, but not for the purpose I bought it specifically for, and that's a shame.

review_title: Does not stay connected, ambient temp is off by 25 degrees, need to use a second cellphone for range
review_text: Updated: I am going to 3 stars because I recently dug up an old phone to use as the "signal booster" for the Meater+. When using a second phone or second device it does give you "Unlimited range" because you are now using the cloud connection to view the cook. I am not giving 5 because the ambient is still off by 25-30 degrees and it seems crazy to have to use 2 cellphones for this. But it is a lot better when doing so. I wish this was better. I read all the reviews about it staying connected and I thought my smoker is on the patio and only separated by a glass door it should be fine. Well, it still doesn't stay connected at all. The second I close the door to the patio it disconnects. I even brought in my brisket to rest in the oven with no heat on and it still wouldn't connect unless I pressed the phone against the oven door. So basically this is useless to me. Also the ambient temp is off by about 25 degrees. So when my smoker was going at 225 it was reading at 200 - The internal temp seems to be working fine but what is the point of using a wireless thermometer if I have to go outside next to my smoker to check it when I have 2 probes I can just use at that point. Meater + not worth it.

I've had 3 of these. The good: They start off A+. They work, they are accurate (sometimes it will have a mood swing and throw some bizarre longer temp time but gathers it back. You can see the graph for your cook, compare using different temps (I used mine on my Traeger). I really learned how to perfect pork shoulders!! The bad: After some time they may not charge so you are all ready to put on the shoulder at 1am and your phone won't find it... grrrr it didnt charge!!! Or did it? The red / green LED on charger can be ambiguous. SO - after using a few months it may or may not be charged. This is with 3 of mine and my brother same experience. I thought I learned my lesson and began REALLY CLEANING IT every cook, especially the back / transmitter end for it to charge properly. Regardless I'd still have problems. And it can be a unsettling at 1am :( The range is also totally unreliable as my (and ALL?) smokers are totally metal.. so you have to use an old cell phone in a ziploc right beside smoker... no big deal - just don't buy the long range one. So- I gave it a 3. It was great at first but now I am done with them - to inconsistent in the long run. I pretty much know cook times by weight and just use a probe to take temp. My brother EXACT same description but with 2. (***Mine was actually 2 - I destroyed first one in the garbage disposal - MY FAULT)

The Meater + is a great product as long as it is working. Just hope you don't have to try to get it replaced under warranty. First you have to go through many steps (which assume you are an imbicile and can't follow directions) on their "support" website. When you finally get to the end -- where you hope to actually find out how to talk to a person, you get a form where you have to fill in model, serial number, where you got it, etc. When you get that done three options appear at the bottom: Email us, Chat with Us, Contact, only, surprise!!!! only the Email one works. There is no working chat option and never a phone number you can call. After you send the initial email don't expect a real response for at least two days. And even then that's just the beginning. Five emails and 11 days later I finally learned they were sending me a new probe. I also found out that warranty support is based in the UK, and if UK workers happen to be on holiday, you will hear nothing until they get back. You would think Meater could do better.

It's a good thermometer, fairly accurate. Easy to use and charge and set up a cook. This is the plus version, and when I say there is no plus about it, believe it. It's supposed to have 165 ft range.... more like 10 feet. Literally. The app disconnects after about 10-12 feet everytime. Have the block right next to the cook too, everytime I walk away disconnect. Every single time. This is my second MEATER and both have had terrible range and disconnect issues. You can theoretically pair another device with it to act as a bridge but why in the heck should I do that? MEATER claims 165 feet, you kidding me? They also say you can share or create a web link to the cook so you can check remotely. Yeah that don't work either. Says my cook ended at 97 degrees at 1249 am but the cook is still going and I pushed through the stall sitting at 188. If you don't mind going outside to check it constantly and see the readout on your phone right next to the cook then it's a good thermometer - but a $10 instant read is better. It's a wireless thermometer, but it's not.,,,

At first it was great. Now, not two years later, I can't get the probe to connect. New batteries. All metal surfaces on probe "sanded" clean , app was uninstalled and reinstalled and still no connection. I'm hoping someone in the know gets to see this.
I keep losing the Bluetooth signal when I walk away from the BBQ. Incredibly frustrating.

review_title: A Wonderful Product but It Will NOT Maintain Connection. I DON'T RECOMMEND IT.
review_text: I've owned it for a year. I'm a skilled & experienced home cook and I understand the need to, in some situations, know what the temperature of your food is. That's why I invested in this tool and this thermometer, with the app, is a really excellent tool..... when it works. Sadly, it often just doesn't. I cooked Thanksgiving dinner today. I needed to monitor the temperature of the turkey in the convection oven and, after the bird was done, the dressing as it baked. My Meater would NOT maintain a connection no matter what I did or what I was cooking. It lost the connection repeatedly almost as soon as I closed the oven doors and it was beastly hard to get it to reconnect. My Iphone was maybe 3 feet away from the probe in the oven but that mattered not at all. It was virtually useless. I'm seriously fed up with this tool. I finally plugged in my old wired probe and was able to successfully complete my turkey breast and the dressing, but it was so frustrating to not be able to use this kitchen tool that I paid SO MUCH for. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THE MEATER.

I like this unit, but it's a lot of work, and has prompted some heavy rage. First of all, I believe I was the first one to recognize that the original instructions and marketing mentioned NOTHING about the charging unit being a CRITICAL PART of the Bluetooth broadcasting system. They fixed that. (Be sure the "charger" is close to the temperature probe at all times. If you cook outside, carry it out with you and put it near the grill!) After getting the Bluetooth to work, it took a while to get the software to cooperate. (They really REALLY want to you to "SIGN UP, LOG IN, GET AN ACCOUNT!", which I hate. I didn't buy this thing to join a club.) Next gripe; if the battery dies during a long cook (like the 14 hour brisket I did last month), you lose ALL the data for the cook, which ruins your ability to learn from the data collection, and refer back on your next cook. So....the thing works....(usually, now that the "charger" is recognized as a part of the antenna), but is it worth the price? Not so sure.

Positives: Great app. Measures internal and ambient temperature. Very sharp. Cleans easily. Negative: If you're going to advertise that the range is 165 ft, the range should be close to that. The connection starts to fail at about 10 ft. The advertisements show people monitoring the probe from a different room in the house. This is definitely not possible with this product. You need to stay right next to what you're cooking at all times. And you need to constantly check the app to make sure it's still connected. If it disconnects, there's no notification. The box needs to be very close to the probe. And your phone needs to be very close to the box. If you walk into the next room for a moment, you will get disconnected. For the price, I expected the claims about the range to be close to what they actually are. I should have checked online. There is a section of the blog that tries to help users with connection issues. There is a whole community of users who struggle with the range of this product. If the range is 10 ft, just say it's 10 ft. Don't just say it's 165 ft to get people to buy the product.

review_title: Good cooks just takes a bit to figure out
review_text: The setup seems “Apple” like with its absolute minimalist documentation. The 2nd or 3rd step is charge it for 6 hrs, with no reading ahead in the documentation. I get that it wants to be the cool or hip new device but maybe some real documentation or set the expectation that you will start then have a long wait until you finish setting up the device. There is no real explanation on how it calculates the time remaining. It seems to be accurate but no idea what or why. I think it’s great it is doing this but maybe a few words on how? The cooks have been great. How ever the ambient temperature is way off from the cook surface or dome temperature. And if you ask about this on their FB group they get really defensive and remove your questions. Other cooking groups allowed the question and actually had an ok answer to why - the Meater+ ambient temp is taken really close to the food so the temp possibly picking up the food temp as well. Other group members also recommended using a different surface/grill temp to use to repeat the cook. Over all it does a great job, it’s just odd they they want to keep most of the use and functionality a mystery for the sake of being cool. I would buy again and have recommended it to others with a heads up on what to expect.

Worked great for about a year and a half then it stopped working. It won’t read the ambient temp and it says the internal temp is at 32. Meat is fully thawed and has been out on the smoker for about an hour. Super disappointed as I’ve loved my thermometer so far. I tried resting it, and I’m running into the same issue. Huge bummer as I was a big fan.

review_title: Good luck getting it to connect
review_text: It’s great when I can get it to connect. Every time it seems like either the battery is dead or it just won’t connect. The 1/5 times I am able to connect it, it takes me forever. Over this useless metal stick.

Wonderfully simple to use and app works great. Steaks are perfectly done to desire. App is precisely tuned to get the steak how you want. Grilling is so much more joyful. Cleanup is a snap also. Update: After 2 years using it in my smoker 95% of the time I finally found a location, probe-charging port-and phone/myself where it stayed connected so play around with it especially probe and charging port locations to where you want to relaxe but in truth it could always be further.🙄 The other Con has been the size dia. of the probe itself. Its Wide and not all my fish and steaks are over an inch thick to be able to get a good center insertion Plus the Tip is far from being a sharp point making things harder. It still performs perfectly but I reduced it 2 stars for these hassles.

review_title: Not as reliable or easy to use as I had hoped
review_text: Initial setup was straight forward, up and until I tried to pair the Meater to the App. It took multiple attempts to sync up. Using the Meater is simple, as long as you can keep the Meater and its charging base VERY close (within a few ft) when using a metal smoker. Definitely needs to have the dock and the meater as close as possible when in use. As for connecting from the dock to the phone/tablet - I've found it works better when I use a tablet I can leave closer to the dock and then sync it with my phone that is upstairs in my office in order to avoid losing connectivity. As for accuracy, I've repeatedly had a "medium rare" top sirloin come out "well done", even when following all the prompts and timing from the Meater. The app does ask for feedback after each use, including accuracy, so I can only hope they're fine tuning the experience. I've used the Meater in an indoor oven setting - and it works OK on a stainless steel sauce pan in the oven, but when I used a cast iron skillet it struggled to accurately read the ambient temperature. I'm not sure why, but the steak took 3x longer than anticipated - and again came out "well done" despite a "rare" setting.

I bought one of these and it worked great for about 2 years before it broke, so I bought another that lasted another year or two, then bought a third. This one broke in just a few months. It’s always the same thing - the probe stops charging, no matter how well I clean it. I’m unfortunately going to switch back to a wired thermometer. Hoping that is more reliable.
Was too confusing to hook up for an old guy with no kids around

I had one of these when they originally came out and I had nothing but problems with it disconnecting all the time. I figured I would give this new one a shot since it's been a little while and they have some new products out and I just wanted to try something new. Well I used this on a prime rib with my offset smoker. As you can see from the picture the ambient temperature on my chamber probe is reading one temperature and the ambient temperature on the app from the meater is completely different. Thankfully I pulled my prime rib early to have it carry over longer because I wanted it medium rare. By the time I cut it it was barely still medium rare and the temperature probe was reading 133°. This thing just isn't nearly as accurate as my Inkbird products. I'll probably try it a few more times just to make sure but I'm definitely not going to waste an expensive cut of meat on this.

I had very high hopes for this product. And wanted to give it as many chances as I could to make sure that it wasn’t operator error before giving it up. But we just struggled with the connectivity to the app. When we did get a reading, it just seemed off and I felt like we had to babysit it more than I would’ve just a regular digital meat thermometer. The quality was great and it was fast and easy to read, very bright and clear when we could get a reading. For us the functionality was below average. Way more effort than we wanted to give. We didn’t get a chance to test the battery life because we gave up on it before it wore out.

Great product, before it breaks. I had mine for less than two years before the thermocouple separated from the thermowell. See the photo. It has a 1 year warranty but for over $70 for thermometer, I expected more than one or two years. I'm look for a similar product from a competitor because I believe this product should last more than 2 years.

Bombards you with ads. requires a new account and unique password to use. Not good if you just want a simple, reliable temperature reading. How would you like an advertisement to show up for A1 steak sauce because you set it to beef?
Connected easy, overall neat design. Mine runs about 10 degrees hot. Checked it. in ice water and boiling water always about +10 F and no way to calibrate it.

I went with the Meater Plus so I could monitor my cook using either my tablet or my phone. I read most of the reviews on the off branded blue tooth/wifi connected thermometers, most of those related connection issues. I seem to have one that drops connection between the probe and the extender box. Place the extender closer to the probe they said. The only way to get it closer would be to put it in the smoke box. The issue resolves by removing the back cover and placing it on the pellet hopper. The other thing I noticed is that the temperatures both the meat and the ambient start out about 25 degrees less than what my smoker indicates. The 25 degrees decreases as the meat cooks. currently its about 6 degrees off on the meat and still 25 off on the ambient. I am not sure which is more correct. I would return it, but am beyond the return window being the 2nd time I have used it.

I have had this for something like 2.5 years now and can confidently give pros and cons. pros: accurate measurements and software is easy to use. I have made some really good food on this. cons: Loses connection constantly especially if it is in a oven. example is having it in the over and losing connection while I am in the next room over which is at most 10 feet away. Poor Battery life as in if you have a long cook like a brisket it has run out of battery during cook even with it being fly charged before and had I to take it out charge and place back in.

I put this head to head against my ThermoWorks Smoke and Thermopen. I smoked a Boston Butt and had the ambient temp probe right beside the ceramic part, and the internal temp probe inside the meat close to where I had the Meater + . The Ambient temperature was way off (30 degrees less than my Smoke probe). I had prior calibrated the smoke to 32F and 212F. and it was within a degree. I verified this with a third thermometer I had as well making the Smoke the more trusted thermometer at this point. The internal temp was 5 degrees less than my Smoke Probe which is within possible error from not having the same insertion depth, different muscle, or more fat. but my thermopen was right on to the smoke, and 5 degrees higher than the Meater +. Overall I like most things about it but the ambient being off by so much when it's so important in smoking, makes me rate this no higher than 3. Other people have had good luck, so maybe I'm the odd one out, but I will not purchase this again.

No issue with battery life, versatility, or accuracy. Device functions as advertised and I find it useful. Major complaint is that until the device is in use and the meat is in the oven, you have no idea how long the cook will take. This makes planning a meal more difficult than it needs to be. Cook time is calculated using internal temperature and the ambient temperature. If the meat isn’t at “room temperature” it can take up to 30 minutes for the device to calculate the cook time.

I got this for Christmas and it worked great at first. About 6 months later, it constantly loses connection. I usually have my phone 10-15 feet away while in use . I’ve replaced the battery, still no good. It’s intermittent at best. To be fair, I have used it a lot for grilling and smoking and even once or twice in the oven. I want to try another brand, though. I feel like it should’ve lasted more than six months for the money it cost.
This device is great when it does work but it is super finicky and loses connection if the probe is any more than 5' away. Not worth $100 in my opinion

Worked well for a couple of years. Then the unit separated into two pieces. After resecuring the two portions of the unit, it has been off by 15 to 20°. Something this expensive should not fail after only two years.

review_title: If it works properly it will be a useful tool
review_text: If it worked perfectly it might be worth the price. Received it as a gift. Connection and temperature reliability have been inconsistent and therefore unreliable. I just use an instant read thermometer for accuracy.
26 days past warranty ours broke ! No promo code or anything given to buy a new one. Disappointed because we do love this product.
Bluetooth range is terrible. Move more than 30-35 feet from the cooker-thermometer and it loses the connection. Why isn’t it hooked via wifi? Update - just threw it in the trash!
Constant connection issues even when the devices are less than a foot away
Great when it works. Terrible when it doesn’t. I’ve only had it for a year and it constantly disconnects from the Meater probe, or from the phone unless the phone is within 15 feet of the probe.
I have to be within 10ft. to connect to it. The range is too short. It works great, but connection is terrible.

The temp seems to be somewhat accurate , but the distance between the thermometer and your phone is very short. If I am in my house and the smoker is in the backyard, it’ll disconnect and reconnect probably 30-40 times during an all day smoke. Very annoying.

Expensive device with less than desirable results. Grilled three steaks; all were 2.5 inches thick and the steak with the neatest device turned out rare and we set it for medium rare. Could have gotten better results with a $15 instant thermometer.

This worked well for almost 2 years and then the probe fell apart when it was removed from some ribs we were grilling. Update - after we shared this information with the manufacturer's customer service, they gave us a nice discount to buy a replacement probe.

review_title: Works if you plan to stay nearby

I loved the Meater+ and have used it for a few years now. I always had connection issues and just recently the sleeve came off of the probe and it won’t connect at all. I assume the probe is done for. These are kind of an expensive for how many issues I had with it and then for this to happen now. A little disappointing

review_title: Works but ambient oven temperature reading is wrong.
review_text: I've had this thermometer for a while. It works as advertized however I have two problems: 1) The battery discharges while not in use 2) The meat probe temp is fine, but the ambient temperature reading is wrong. It reads a hundred degrees too low or more.
Lost connection regularly and the ceramic part of the probe cannot handle high heat (causing the alarm to go off). Wanted to like it, but too many issues to recommend.

review_title: Clingy little baby of a thermometer
review_text: Can’t walk away….like at all. Specs say 165’ but mine will disconnect when I go more than 20’. Which I think kind of defeats the purpose. Seems to be accurate and was easy to set up but HUGELY disappointing that I have to keep my phone no more than 20’ away from the probe while in service. It’s too late to return but this is not the intended use.

Smoked brisket with thermopro tp25, big green egg wireless thermometer and meater +. Meater + reads 10°f low and ambient temp 23°f low. The other 2 probes are spot on. Test calibration with boiling water at sea level and read 203°f. Keeps loosing connection. I don't recommend.

The estimated cooking timer in the app can take a very long time to load which is frustrating (sometimes over an hour). Also have noticed the temp reading off by 5-10 degrees at times. The magnet on the home base is convenient as long as it’s not close to the heat source. Wouldn’t buy again for the price.
Range is limited indoors and it seems to drop Wi-Fi sometimes, not always.

review_title: Works ok but broke after a few years
review_text: Works pretty well but I've had mine 3 years and it's coming apart. Not sure if I will be re purchasing.
tried it several times... got a cheaper one that works better honestly

review_title: Wonderful, but on my 3rd one now and I'm sure I'll have to buy again
review_text: Due to my meat-based diet, I use my Meater probe and iPhone App almost daily, often twice a day. Its easily seen hundreds of cooks on my grill, in my smoker and in my oven. My thoughts: Pros: - Good quality. Durable and has held-up to hundreds of grilling sessions. I've actually over-heated it a few times and it still works great. - Great App on my iPhone. Free, well designed, bug-free and very easy to use. Supports the use of multiple Meater probes simultaneously. Will warn you (loudly) if the external portion of probe gets too hot. - Fairly good accuracy at calculating cook times and when to remove meat from the heat source to achieve desired temp. - Solid bluetooth connectivity. Good engineering and software development has made this very solid. - Long battery life in the charging unit on a single AAA battery. - Fair price. Cons: - After a few cooks, the ambient end (square-end) of the Meater probe gets dirty and baked-on grease or smoke which can prevent the probe from charging properly. You have to keep an eye on it, and scrub it clean to ensure a good charging surface. Scotch-brite or sand paper do a good job. - From time-to-time, the Meater probe and charging station won't sync-up right away, but will about half-way into the cook. I'm not sure what causes this, but it happens every so often. Minor annoyance. - My biggest con is that these probes seem to fail over time. I'm on my 3rd Meater probe now and I'm certain I'll be buying another one a year from now. They just wear-out over time and I'm not sure why. The fact that these wear-out over time, but I keep purchasing them should be testament to how well these work and how much I like them. I'd recommend it.

review_title: Great instrument - I was able to sit in the next room and watch the temps on my steak
review_text: I have always wanted to try cooking a steak in the oven first and then doing a reverse sear on the grill. This instrument made that very possible. I set it to 125 (for a rare steak, it turned out medium). Cooking it at 250 worked as the recipe indicated, kept the juice inside and them temp was uniformed through out the steak. What this instument taught me is how much a steaks temp rises while its resting, out of the oven the temp went from 125 to 132 sitting on my counter. By that time the grill was ready (remove the Meater before searing the steak) 2 minutes on each side was enough to make the steak medium inside. I learned alot with this instrument and look forward to Saturdays steak. I gave it 4 stars because I would have liked to be able to make custom alerts so based on temps reached.

Mostly awesome but two flaws. When this thermometer works, it is simply amazing. The app shows super useful information. It really is a game changer for cooking meat properly. However, there are two flaws: (1) there is no battery level indicator. Nothing more frustrating than going for the cook to find out mid-cook that your battery is dead. It would be great if there was some level indicator on the block itself. The only solution I have to this is to change the battery on a set schedule, which isn’t optimal because I throw away batteries that may still be good. The second problem (2) is that the connection is hit or miss. There has to be a better way to show connection to your phone. As it stands now, you open the app, remove the thermometer from its base…and hope. Most of the time it connects quickly sometimes it doesn’t. WHY? It’s so frustrating. Every time I have the thermometer and base right next to my phone. With all that being said, once it is working with sufficient charge, it’s awesome and a game changer. They could improve it though.

Got this probe as a Father’s Day gift and it has been the best one I’ve owned so far. I’m nine hours in to a cook and the battery is still nearly full. Easy set up, easy use. Only setback is you have to keep the base fairly close to the probe or it will constantly disconnect, and that is not that big of a deal. The base is magnetic so I can keep them on the fridge when not in use, and the wooden design is fairly decorative and not an eye sore. All in all I highly recommend.
So far, so good. Haven’t used it in cooking yet, but charging and setting up with the app was a snap!
It loses connection if you're not real careful. Other than that it's pretty good
Temp appears to be on point. Worked well on my chickens.
Bluetooth connectivity requires phone and transmitter to be in close proximity

Cooks the meat perfectly….from steaks to briskets

Our last Meater+ died on us and was not accurately reading temperatures, but we had it for about three-ish years, hence the four stars, but otherwise, we love it. My brother's did the exact same thing. We just tossed it and bought another. I appreciate the accuracy of this thermometer. It is water/liquid resistant. It's small and you can take it anywhere. Love this product, just wish it lasted longer.

Be sure it is in the fattest part of the meat or it may not cook properly. Mine stopped working so I watched a Youtube video which told me to wash the end in soapy water and dry. That did get it going again.

review_title: Outstanding Once Set Up But Why Not Rechargeable?!
review_text: This thing is GREAT once it’s set up. The app is outstanding, super helpful, love that it estimates cooking time and is really helpful with knowing whether your cooking equipment temps are accurate (via “ambient temperature” feature). The app has lots of great features and the device and charging dock design is sleek, compact, and very easy to use once it is set up…. I am not giving it 5 stars because: setup was dramatic (and I live with a computer engineer…who was also annoyed by it) AND why are we using a regular AA battery to “recharge” the device vs just making the charging dock USB-C or something. Also, there is no indicator on the charging dock or device that lets you know when it’s fully charged (or charging) - gotta have the app. I need to mess with the notifications and sounds more because the default is SUPER annoying (like literally every 30 seconds). Make sure you open the package and charge it BEFORE you need to use it for the first time (not at the exact time your Christmas roast needs to go into the oven…).

review_title: Would be five stars but not being able to tell if it's charging or not is terrible!
review_text: Bought this a week ago. Used it straight out of the box and it worked great cooking a pork shoulder on my Weber Master Touch. Love that it tells you both the temperature of the meat and the ambient temperature but the best feature you get with this Meater+ is the software! The software basically cooks the meat for you. You set a desired temperature end goal and the software does everything else. The Meater app tells you when to pull the meat from the grill and how long to rest it to get the meat to the desired internal temperature through carry over cooking. Fantastic! Now to the bad. You have no way of knowing if the probe is charging. You can press the button on the front of the Meater+ block and see that the battery in the block has power but no way to tell if the probe is actually charging. I completed my pork shoulder last weekend, washed the probe after use, making sure to scrub the ambient end with the scouring pad side of a dish sponge like the paperwork says and placed it in the block to charge until I used it again. Perfect experience. Get another pork shoulder prepped and ready to go today, pull out the Meater+, excited to use it, and the Meater app shows me my probe has no charge. The probe had enough battery to connect to the phone for five mins but completely died afterwards. I am now very frustrated and sweating as SouthEast Georgia is 95 degrees today and I'm standing in front of a hot grill trying to get a $100 meat probe to do it's job. I go in the house, grab my trusty, rusty ThermoPro and get it all going. I then scour the internet to find that apparently I did not scrub the ambient end of the probe well enough to get the thinnest layer of carbon you could possibly imagine off of it in order for it to charge. The ambient end of the probe was aluminum colored, did not have an oily sheen or feel, and definitely was devoid of food particles. I assumed it was clean. It was not. When cooking on charcoal, the smoke leaves behind a layer of carbon that I had to lightly scrape off with a razor blade. Touché, Meater+. I appreciate you for your initial great experience and fantastic software but I hate you for the fickleness of having to be scraped with a razor blade in order for your block to charge your probe. Touché.

Very handy tool for grilling or baking various meats. Easy to use phone app that has recommended preset temperatures for all types of meat and fish. Also allows you to customize your temperature settings. The only thing you need to know is that it doesn’t conduct heat not accurately predict “remaining time until done”. As an example it might say you have 1.5 hours left until done even though you know that can’t be right. I’ve cooked a small turkey breast or pork loin many times in the oven at 350 and know it takes 45 minutes to an hour. The longer it cooks the Meater starters reducing its estimate quicker than the elapsed time so it always ends up close to what I expected. In others words you need to have a rough idea as to how long your item will take before trusting the estimate. But the temperature of the meat is always displayed on your phone with no wires which is very handy. The app also has a ton of great recipes for all sorts of meats and fish for baking or grilling.

review_title: Not ready to give up my wired thermometers; close but not quite!
review_text: Update (2/3/2020). I've had this for a while and still really like it. I had problems with not being able to charge it, but it was the back end of probe getting covered in "stuff". I used a sharpening stone and rubbed it a few times and it's back to new. I try to keep it flat on the stone so that it stays even. (btw, if you don't have a good real stone, you should get one. I'm using one that's been in the family for at least 50 years.) old review stuff: Just to give a little background. I barbecue at least once per week. I prep meals for my large family using both a offset smoker and a Weber Kettle Grill (22"). My primary cook is the Kettle. I will general cook tritip, chicken, or fish. I purchased the meater+ to replace my old dual probe Maverick (a great thermometer btw but hard to set up right). The first thing I noticed is that the probe range is greatly reduced by placing it into the kettle. That bit of info is pretty clearly stated and is the reason I purchased the Meater+. The Meater+ charging block serves as a Bluetooth repeater. I placed the charging box (which has magnets) near my kettle and this greatly extended the range. For me, the charging block/repeater needed to be within 3-4 feet of the kettle to get a stable connection. To connect to the WiFi, you need a second device connected to your Meater probe. Once you do that, the range is basically unlimited. I hope this little chart makes sense. Probe--3ft--> Block --10to20ft-->Device1-->WiFi-Internet-->Device2 The main limitation of the probe is its low temperature range. I think my Maverick goes up to 700F for both probes. The meater can only handle about 212F (boiling) for the internal probe. That's a little low. I think given time, I will screw up on a longer cook and end up exceeding that limit. The external temperature is a fairly respectable 527 F. However, this means you should not put it directly over charcoal. If you are going to seer your meat over a high flame, I would recommend that you stick the probe in after you do that. Because all of the electronics are in the probe, the probe must be inserted 2.5" into the meat. For roasts, large pieces of fish (salmon fillets for example), or large chicken breasts, this is pretty easy to do. I would not recommend this for small stuff. This is the primary advantage of wired probes. As long as the tip of the probe is in the meat, it doens't really matter where the rest is. There are very strong positive and negatives for this product. Positive - Great software interface, convenient, works great within its limitations Negative - Poor connection range, low internal temperature limit. Thermometer not suited for smaller pieces of meat (less than 5").

review_title: Updated: Need to understand the limits...
review_text: UPDATE: I finally figured out how to make this my go to thermometer for grilling. Lesson 1: Buy really good, strong batteries like the lithium duracell/energizers. Since it's a single AAA battery, the more power you can give it to charge the better. After clean up from a cook, make sure you double check that the battery and most importantly the probe are well seated in their slots. If the probe is not fully seated, it will not have a charge when it's time to cook. Watch the little light, if it's red when the probe is seated, the battery has no charge left. Lesson 2: to get maximum range to your phone you have to experiment with placement of the dock. The dock is a bluetooth repeater so place the dock at the midpoint between the grill and your phone. I have enough confidence in the Meater now that i bought the 4 probe version too. This works well when cooking roasts or briskets. I can monitor the temperature in the point and the flat to let me know when to rotate the roast for a more even cook. Old review is below: I have owned a Meater+ for over a year. It has much potential, the concept is good, the application is good, the interface is easy to use, however the Meater+ continues to fail at basic functionality. Numerous times, I have started a cook only to find that the device has no charge. I continously put in NEW duracell or energizer alkaline batteries and the device is DEAD when i need to use it. The basics are like this... Put a new, strong battery, AAA, in the base. Make sure the Meater+ probe is securely positioned in the base. Put the device away and the probe should be fully charged when you need it, right? Nope. So many times, I have tried to use the Meater+ and it's dead... When it works, it's awesome, but that is not always when you need it. For the bluetooth range of 165 ft, maybe it has that range in a flat, unplanted farm field. My house is brick and my kamado and weber kettle grills are ~40ft from the kitchen, with careful placement of the charger and my phone, I can get the signal connected, but the range is no where near 165ft. The product concept really shine with rotisserie grilling. No wires is the only way to go. I am researching other options/products, because i grill often and this product is nice to have in mix. As for the Meater+, my opinion is to not waste your time or your money on this product.

review_text: Second Edit: I used it again and after a shaky start, worked through a whole 4 hour cook time. The next time I tried to use it, the probe wouldn't pair with the base. Eventually gave up. You just can't count on it. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Edit: One hour into my second use, the probe lost contact with the Meater + and wont connect now 1 hour into a 12 hour cook. Nothing moved, the base was 15 feet away from the probe, and my phone was 20 feet away from my base. After I got the disconnect notice, I moved the base closer to the probe, but it won't reconnect. I could pull it out of the meat, clean it, put it in the base and try to reconnect, but I have a second wired probe in the meat I am already tired of screwing with this. It would be a really cool product if it worked, but it hasn't worked correctly two times in my first two uses. I wish I hadn't bought it. ----------------------------------- Got my Mater+ a few days ago, got it charged, downloaded the app, and got it paired and everything working. Perfect. I wanted to have it before cooking Christmas Eve prime roast. Fired up the app today, got the probe out of the Meater, and I couldn't get the probe to communicate with the base. I messed around with it for about 20 minutes, and got the whole chain communicating. Put the roast in the oven, and got it cooking. Then about 25 minutes into the cook, the probe stopped communicating again. The base was no more than 4 feet away from the probe. The only instructions were to move the base closer to the probe. I updated the base software, and came to a point in the cook where I could take the probe out of the meat. I cleaned it off, put it back into the base, took it out, and it started working. I put it back into the roast, and it continued to work for the last 1:30 of the cook. It was actually really helpful. I like this product, but it scares me that it was so temperamental when it was brand new.

review_title: Perfect complement to roasting larger pieces of meat; cumbersome for individual meal cooks
review_text: I was a dedicated Weber iGrill user for many years and was waiting for the day when someone would invent a decent wireless probe. The Meater is a terrific product, combining internal temperature and ambient temperature in one wireless probe. A couple items of note: 1) You need to make sure you set up the Meater probe and open the app EXACTLY in the order in which the directions say. You can't open the app first and then put the probe in the meat. You won't get a connection. You need to put the probe in the meat first, determine you have a good connection, and THEN open the app. Not sure why this is so important to functionality, but I'm glad I discovered this before my first cook. 2) The Meater probe has more girth than other wired probes, and before you break out the high school humor, here's why that matters: For individual cuts of meat that are an inch thick or less (like if you're grilling for yourself), it's challenging to ensure you've inserted the probe in the center for an accurate temperature reading. This means you also have to watch that the ambient end of the probe isn't angled too much where it might touch the grill grates. 3) The Meater probe has a minimum insertion depth, and before you break out the high school jokes again, here's why that matters: in order to insulate the transmitter inside the probe from getting too hot, you need to insert the probe at least 3 inches into the meat. For smaller cuts of meat, this can pose a challenge. 4) The Meater transmitter box needs to be within 10 feet of the probe for it to work, which is fine, but the box isn't weatherproof. So if your grill area doesn't have a covered space for the transmitter box, you'll need to put it in a container with a lid if you plan to cook in the elements such as rain or snow. 5) The Meater app is super easy to install and navigate once you get your meat on the grill. It gives excellent visual representations for internal temp, target temp and ambient temp. 6) Do NOT put the Meater probe in the dishwasher. It's super easy to clean and takes 15 seconds to wash, dry and put back in the transmitter box to charge. The transmitter box is magnetic, so it sticks to the fridge or grill. Overall--great product, and I highly recommend it.

review_title: Meater+  is a fine wireless thermometer
review_text: I've only used this on 2 cooks so far; a rotisserie port roast and for some reverse sear steaks. I did remove the Meater prior to searing as it was going over an 1800 degree infrared burner and I didn't want to risk damaging the ambient sensor. The meat probe was accurate but the ambient never came up to the actual. As reported this is likely due to the ambient probe being close to the meat. The app was easy to use and works as expected, though they need to update their videos or you may not be certain if you are connected or how you are connected (bluetooth or wifi). If you have spare device you can run the app on, I would recommend purchasing the Meater and not the Meater+ and use one device as the wifi repeater and a 2nd to monitor the cook. Unless you are outside or have minimal barriers between the base unit, bluetooth is just too unreliable. With the wifi I can hang out in my basement and monitor everything with no issues. Even the extended bluetooth would not allow for this. The app is actually pretty decent with all the features you would expect. I have it installed on 3 Android devices including a Kindle Fire that I installed the Google Store on. It also appears to be available on the Amazon app store. Pros: -Wireless thermometer with bluetooth, wifi (with a 2nd device running the app) , and cloud (2nd device running app) -Accurate meat probe -App is easy to use and widely available Cons: May not be able to depend on the ambient sensor depending on how the Meater is inserted Not really a con, but their documentation video's need to be updated to reflect the changes to the app Max temp on ambient sensor, may not allow for using the Meater during searing I may revisit this after I've had a chance to use it over the next few months. Right now I would recommend it. Updated 9/6:/2020 Used it on baby brisket (2lb) in the Kamado. Worked great,ambient sensor seemed accurate. Apparently ambient accuracy is an issue with larger cuts of meat. The bluetooth signal became very spotty once it was wrapped in foil. The Meater was entirely covered. Perhaps wrapping and leaving a hole for the thermometer would work better.

review_title: A bit pricey but delivers consistently great results.
review_text: I bought a pellet grill recently and felt like trying out a wireless probe to compliment the wired probe that came with the unit. The meater app is really useful for taking the guess work out of safe cooking temperatures for different kinds of meat. The app also lets you know when to take off the heat in order to reach temperature without overcooking. The estimated cook times are also a handy addition. I think for the price it might not be the most economical choice, an instant read thermometer and a little vigilance would save you about 50 bucks, but you can't deny that this is a quality wifi thermometer. Update - I took off a star because the bluetooth range is short and inconsistent. Which is fine if you plan to stay near the grill or use a second device to transmit through wifi.

review_title: Greatly convenient, but you need to know a few things to use it
review_text: This thermometer has greatly simplified my life allowing to cook very good steaks. Predominantly I use it to grill beef steaks like rib-eye, striploin and tenderloin. You can adjust to using it but it is better if you know these tricks: 1. Put the base very close to the grill. Better somewhere on the grill where it is not very hot. If you bring the base 20 ft. or so away, it starts losing the connection. You, with your smartphone can be much further, the app will tell you if it is disconnected from the base. 2. Set the target temperature a lot lower that you want. In general, the thicker is the cut, the lower should be the target comparing to what's the real temperature you want to achieve. For example, for a standard 1.5 inch steak, if you want 135°, set it to 125°. It tells you to remove it from the heat 5 degrees below that target but still while you wait for it to cool down, the temperature may go 10° or even 15° above your target. A very thin steak may be OK with the exact temperature, but 2" cut will need a big adjustment, or you will overcook it. I wish I could be able to enter the depth of steak into app and it would adjust. 3. Insert the probe all the way down till the beginning of the black tip. If you leave an inch or so of the silver part out you may start getting "close to overheat" and "overheat" messages, which are very annoying and also covering the entire screen so you can't see anything. I have a low-power grill and it also has an infra-red bar, so there is no open flame, but still it does that. Nothing bad really happens, the probe is fine and working, it's just an annoying paranoic mode. 4. Always clean the back of the tip of the probe before recharging, or you may end up with "low battery" right before you need it. That's a contact part and it gets greasy. Use a very fine sand paper to polish it when needed. So, yes, it is useful, I like it and my steaks improved a lot since I don't open the grill too many times, only when need to turn the steaks over. But there is a space for improvement.

review_title: A nice improvement from earlier temperature probes.
review_text: The most attractive feature of this probe is the combined internal and ambient temperature sensor in the same probe device via Bluetooth. All the previous systems had separate probes for internal and ambient and use a separate device for remote monitoring. It is very nice to have a single probe that is monitored from ones phone. We have done several cooks with the device and we have had good results. The finish temperature seems to be very accurate. The ambient temperature measurements seem to be correct as well. This is very important for smoking foods. Smoker and grill temperature gauges are notoriously inaccurate and cooking temperature is very important. As several other reviewers have commented, we have noted projected cooking times are not accurate. This is not that big of an issue as most of the foods we prepare we have done for many years and have a good sense of the cook time based on the ambient temp and weight of the meat being cooked. The other issue are occasional connection issue. We have also had some confusion with keeping the probe and range extender matched when using more than one probe. The last observation, comment would be regarding the cloud functionality. In practice not really very practical as you have to have two phones loaded with the Meater app and one has to remain at home in order to monitor the cook when away from your home or out of Bluetooth range.

I was highly skeptical but I must say this things work extremely well. It is a bit annoying that the connection drops if you go too far way from the antenna but for me is not a big issue once I know it, given that my kitchen is not far from the BBQ. The temperature is spot-on, as compared to a Thermapen. You can set the target temperature (including choosing from many predefined options by type of meat, cut, desired fondness, type of cooking). Two features I like a lot: 1) the expected remaining time, available a few minutes after start, is a great feature for planning a meal; 2) The temp graph, showing how the internal and ambient temperatures progress (so you can quickly see if there is a problem, like burners off). The only thing I don’t like (apart from the bluetooth limitation) is the choice of material for the case/repeater. This is wood/bamboo: it looks nice but will get dirty very soon in a cooking area (that’s why 4 and not 5 stars).

>>>>>>>>>>>> UPDATE: Changing from a 1 star to a 4 star. Customer service surprisingly reached out again with return shipping labels (and no explanation). I followed the instructions and returned it, thankfully it was not in the trash yet. New one arrived today, seemed to connect just fine, temp guage appears to be working. Wish customer service had just gone this rout to begin with, but grateful they reached out. I may have just had a faulty one, but time will tell, and I may change to a 5 star if all keeps working great. >>>>>>>>>>>>>>> For starters, I typically don't write too many reviews unless the product and their customer service disappoint. When you finally get the probe to connect to the app (which is 50/50), and you wait forever for it to calculate its cook time, the temperature sensor works half the time. When compared to a wired Guage, the meater is always about 10 degrees off.. which is quite substantial. Contact customer service and they find some excuse to not honor the warranty... "your ambient temperature was above 500 degrees farenheit at some point, so we can't help you" firstly what piece of junk can't withstand high temperatures when that is its sole purpose, secondly, if I were cooking my steak at 500 degrees, I wouldn't need a temp guage... i'd just wait for the black smoke... Do not buy, despite the excessive social.media campaigns.

review_title: Amazing, must have device, with a serious flaw that could be fixed.
review_text: I have owned this device for three years and it has exceed my expectations in cook after cook, whether in be BBQing or oven cooking, and I have used it with a wide variety of meats. Somehow, it just "KNOWS" when to take your project off the grill or oven at the exact time to then let it rest. I have NEVER had anything less that a great outcome when using the Meater. My complaint is this, and why it is only 4 stars instead of 5: The range of the device via Bluetooth is utterly lacking. The basic idea, is that the Meater connects to it's "base" (the wooden holder) and then connects to your phone/tablet, etc. But, as said, the range is pathetic. The whole idea is to monitor your cook from afar, and not have be doting over it within physical close proximity. There is one version of Meater that offers WiFi connectivity but it is a four probe set and very expensive. The ideal Meater would be a single probe (maybe two), that interfaces with your household WiFi so that range is no longer an issue. But it still deserves four stars on account of it being an EXCELLENT tool in any amateur chef's toolbox.

The Meater+ performs exactly as advertised and deserves 5 stars. It’s simple to set up, intuitive to use and gives you exactly what you need - remote reading of internal temperature of your cook. The app on the other hand is supposed to help with cooks and when to “remove from heat” and how long to rest. Sadly this is not always accurate and needed a learning curve on my end to get close to my results. First off I stopped using the Meater for fast and hot cooks. The app just seems unreliable in timing calculation and alerts here. I believe it comes from the device reading temp in the grill but not from the grate. For low and slow the app helps much more but actually thinks that when I remove a 12lb brisket from a 225° smoker after 11.5 hours, that the internal temp will rise another 5°. No sir. So here I am just ignoring that alarm and letting it smoke until it hits the right temp. Also the app told me to rest my above mentioned brisket for 5 minutes. I laughed about it and let it rest an hour. To conclude, I make it sound like those are arguments against buying the Meater. No, get one! It is an amazing device that improved my cooking greatly. There's just a few things to consider that wouldn’t come to your mind if you use no thermostat or one without an app.

review_title: Well made, accurate, but a little pricy
review_text: My previous digital thermometer broke so I stumped up the bucks for a wireless model. My small oven will not work with the door unlatched so cannot run a wire. Out of the box the thing seams to be very good quality, stainless steel and strong magnets on the Wooden case / Bluetooth repeater. The good, it’s appears very accurate, I’ve done a rib eye roast and a pork fillet both cooked to a perfect medium rare. The cooking / resting times were very accurate and the app is Super simple to use. The not so good: (all pretty minor) It took a bit of faffing around to position the Bluetooth repeater on the outside of the oven, so it is aligned with antenna in the probe so the signal doesn’t drop out. I’ve not tried it with a joint rotating in the oven but believe there could be connectivity issues, should be able to work it out though- the documentation appears a bit limited on this. Is the antenna linear or circular polarised, is there a preferred alignment etc etc the probe is double the diameter of a normal wired thermocouple probe not an issue for large joints or chickens etc but it left a big hole in the middle a pork tenderloin (having said that I don’t really need a thermometer for pork tenderloin after searing on the stove it’s 10mins at 170’C in my oven to slightly pink and juicy) I mainly got this for reverse searing large joints and the BBQ. Not had it Long enough to comment on reliability / longevity of the device but yes I would definitely recommend it, even though it’s triple the price or more that of a good quality wired thermometer.

The description sounded interesting so I decided to get it and see how it worked. The unit requires one AAA Battery in the back to provide the power for the Bluetooth connectivity. pairing to the phone was simple and painless. The distance for the Bluetooth is more than adequate to connect to my phone and progress being immediately displayed for me, lets me know when it is time to start the sides. The Meater app is easy to download and works fantastic. It is not a put it on and done, scenario for meat that needs to be flipped but based off the temp, you know exactly when you half way to the desired temperature, and flip it then for the perfect cook. I was impressed with the performance of the Meater on the first cook. We did a pork roast and it came out of the grill perfection. after that, we did a cookout with family and did New York Strip on the grill, and again, cooked to perfection. On the 2nd cook we had multiple steaks and needed to be able to cook them to different temperatures as some like theirs Rare and other's Medium Rare so we decided to invest into the Meater Block as it will give us the ability to manage 4 different steaks to different exact temperatures and a fifth with our original purchase.

review_title: Not recommended for charcoal users - Great app, accurate internal temp, poor ambient reading
review_text: As a UDS/charcoal user w/o a thermostat like on a Traeger, I am compelled to know what my smoker's ambient temp is to make sure it's not getting too hot or too cool due to whatever variables. The disparity on the ambient temp is just way too large. For example: I am early into smoking a turkey breast roast as I type this up (and I did a chicken last weekend with similar results): my two other probe systems show the ambient temp is 252/253F, but the Meater+ is showing 196F. If I saw 196F on my regular probe, I'd be going out there stoking the fire or seeing if one of the kids closed the damper on me. "Well are the probes near each other?" Admittedly not as close today, but on the chicken the probes were all nearly touching at the same point for about an hour and consistently showed about a 50F difference until towards the end. It's a reluctant deal-breaker for me, but maybe not for you. The internal temp is spot-on, it has a fantastic app, and I get really good range on it w/my Android device. How good? I have the repeater on a window sill by my back patio where the smoker is. I can go upstairs w/o issues, but I lose signal if I go out the front door. I love the charting, the cook completion estimate (though this takes a while to kick in and fluctuates greatly based on temp rise), how easy it is to clean and charge... it has so much going on for it!

It really can't take the heat. The max is 600 degrees F. My grill gets hotter than that and I like high heat to cook my chicken and steak. You do your way, but mine works for me. Fast high heat is the way I go. The probe can't take high heat and the app warns you with a LOUD alarm when you get close to the max. I have to pop the lid and it cooks unevenly. If I monitor the temperature carefully, it works fine, but that's not how I roll and the result is not as good in my humble amateur chef's opinion. If that works for you, great. It pairs up with my bluetooth easy. That's nice. The app talks to the box/charger the probe comes in, so you do have to keep the box close to the probe. That was a surprise.

review_title: Too much forced hand holding, but works

(They'll tell you it's required for Bluetooth, but I got a working connection without it and only had to suffer the app constantly notifying me it was needed.) I cannot use it without various notifications on and associated with their sounds. All I want is to be able to check the temperature. I think all the "helpful" settings and features are great for many people. Not being able to use it the way*I* want to use it (minimalist mode) is annoying. I'll use it.. sometimes.. But not as often as if it wasn't annoying. And, I certainly won't recommend it to people who enjoy cooking. Edit: I added a star. I used this for Christmas rib roast in the oven, and for roasting chicken in a Kamado grill. It did very well. I think I can make this work. Oh, I also used it to reheat a partially frozen lasagna. I am actually pleased with this device.

review_title: Awesome! Could use a feature update though.
review_text: Love this thing! The only reason why I didn't give it five stars is because I noticed today when smoking some chicken breast that it doesn't give you the ability to modify the target temperature while you're doing a cook. For example, I wanted the smoker at 225° until the internal got to 135°. Then, I turned the smoker up to 400° to crisp the skin until the internal reached 165°. In order to adjust the target temperature to 165° from 135° and alert me, I had to cancel the cook and start a new cook with a new target temperature of 165°.

The MEATER Plus is easy to set up and takes the guesswork out of cooking meat. I’ve used it while smoking steaks, chicken, and other meats, and the wireless app makes it convenient to monitor both the internal meat temperature and the ambient cooking temperature without constantly opening the grill. The guided cooking feature and estimated completion time are also helpful. The connection range can occasionally vary depending on walls and grill placement, but overall, it’s a reliable and convenient thermometer that helps produce consistent results.

I’m an avid griller/meat smoker. I had tried some competitors products and they don’t come close to this product. It even gives you recipes through the app. Accuracy is amazing as long as you place it correctly (it gives you tips in app). The usefulness for those who grill (<500degrees) or smoke meat is invaluable. Overall, an incredible value.

I was skeptical about buying one of these things; it is a lot of money for a thermometer. I have purchased so many of these wireless thermometers, and they are all pretty much junk, so investing this much took a minute. My sons' father in law actually has one, and my son had mentioned how much he loves his, so I took a chance. It is also worth noting that his father in law drinks a lot while cooking; and still has great success with it. I'm so glad I got this. I cook a lot for my ministry, and have used it five or six times, in several settings and situations; each time I have been very pleased with the results. In the oven, the smoker, grill... doesn't matter. I did run into one hick-up after using it on the smoker. The blunt end of the probe had gotten smoke residue on it, and I did not get it all off when cleaning it. The probe did not charge, and the next time I went to use it, it was dead... Even a little grease on it will prevent it from recharging. Fortunately, the app has a very good trouble shooting section, and cleared up the issue very quickly. Not only that, but after 15 minutes of charging, the probe was not fully charged, but charged enough to use it for what I was cooking. It is also important to make sure the probe is not pushed into the meat too far; it will give a faulty reading for the ambient temperature of the cooking environment. The meat temp will still be fine, but it affects the estimated cook time. Other than that, the app is awesome, very easy to install on my smart phone, and very easy to use... effortless. If you are on the fence over this thing, get one. I would rather spend $100 for a great thermometer that actually works, than spend $40 on one that ruins half of what I cook... food is too expensive, and too much is resting on my performance, to take the risk... Buy one; you won't regret it. God bless you, and your cooking efforts!

The Good: The design is slick and well thought out. The app for the Meater works well and the accuracy is spot on. A green light flashes on the base if the thermoprobe is within range and connected. It flashes red if not. The app will tell you as well if you are connected. The base station will give you considerable more range than advertised, but see the next section for the caveats. The app also has settings to change the different alerts. You can only choose from their list of sounds which is considerably less than the full array you have on the iPhone, but still, there are four alarms and maybe 12 or so sounds to choose from. No need for too many. The initial settings were just fine for me. They have just updated the app to add all sorts of carnivorous delights you can cook with the probe. From venison to kangaroo. This is a nice addition as I often go in for antelope and other less common meats. The Bad: The instructions leave a little to be desired, but it is not hard to figure out unless you are the easily frustrated type. There is a card in the box for support and the website has support as well. The Meater + comes with a bamboo magnetic base for charging and storage and in the back it has a repeater to get to the 165' range it touts. The base (and I assume the basic Meater) must be within 33' of the base for ovens and some types of grills. For smokers it is much closer. That number is in the fine print. In the case of the Orion Cooker I have, I can get the base station to recognize the thermoprobe about 12' away, through the smoker and the window to the breakfast nook. The base station has to stay there so it can connect to the probe. Once connected the app can pick up the base station, and thus the probe) all over my house and considerably farther away than 165'. But if someone moves the base it might disconnect and then you won't get updates or alarms and you might overcook your meat. The Ugly There isn't much wrong with this unit and I do recommend it to others. That said, it is a bit misleading (or just obtuse writing) which will lead you to believe that you can just plop the probe in some meat and your phone will pick it up all over the house. I read several reviews (and one YouTube video) that slammed the Meater for the short range despite the fact it is in the literature and on their site. It is probably not as prominent as it should be, but think about it, how can a little probe hold a battery, two thermoresitors, and an antennae and get 165' range? Not with today's tech I fear. Maybe when the Federation is founded. Either way, if they were a bit clearer about that for the Meater and instructions to first remove the probe before using the app. My guess is those who had issues already had the app open and so the probe paired with the phone and they didn't get the range they desired. Some Pointers If you turn on the app then remove the probe, the probe will connect to the app/phone and your range is now 33' (10' for a smoker). What is not said is that you have to fully exit and quit the app (swipe up on Apple), then remove the probe which causes it to pair with the base. Then open the app and your phone will pair with the base. Place the base where it is still flashing green when the probe is in the meat and the lid shut. Now you can use it all over the place. The app will show if it is connected properly and if it is not. I didn't notice where an alarm would sound if the base and probe stop syncing. If it doesn't have one that would be a nice addition. A nice loud one that vibrates as well. Wish list They make a basic Meater with four probes, which is a great idea if you are smoking different meats at the same time, or maybe just using the smoker, the grill, and the oven at the same time. I wish they had something like that for the Meater +. I assume it will come out at some point. Then again, I rarely would need more than one as I'm not running a restaurant. Also, I wish the magnets on the back were a bit stronger. For some reason my fridge it will slip down a few inches before attracting to some metal large enough for it to grab onto. Other kitchen items like the pot rack and microwave side have the same issues. I just think the weight of the base, battery, and probe are too much for the magnets to support. Bottom line, great unit, does what it says (even if you didn't read all it says). Just remember to remove the probe from the base first before opening the app or your range will be that of the basic Meater.
