review_title: Love the Meater Plus. Accurate, versatile, great range, easy to use.
review_text: My husband bought me the original Meater for Christmas a few years ago, and I returned it since the range was poor and it didn't work inside most of my appliance. I have since bought the Meater Plus and I love it. Although some of my appliance have built in probes, some of them don't. Although I do have an Instant Read probe that I still use to verify doneness of proteins, the Meater Plus is so much easier to use and you don't have to constantly check the food so it doesn't get over or undercooked. I am an experienced cook, but as you know foods can look done on the outside, but you can't see how well done they are on the inside. This Meater Plus is the perfect solution for perfectly cooked proteins and other foods. So what do I love about the Meater Plus? 1 - It works using an app that can be downloaded for either phones or tablets using Android or IOS operating systems. 2 - It easily connects using Bluetooth and the Meater cloud through your router. 3 - In the app settings, you can set your preferences for the various alarms. 4 - When a done temperature preference is set in the app for a cook, the app will let you know when the food is done, and allow for a resting period when the temperature will increase. So, for example, if you want a medium rare steak and set the temperature for 130 degrees, the app will tell you the steak is done at 125 degrees and allow for a 5 minute resting period that the temperature will increase to 130 degrees. This means perfectly done proteins every time. 5 - You can choose a preset in the app, and then modify it to your preference. 6 - This probe works well to monitor food inside any oven and even in cookers like the Ninja Speedi, Ninja grills, and pressure cookers. 7 - Cooking progress can be monitored wherever you can take your phone or tablet in the house. You don't have to stay in the kitchen. 8- Works with rotisseries where wired probes aren't practical. 9 - Can be connected to Alexa for notifications. 10 - The base unit is powered by an "A" battery, and pressing a button lets you know if the battery is still good. The probe is charged in the base unit. 11 - The base unit is magnetized so it can be stored on the side of any metal appliance. This means not having to find it in a cabinet or drawer. I have two of these, and keep them on the side of my Anova oven so they are always handy. I have used this Meater Plus in my ovens, the Ninja Speedi, and in my pressure cookers with great results. I have the app on my phone, and can take my phone in the family room while I watch TV and still monitor the progress of my food cooking. I also like the display of the ambient temperature. This tells you whether your oven is actually getting to the temperature you set it to. In my experience, many ovens never reach the temperature you set, so trying to estimate when your food will be cooked is all guesswork. The Meater Plus takes the guesswork out of cooking. Once you set a done temperature, the app estimates when your food will be fully cooked. This make is so much easier to make sure all of the other components of your meal will be done and hot at the same time. No matter how experienced you are in cooking, there is always a certain amount of guesswork in knowing when foods are cooked to the preferred doneness. The Meater Plus eliminates some of the guesswork. I should also mention that the range of the Meater Plus is greater if you remove the probe from the holder before opening the app. This was mentioned by one other reviewer. UPDATE 11/14/24: I purchased 2 of these Meaters 2 years ago and I still love them. As mentioned previously, the probe should be removed from the charger before opening the app to increase the range of the probes. In the last 2 years, I have used these probes in a few ovens and pressure cookers as well as outdoor ovens and smokers. I have never been disappointed with the performance of these probes. What I love about the Meater is:: 1) The charging units for the probes are magnetic. So, I can store them on the side of an oven where they are kept handy. 2) The app is so easy to use. Choose a meat you want to cook to get suggested internal temperatures for your choice, and still have the ability to modify the done temperature. You can also add and save your preferred temperatures for the meats you are cooking. 3) The app allows for carryover temperatures, so the app will say the food is done when it is 5 degrees less than the chosen temperature. 4) Whether cooking indoors or outdoors, I can monitor the progress of my cook inside and on the phone app. 5) The app tells you the ambient temperature of the oven or grill you are using. So, you know if the temperature is actually the temperature you set. 6) My favorite is that the app calculates the time it will take to finish cooking, and this estimate has been spot on. For me, this is important since I try to get sides for the meal done at the same time so everything is hot for serving. I should mention that I also have a couple sets of "wireless" meat thermometers that the probes are attached to wires that must be connected to the base unit. The base unit connects to an app on my phone. Although these meat thermometers work fine and are color coded so you know where each probe is monitoring, the wires get tangled when using 2-4 of them. These meat thermometers are much easier since they are truly wireless. I tries another set of wireless meat thermometers and sent them back because they kept losing the connection. By the time I was able to reconnect them, the meat was over done. The Meater Plus is the way to go. Unfortunately, the Meater block is not the plus version, nor is the block magnetic to stick on the side of an appliance. This Meater Plus works great and I plan to stay with it until they develop a set that works as well. Incidentally, I am back to buy another one. UPDATE 09/13/26: I have had 2 of these Meater Plus thermometers for over 4 years, and they still work perfectly and accurately. Since then, I have bought 3 different rechargeable meat thermometers that work fine when they are charged. The problem is that the rechargeables are drain when not in use. So, I have to remember to charge them the day before I plan to use them. Since the Meater Plus base unit uses batteries to charge the probe and the base unit, they are never out of power. In the 4 years I have had the 2 Meater Plus thermometers, I have not had to change the batteries in the base unit. I have just purchased the Meater Block Smart Meater with 4 probes that uses batteries for the base unit and can be plugged into USB for longer cooks to save the batteries. If this doesn't work for me, I will purchase 2 more of these thermometers since the app supports only 4 thermometers. Personally, I wouldn't recommend any of the rechargeable thermometers since they are never ready when you need them unless you can plan a day ahead to charge them. I hope this review was helpful for you. I will update this review if my opinion changes or I find more ways to use it.

review_title: An essential tool in any kitchen or on any backyard patio. This is your buddy.
review_text: No more forgotten or overcooked meat. The MEATER works and it will help you cook the meat perfectly every time. It's suited better to indirect grilling methods (which I prefer); that is, you cook on the side of the grill without a lit burner. The MEATER monitors the ambient temperature while also monitoring the interior of the meat. The app then controls your cook. When you set up a cook, the app guides you through the process allowing you to select your cut and preferred doneness. When your MEAT is ready to remove from the grill the MEATER will notify you, but it gives you heads up 5 minutes before the finish cook time. The app then even suggests the proper rest period letting you know when it's the perfect time to dig in. The Bamboo housing, which also charges the MEATER probe is stylish enough that I don't mind it clinging magnetically to the side of my fridge when it isn't in use. The case also re-charges the meater probe (via AA or AAA battery can't remember which, lasts a year) and acts as a bluetooth intermediary between your phone and the cooking probe. This way your phone connects with bluetooth to the case not the actual probe and the probe connects to the case... allowing you to keep the case near the probe during the cook and you have much further range with your phone from the case. If you had to connect your phone directly to the probe the range would probably be horrible, but with the MEATER case you get a great bluetooth connection and are free to roam your house or back yard while the cook is perfectly monitored. Keep in mind that this probe really needs thick cuts, you have to get the probe buried just over halfway into the cut. Better with thicker Burgers, Steak Cuts or Chops. So cut, em thick boys! (or gals or...whatever. We all gotsta eat!) I like the magnets on the bamboo base because it allows me to stick the MEATER case right to the metal shelve on my grill while I cook. (I keep it at least a foot from the hot grill) The nice thing is, if it's raining on the deck i just stick the MEATER on the underside of the metal grill shelve and it stays nice and dry aaaaaand so do I!; because i don't have to go outside at all to check on the grill. I think you might still need a quick read grill thermometer (you know the ones that fold out and you stick in the meat for a quick check) for things like thin cuts or wings, so it isn't for every scenario. But, if your a novice and you never cooked a roast or bird before, MEATER will take the guess work out and help you get it right the very first time. I love grilling and cooking and I love the MEATER, a fantastic tool! I know absolutely nothing about the folks over at MEATER HQ, but if I can deduce anything from having used the MEATER I can say they love to cook as well and have a passion for perfectly prepared delectable cuts... every time! Get one!

review_title: Once you start using it, you will wonder how you ever cooked without it
review_text: I do not know how I ever lived without this thing. It has completely changed how I cook meat, especially larger cuts. Being able to track temperature live on my phone while I am doing other things makes cooking feel almost foolproof. Now let us talk about what it is and what it is not. Most people seem to use it the way it is shown in the pictures, to make sure they do not overcook a steak. That is fine, but it is actually one of the least useful ways to use it. The device measures both the internal and ambient temperature of what you are cooking and uses those readings to predict total cooking time. The problem is that steak cooks so quickly that it never has time to make accurate predictions. By the time it is ready to tell you it is almost done, it is already done or even overdone. That said, even for steaks it is still very handy. Being able to monitor your meat temperature in real time means you can stop guessing and hit your preferred doneness every time. Just make sure you are doing your own mental math about carryover cooking, because you cannot rely on the predictive feature for the length of cook or resting time with short cooks. Where this thing truly shines is in slow roasting. If you are making prime rib, tri tip, pork roast, or pulled pork, this is your best friend. Stick it in at the start and after about twenty minutes it will give you a remarkably accurate estimate for total cooking time. If that timing does not line up with your plans, you can adjust your heat early. It is also excellent for knowing exactly when to pull the meat, whether you want it ready to slice or fall apart tender. I actually have two of them for when I am cooking for a crowd and some people like medium rare while others want medium. It makes it easy to track both and know exactly when to pull each one for perfect results. It is not perfect. In my experience it tends to overestimate total cook time because it sometimes reads the ambient temperature a little low. Since the probe is still inside the meat, which is cooler than the oven, it does not pick up the true oven temperature accurately. Even with that small quirk, it is one of the most useful kitchen tools I own. Once you use it, you will never go back to guessing.

I rarely write reviews, but believe this product is so outstanding I had to "sing it's praises. This "smoking/grilling" thermometer is, without a doubt, one of the best tools available for keeping tabs on your BBQ/grilling/smoking "cooks". I just received my "Meater+" thermometer 4 days ago and did my first cook (Boston butt) two days after it arrived. I will say, that I did a lot of research before making this purchase and as usual, there were some negative comments. I believe many of the negative comments are due to people not setting the Meater+ up correctly, especially where it concerns the " Meater+ "App". I had no problem at all setting up the thermometer. Once you are ready to begin using the thermometer, open the app and follow the step-by-step directions to get everything going. One of the criticisms I read concerning the app was that the thermometer kept losing its connection to the "repeater" block. This is actually the charging station and case in which you keep the Meater. The charging station must stay close to the probe for it to say connected (Bluetooth). I set the the Block right next to the grill, about 3 feet away. When setting up the Meater, be sure to pair the probe and bluetooth connection FIRST. Then open the "app" and the smart phone (or tablet) will pair with the "repeater" and give you the ability to monitor your cook from some distance, depending, of course, on what the obstruction is between you and the grill. With the "Meater" you can monitor the ambient temperature, the temperature of your meat, an estimate of when the the cook will be done and you can either use a programed cook or set up your own custom parameters. The app will log the cook and display a graph of temp fluctuations. and allows you to make notes concerning your cook. The app is one of the best, most well thought out apps I have seen. I also monitored the temperatures with my Thermo Pro wired thermometer. The ambient temp reading was within 5 degrees throughout the entire cooking process (keep in mind the probes were not in the exact same location). The internal temp of the meat varied by as much as 20 degrees. This could also be due to the probes of the thermometers being in different "densities" within the meat. I believe the accuracy of the Meater+ is spot on. If one would like to read a review of the Meater+ written by a professional "griller" go to "foodfirefriends.com. And no, I did not receive any compensation for writing this review.

review_title: 2 Probes, 2 Cooks, 2 Epic Fails; WASTE OF MONEY
review_text: Update 11/28/23: AFTER MY REVIEW, the TempSpike customer service reached out to me and asked me to get in touch with them. In short, they sent me a new TempSpike told me to discard the old one. I used it this weekend and the results were also disappointing. TempSpike was fully charged. Insert d in my turkey on my Kamado grill rotisserie. Result: temperature was way off, intuition told me to use a different thermometer to check accuracy: 2 other thermometers told me my turkey was already done meanwhile TempSpike was reporting that I had 10 degrees to go. That can be the difference if having a moist breast or a dry one. Also, the cook was 3 hours and the battery was all the way down to where it was showing red to charge; this was a 3 hour cook. So, if I had to recalibrate the TempSpike to read correct temperature, the battery is still a fail especially if you were gonna have a low and slow cook like pork butt or brisket. I purchased this is April and had to return it because it wasn’t working. I figured it was a fluke and ordered another one. I used it once and it worked fine. Had to keep the phone on same level as base or I would lose signal. That’s not a deal breaker for me. What is a deal breaker is the fact that I only used this once and the next time I needed it (today) the probe wouldn’t hold a charge even after charging the whole night. I called up customer service and they are sending me out a new one that takes 3-5 days. I was planning on using my Joetisserie this weekend and I was planning on using a wireless thermometer since a wired thermometer on a rotating turkey is just not possible. So my cook today was salvaged because I had my old reliable Redi Check wired thermometer. But I guess this weekend I’m not going to have a choice but check temp sporadically with a handheld thermometer. Thanks Thermopro. You’re 0 for 2 so far. Let’s see what happens when I get the replacement.

review_title: Save your money and get a cheap instant read thermometer.
review_text: For the money this thing is junk. First cook the temperatures were all over the place. The app kept alerting that the ambient temperature was too high, and the meat temperature barely changed. Before I could even finish smoking the brisket, I lost connection to the spike, so I checked it other ways. Confirmed meat temp was a good 20-30° higher than the last reading from my app, and the manual thermometer on my smoker and an infrared thermometer both gave me temperatures exactly where I expected them to be. I calibrated the thermometer using boiling water and an ice cube and got readings I expected, so I rechaged and hoped to try again. The next time I used it for a beef roast, and pulled it at 130. The instant read said 150, so I cut into to check and sure enough, it was way over cooked. Gave it one last try at Thanksgiving when I attempted to smoke a chuck roast. Went to charge it and couldn't get the spike to register at all. It looks like the battery in the spike is dead. Overall, I think I got to use it 5 times over 2 years. Not once did it work right. I was always better off just using a $10 instant read thermometer. Oh, and the app is a pain in the ass as well. The interface is so clunky and the alarms so obnoxious, that I felt a sense of relief when the unit died and I didn't have to deal with it anymore.

review_title: I cant trust this probe, temperature not accurate on mine! Really bummed
review_text: I bought this thinking that it was going to be such an amazing item. I love bbq'ing and smoking meats! I use both a traditional offset smoker and over the summer bought a Trager pellet smoker. Been using the Trager a lot- its so easy compared to traditional methods. Anyhow, thought that the wireless probes would be a game changer for me- no wires, no mess and no hassle. Me being me though, the first couple of times trying to use this probe- I also run my traditional wired probes just in case and so glad that I did. The wireless probe I received is not accurate. The inner temperature is closer to being accurate but the ambient reading is way off. Either way, with both of those temps not being accurate, I cannot trust my cooks to this probe.... Would have loved for it to work- great concept but it burned me- no pun intended!

Doesn’t matter how I prepare, there’s always a reason this garbage won’t do what it’s designed to do. You know what has NEVER failed me? My $5 meat thermometer. No Bluetooth, no batteries, no app, no IT certification required. Congratulations, ThermoPro. You’ve managed to make a thermometer less reliable than a $5 stick with a dial.

review_title: Save your money by something else
review_text: Gotta say pretty disappointed in this for as popular as it is. I've had it for close to 6 months and the more I use it the less I like it. First the instructions are pretty terrible. I love the convince of one probe for both internal and ambient, but whatever tech they are using the ambient portion of the probe is strongly affected by the temp coming off whatever you are cooking. For example you have it in 44 degree brisket and you put it in your pre heated 250 degree smoker it reads the ambient temp as 175 degrees and as the brisket gets warmer the ambient goes up but never giving you an accurate ambient temp. Charging the probe is nearly impossible. If it isn't seated perfectly in the booster pack it will not charge. Takes forever to fully charge, and it only last 12hrs fully charged, not the 24 it boasts. It doesn't seem to shut off either so after you charge it, all those lights just keep blinking and drain the battery. Really wish I had not purchased this or at least not given it so many chances so i could return it. OH AND, there is no 500 ft range. Maybe a 100ft at best. Also the recording feature ahuts off randomly. The only thing I will give it is it does measure internal temp well. Bottom line save your money and get a product. ***** additionally I still have it the battery only last 6 hrs at best now, the company asked me to reach out to them. I did and I never heard anything back. Just dont waste your time with this hunk of garbage

review_text: I have two of these and I hate both of them. They simply do not hold a charge for any length of time. It has happened every time I have taken out a previously charged probe, only to find it fully discharged. Don’t waste your money on this!

You also have to insert it so far its almost impossible to use it on short time cooks, chicken thighs nope, drum sticks nope, chicken breast yes. Likes: - Connection to phone was a breeze. - Graphics in the phone app are straightforward and well-designed. - Booster (the base) held an exceptional charge Dislikes: - Probe lost power extremely fast. I fully charged the probe and base (charged until the light went off, and then left it plugged in a few hours more until brisket was ready to smoke). I inserted the probe into a brisket at 11pm and put it into the smoker. By 4am the probe’s battery light on the app was already showing low power, but brisket was in “the stall” so I had some time. I took the probe out and put it back on charger for another hour to try to get it enough charge to continue. At 5am I wrapped my brisket in foil (Texas crutch) and reinserted the probe to bring brisket up to 203 degree target. At 7am the power in the probe was out again and brisket was at 190 degrees. I pulled the probe out and recharged it for a couple hours. Upon reinsertion, battery indicated it was nearly fully charged, but lasted only 4 hours this time. review_title: This will ruin your meat.  They need to work out the bugs
review_text: So I'm a longtime ThermaPen user and proselytizer. ThermaPro's pens are the best in the business. So I got this thinking it would be the same; long story short, it isn't. There are 3 big problems with this: 1) the probe itself is inaccurate. I had a 2 inch dry aged ribeye I reverse seared, and pulled it when it reached 115 (i like rare-ish). When i used my thermapen, and another instant read to check it, it read 145!! I was concerned when it seemed like the app was jumping 2-3 degrees at a time, and I really should have known that the system was lagging. An 85 dollar steak was ruined. I tried with a smaller cut, a 1.5inch prime top sirloin from costco, and pulled it at 125, it felt incredibly firm, and again with my instant read it came out at 155. Total shoe leather. Garbage. 2) the ambient temperature is low by 20-30 degrees, when double checking with weber igrill, a laser thermo, and a cheap wired thermometer. 3) the app is terrible. The presets only go down to 125, the "time left" counter is more laughable than a Windows 95 file copy time estimate (i.e. inaccurate), the app's UX is ugly, like I said before, temperatures don't increase in increments bigger than 2-3 degrees. Big disappointment. Returning today to a UPS store.

review_title: Disappointing Durability - 2nd one in less than 1 year
review_text: I recently purchased my second ThermoPro TempSpike, having used it daily for cooking baked chicken. Unfortunately, I am compelled to share my less-than-satisfactory experience with this product. Durability Issues: The most significant issue I've encountered is the short lifespan of the probe. Despite regular use, which should be well within the capabilities of such a product, the probe has failed consistently, and it hasn't even been a year yet. This lack of durability is a major drawback, especially for anyone relying on this thermometer for daily cooking. Replacement Frequency: The fact that I am considering purchasing a third unit within such a short time frame is a testament to the unreliability of this product. It's frustrating and not what I expected when I first chose ThermoPro TempSpike. Advice to Potential Buyers: Given my experience, I would advise potential buyers to consider other options. It might seem economical at first, but the need for frequent replacements negates any initial savings. If you're looking for a reliable cooking thermometer, it might be worth investing in a higher-priced brand that offers better durability and reliability. Conclusion: In summary, while the ThermoPro TempSpike seems promising in its functionality, its poor durability makes it a less viable option for anyone who needs a dependable kitchen thermometer. I'm disappointed with the product's performance and would recommend others to look for more reliable alternatives.

review_title: Not exactly as convenient as described. Disappointed to say the least.
review_text: Let me start off by saying I do competition BBQ. I understand how to cook and smoke meats and the learning curve it takes to understand the gadgets and such. I was looking for a wireless Probe I could monitor my smoker and meat from a small distance and be able to prep meat, walk away from said smoker and have accuracy. I purchased this thinking it would be easier to monitor temps of smoker and meat at the same time with out all the wires. Currently I have a Weber temp probe that has 4 probes that connect to the box and box is blue tooth’s to my phone. I also bought this Temp Spike. I have a barrel smoker, it needs a little babysitting, it’s not a set and forget. I did some research on these types of Probes and I thought this was the best bang for my buck. Sadly I’ve been disappointed. Walk 15-20 feet away and the monitor goes nuts because it disconnected. I Played with the booster and still have to basically be with in a eyes reach of said thermostat for it to register. Essentially the probe connects to the “box” and box connects to app. Which app could use a little help too. ( I’ve seen grade school kids make ones with better features.). Well if I can see the thermostat on my smoker the ambient portion of this is pointless. Plus it’s not accurately calibrated. Temp spike was reading 295, my Weber ambient probe the was next to it read 325, smoke thermometer on the barrel it’s self was 325, thermal gun read 327. 25 degrees is 25 degrees and it can change a cook time by an hour depending on what your making ( ie. brisket). Can it register internal temp, yes, but don’t walk away because you lose your connection, it goes nuts, and you have to reset it or reconnect when you walk away. Literally walked from my smoker to my garage less than 20 feet. (Yes, I understand you can turn off the alarms but then what’s the point. ) It’s a large diameter thermometer so smaller cuts like chicken breast or steaks ect it dosnt do well. Stick it in a pork shoulder or a large brisket and it works as a thermometer. Anything else and it’s just to big and leaves a big hole. Also, battery life. Not the best, and have the connections cleaned and back to factory shine or it won’t charge, it’s good for about 1 cook. Sorry for the bad review, was really hoping this would work out. An idea for improvement would be to give the temp spike box better blue tooth range so once it’s connected it doesn't drop. I understand the probe need to be small and compact, but give the box moor oomph. That way we can leave box by probe and continue to move on with life.

Bought TempPro TempSpike Nov 2023, used it for 3 Thanksgivings and a few prime rib dinners. It has stopped working. When it worked it was great. Now I need one for Thanksgiving and I don't have one. review_title: Not fully convinced with this one
review_text: I come to the decision that using a wireless thermometer with data capabilities is a most in order to continuously improve my cooking/smoking. In comparison with other products on the market this is in the low budget range with some of the features. Here are some of the things that don’t work well when trying to decide which option you should go to: * The probe and base: * I ordered two TempSpikes, the first one stopped syncing between the probe and the base after the 3rd cook on temperatures below 300F. I didn't get a response from support and was able to returned to Amz within the 30days timeframe and hoping the second doesn't get any issues * It lacks the capability to connect directly to wifi or to allow one device/tablet to sync into the cloud and watch the cooking from another device while you are out of range, like doing errands. * The app: * Switching between landscape to portrait doesn’t work on the iPad, you have to forcibly close the app and open it again, which will stop your current cooking recording * Update, in version 2.0.5 completely removed landscape mode which is the natural way to support the iPad while charging. Before the update Landscape mode on the iPad doesn’t fit the whole screen, you have to scroll down middle way to see both internal temperature and ambient temperature * No cooking time clock. Some comments indicate this display was there before and then removed * Update not fixed with the new start/stop recording button outside of the profile selection. Not able to change cooking temperature or profile after start. You have to stop the current cooking and start a new one with different profile or temperature setting. This will not allow you to record you whole cooking if you have more than one cooking temperature steps, like when you need to wrap in foil/paper * Export option is broken. It ask for your email address but nothing is sent/received. It should be more like when sharing in Apple, ask about what to do with an excel/CSV file or similar format and then let the phone/tablet manage the sharing/exporting, which will allow to save on the device, email etc. * The share/screenshot option crashes the app (it doesn’t even show up as open) * Not a cloud features. If the app closes/crashes it will require you to start a new cooking instead of continuing with the last one. It doesn’t allow you to collect data from one device and watch/manage the settings from another device when you need to go out of range. Overall, I'm not fully convinced that this is a good option and basically you get what you pay.

review_title: There are much better wireless thermometers than this...
review_text: I wanted to like this product but it just isn't up to snuff. I've had it for about eight months have done maybe a dozen cooks with it. It's packaged nicely and has clear instructions. The Bluetooth range is very good. The app works fine, but I need to find a setting that allows it to keep the phone always on so I don't have to keep unlocking the phone to check what's going on with temps. Totally dissatisfied with the ambient air readings. Internal meat temps are satisfactory but ambient cooking temps are not. I use a wired probe that's known to be accurate to monitor differences and sometimes this product is off by as much as 50 degrees! It almost always reads too low. I read that can happen if the meat is cold and that makes sense, but it still takes FOREVER to catch up to the wired probe, and then as the cook progresses if there's a rapid change (like if your fire is getting out of control), this thermometer is very slow to pick up on that. Then there's the issue of charging. The booster charges up just fine, and maintains a charge for a very long time. The probe? Not so much. The issue I have charging the probe is that it takes a LONG time to indicate full charge. I have made the mistake or relying on that, and then after taking it out of the booster/charger station and turning on the app, I find out that the probe is nowhere near fully charged. So, the day before cooking I'll charge it up, then do it again the morning of the cook, making sure it's fully charged before I need to use it. Again, each charging cycle takes HOURS. I doubt this product is supposed to work that way? Finally the probe is very thick and requires 2-1/2 inches of probe depth to operate properly. This limits the usefulness of this product to relatively large cuts of meat. I will be exploring better wireless thermometer products. It's accurate for the meat temps, but not for ambient temps, and the charging problems are unforgiveable. Nice packaging and range, though.

review_title: I was happy with it the last couple times, but today that changed.
review_text: I can't in good conscious give this product more than 2 stars after today. I bought this a few months back and it worked well the couple times I used it in my smoker and my grill. Today, things seem to have changed in a very bad way. I've kept my grill and smoker on the back porch and the booster was only 15 feet away, just through the back door on the washer and dryer. This allowed the booster to stay connected to my phone, even up stairs, about 40-50 feet away from it. I live in a 100 year old house with lathe and plaster walls, so some issues are expected, but with the supposed 500 foot range claims from the booster to phone, I'd expect better. Well, I was recently able to build a small patio for a new grill gazebo I was gifted, so I moved the smoker and grill about 20 feet further from the old location. This shouldn't have made a big deal, but again, the company claims that with the lid close, the distance between the probe and booster for connection is 35 feet. I can't get the booster further than 15 feet from my smoker without it disconnecting from the booster. On top of that, from where I do have it located so it can stay connected, I can't go further than 40 feet into my house without my phone no longer picking up the booster. This is less than 10% the distance the company claims. Now, I don't know if the company is lying on purpose or what, but this is unacceptable. I won't be purchasing from this company again. Meater wireless probes look better anyways, so I guess I'll be moving over to one of those.

review_title: Not Quite Ready for Prime Time
review_text: I really wanted to like this device. I have had one of Thermopro's instant read thermometers for years and love it. I do a lot of low and slow cooks, so this seemed like a perfect replacement for my current wireless thermometer setup. This device theoretically would allow me to keep the lid closed for most of the cook, and have one small device to track my meat an ambient temps. But, after a little bit of time leaving the probe on in my house that the ambient temperature readings were not even close to accurate. For whatever reason the temp went from about 5 degrees cooler than house temp (I have multiple readings in my house and was able to determine precise temps), to 15 degrees cooler than the room. This continued when the meat was on the grill cooking as well. The temps were almost 25 degrees different from my wireless thermometer I've used for years. The other issue was with internal temperatures. Even though they were much more accurate, they were very slow to update. This caused me to overshoot my target temp for my meats by about 10 degrees because the thermometer didn't update fast enough. It seems like it's on some kind of timed cadence for updates and for me they were way too spaced out. I attempted to use this for three low and slow cooks and it failed the same way each time. One design flaw I found with the device (and reading on competitor devices this seems to be a common compliant of truly wireless probes) is that the probe itself is really big. It made putting this thing into a pork butt, chuck roast, and steak very difficult. If you can't get it into a pork butt easily, how are you expected to get this to fit and stay in place for a more delicate/lighter protein like a chicken. It barely stayed in place with a gigantic tomahawk steak. I love the concept of the device, and I only lost connection twice (which is much better than my other wireless thermometer), so I think there's hope for it in the long term. But, I'm going to hold off buying another one of these fully wireless thermometers until they've had a chance to mature a bit in the market. Maybe in a couple years I'll take a look and see if the technology and designs have improved.

Idk, maybe it's me, but I don't see how after I used my warranty and got a replacement but still having troubles. For whatever reason, the pairing feature is very poor. It says we should hardly if ever have to pair the probe to the booster however, it seems like I need to all the time. This is now the 2nd time and on a new device even, I can't get the probe to sync at all, making it unusable. This was my problem the first time and received a replacement. Here I am again after only a couple uses and I am stuck without a probe in the middle of a cook. The battery life is also very misleading. You're getting about 5 hours, idk how this could be used for a brisket, honestly. Really would like my money back and go back to wired probes.

review_title: when it works, it's great, but when it doesn't, can't figure out why
review_text: I really like this probe. When it works, it's fantastic. However, it's hard to know that 1) the base battery is dead 2) the probe battery is dead 3) comms between the base and probe aren't working and why More than once I've pulled it out and put meat on the grill only to learn the probe battery was dead or comms between the base and my phone aren't working for one reason or another. With only 3 LEDs to troubleshoot with, I have to Google what the blink codes are each time. My wife also connected the probe to her phone recently which broke the connection to my phone. When it works, it's fantastic, but troubleshooting when it doesn't leaves much to be desired.

review_title: Loved while it lasted... Only the good die young.
review_text: To start- it was easy to use with the app and get it set up. The app gives pointers on what temp your meat needs to be and gives you updates on your phone which are customizable. I used the thermometer on the grill and in the instant pot and it worked fine. To finish- the harness (what the battery sits in) is not charging anymore. I charged it up the first time without much of an issue maybe because it comes partially charged already? Trying to recharge it now and it's a dud. Unless something changes my review should remain the same. It's decent if you needed to monitor food for an event but if there are more dud battery harnesses out there I can't recommend a short-term lifespan product at these quality prices.

If TempSpike was a baseball player, it would have struck out in the first inning. I thought I was getting the MVP of wireless thermometers, but turns out, it’s more like the rookie who can’t handle the heat. After a measly four cooks, this thermometer decided it was time to retire. Seriously, TempSpike, I’ve had socks with more staying power. I was expecting a grilling champion, but all I got was a thermometer that tapped out faster than a UFC fighter in the octagon. The only thing spiking here is my disappointment level. TempSpike, you’re supposed to be in it for the long game, not a short-lived cameo. I’ve had relationships with condiments that lasted longer than our time together. So, if you’re looking for a thermometer that plays hard to get and bails out faster than a scared cat, TempSpike might be your match. As for me, I’ll be on the hunt for a thermometer that doesn’t throw in the towel quicker than a 90s boy band’s fame.

review_title: Ambient temp is useless, app could use work
review_text: I have confidence in ThermoPro products and use their instant read thermometers. So when going for an iGrill replacement I went with ThermoPro. Pros: probe not too big, internal temperature seems very accurate Cons: The ambient temp is WAY off and extremely slow to react, nowhere near 500 ft range. I need accurate ambient temp for a wood smoker and this one is off by 10-25 degrees as verified by 2 other thermometers. Also is very slow to react to temerature changes so I I get a flare up it takes too long to register. This is a deal breaker. The range is also nowhere near 500 ft. Perhaps direct line of sight but if there is anything in between the range drops dramatically. Range seems comparable to iGrill about 30 ft through walls, 50 ft outside. Last but not least the app is crude. It displays too much information on one screen making it hard to follow and does not have a widget (really, this is integral to IOS these days). It is going back. Skip this one and try something else.

I have a Thermpro TP08 and love it. I saw a neighbor with this model and thought I'd give it a try when it was on sale. I like not having the cords connected to the probes, and the ambient temp sensor on the end of the probe. That's where the good qualities end unfortunately. I knew the battery didn't last more than 12 hours, but I thought it would last at least 8 in time to finish a small brisket, but it did not. I don't like the thickness of the probe and the ambient temperature takes forever to sync up. If I had a flare up or ran out of pellets, you probably wouldn't know it for about 10 minutes (no joke). I had my other Thermpro probes in relatively the same spot of meat as the this Tempspike at at times I had a discrepancy of more than 13 degrees, which to me is unacceptable. I would return this if I could.

review_title: Not sure I can trust it's accuracy...
review_text: I'm a ThermoPro fan and own many of their items including my instant read, my four probe, my old single probe and my brand new ThermoSpike. This temperature difference has me questioning it's accuracy, though. I smoked a brisket overnight and pulled it to finish it in the oven. The ThermoSpike has it at 176°. Perfect, ready for the oven. I wrapped it, put the ThermoSpike back in and double checked it with my TP19 instant read and I'm getting mid to high 180° range all over the brisket. That's a significant temperature difference and now my timing on the brisket is completely messed up. I was wondering if there was an issue because I had the smoker set to 230° and the ambient temp reading on the ThermoSpike was only showing 205°. My smoker has always been really close to the set temp and that should have been a sign I should check with the instant read sooner. I really love this thing but if the temperature is inaccurate by upwards of 10°, it's no use to me. I may have to return it.
The battery life on these are horrible. Not even a year old and it doesn’t last 4 hours. I’ve maybe used it 10 times in a year and a half.

review_title: Splurge a little more on better options
review_text: When it powers on/syncs, it works just fine. But overall piece of junk. Have gone through 3 since initially purchased, because of failure to sync up/power on. Company will send replacement each time. But grew tired of going through process of getting replacement. Overall poor quality piece of technology.
It was alright. It worked great until it quit. It didn’t last long. It lasted approximately 2-3 months and for approximately 8 grilling/smokings

I have owned the tempspike for about a year, using it three times without a problem. This Thanksgiving, I fully charged it in advance of cooking. On the big day, I was disappointed that the bluetooth connection would not work. I charged it again and managed to pair with the phone, but the pairing was unstable and quickly dropped. It seems this device is now unusable. While this is a budget device, I expected to get more than 4 uses/1 year of service form it. So if you buy, test in advance, but not too far in advance. And don't expect it to hold up over time.

The battery in the probe does not hold a charge. It last about 6 hours. In fact after charging all day and night, the probe battery wasn't showing full. So maybe its not charging correctly. I emailed the company about a week ago but have yet to receive a reply.

The range on it is great. Pretty accurate on cooking temps. The probe never stays charged. It’ll say it’s fully charged and then you go to use it and the probe says low warning and needs to be charged. Useless if the probe won’t hold a charge. Would def look into buying something else as this one has never worked very good since buying it.

Worked well for about 3 cooks. I use it to smoke brisket, which takes around 10-12 hours. First 3 times it worked as expected. The fourth time the battery died about 6 hours in. I charged it up and it then only worked for about 3 hours. Hasn’t been the same since. You start with a full charge and 4 hours later the charge indicator is in the red and you can’t trust the reading you are getting. I’m now looking for something else that works for at least 12-14 hours on a charge. Really disappointed in this product.

The ambient temp always seems to be 10-20 degrees cooler at any given point, I don't believe the internal temperature is accurate as well, if I use a manual probe it seems to always be hotter than this probe suggests. It died on hour 8 of a 9 hour smoke but I imagine it wasn't meant to last that long. Probably could have just put it in halfway through and been fine. There's no way this has a 500ft distance. I set this in an open window sill in line of sight maybe 30 feet away from the grill and then was on the other side of a closed door and my phone would lose connection with the bluetooth repeater (not the repeater losing connection to the probe). So overall probably 40 feet away. I am not impressed at all with this probe. Seems like a waste of money, but I am glad I got it on a sale at over half off.

I enjoyed using this TemoSpike for a year until the probe stopped working. I used it about once a month but 7 months after getting this for a Christmas present the device won't charge, won't connect. I plug the device in to a type c charger that charges my Samsung Galaxy devices and nothing happens. No lights, no charging and won't connect to my phone which have been previously. Very frustrating I have used this all year but now it is completely useless. I don't know if these need to be bought yearly or what. Very unhappy now with this device. Should I try a new brand?
For some reason will not hold a charge after charging for 20 hours straight Not accurate readings of ambient temp Junk.
It was good while it lasted for a year, until the battery broke. Now it doesn't appear to hold any charge in either the booster or the probe. What is the warranty length?
It worked untill it didn't. Crapped out on me a year later or so.
Worked great twice. Hence 2 stars. Probe then failed to connect to booster and that was the end of that.

review_title: Probe doesn't charge, wont hold a charge.
review_text: Worked for a while but always had trouble charging the probe. I only paid $25 so not much of a loss.
Worked great and then stopped after 2 years. Cooking my prime rib with a candy thermometer today, wooo.

Worked pretty good the first year or so, then it would connect about half the time. Now it doesn't connect at all. Great when it works Expected more from this brand and the cost. Side note, Can't really be used on anything other than thick cuts. I used it for smoking butts.

Works well when new. Sat in drawer for a year, charged, and isn't covering a 3-4 hour thanksgiving turkey cook. Battery seems to go bad quickly. Recommend you try something else. Have only used 3-4 times, so not clear why battery seems to be failing.
Battery life sucks and it won’t make it thru a full cook. The prob had 3 bars and I’m 30 minutes into a cook and it’s already gone down 1 bar.
While the length of the probe is superior to other brands, it stops working after a couple of months. Customer service was great a shipped out another unit free of charge, but that one failed also.

review_title: Not reliable after a few uses.
review_text: Loved it at first, but after 3 or 4 uses, it won't charge in the case, and is unusable. Even when it does charge, it won't stay charged or connect to base. Waste of money.
Was nice while it worked. Ours are only 2 years old and neither will charge any more. Def not worth the price if it can’t even last 2 years.

review_title: Zero for two on the device.
review_text: It worked for 4 months, ThermoPro sent a replacement and that workes for 6 months. The probe is not durable and will disconnect from the base.

review_title: Worked for a while, but finding it loses charge quickly, always dead when you need it.
review_text: Well, it worked for a while and would actually say I was impressed.. BUT, after a few months... every time I'd go to use it, the damned thing was dead. If you don't remember to charge it up every time you go to use it, you'll end up having to guess making it a bit of a paper weight.
It was great when it worked.. After a few months the probe wouldn’t hold a charge. It would charge up to 3 bars and within 30 seconds it would die.
Lasted half a year before it was hit or miss, lasted two years before it stopped working. Two stars for two years.
The app is great! But the unit after less then a year is not holding a charge at all!! Very disappointed for the amount of money paid for this item
The probes battery life only last 5 hours but the booster last 8+ hours! I fully charged both before initial use!

I wanted to like this thermometer, but I’m really disappointed in the build quality. During normal use, the plastic top literally popped off while in the grill. For a product that’s supposed to handle high heat, this is unacceptable. It makes me question the durability and safety of the device. Definitely not worth the money if it can’t even hold up under the conditions it’s advertised for.

I bought the temp spike because I liked the app and wireless possibilities. Unfortunately, I’ve had it for less than 2 years and it has become VERY unreliable. There are connectivity issues. The spike goes from fully charged to dead in less than 3 hours (absolutely useless when smoking and real meat). I’m so disappointed. Definitely NOT worth the money.

review_title: Worked twice then wouldn’t connect agian
review_text: Work twice then when connect again
Worked great for 7 months then the probe malfunctioned and reads 400+ degrees at room temperature. Troubleshooting didn’t help. I can’t find any warranty info on the website to see if it’s covered.

review_title: It works but wish it lasted longer
review_text: I've owned this for a year and a half and overall I am satisfied. The battery for the actual probe however will not charge past 50% despite everything i have tried. The app and range are great though. I really like that I can add comments to each cook and log it for future reference (outside temp, windy, etc.) I suggest this to friends. **Update** The battery lasts 2 hours now. It is 2 years old, I will not buy another one.

I had high hopes for this. The company behind the product has some great temperature probes. But this one has been sporadic at best. Things that I like: - handle on the probe is large enough to grip while wearing gloves - usb-c rechargeable booster - when it works, the temp is accurate Things that I don’t like: - the booster needs to be charged more often than the batteries on another unit I have needs to be replaced - I need to remember to check the charge a day before a long cook because you can’t just replace the batteries - the booster regularly looses connection with the probe. More on this. Today is a beautiful day to smoke a pork butt. I remembered to check the charge of the booster and the probe yesterday. Both were at 100%. I got the pork out and prepared it, put the probe in, and verified the connection. Then put the pork into the smoker and closed the lid. Everything was working and I spent a few minutes tending the fire before checking the probe one more time and heading in. That’s when it happened. I looked at the app and the probe had disconnected. I still had a connection to the booster, but not booster to the probe. And this wasn’t the first time. Every time I have used the probe it randomly disconnects. I put a metal table in front of the smoker so I can have the booster about a foot away from the probe. With my other meat thermometer I can keep it further away without any disconnecting. This will reconnect, but worry that I won’t have an accurate cook and I don’t like worrying.

review_title: TP-960 Does Not Hold a Charge
review_text: I will start with the positives. The app is good, easy to maneuver and user friendly. The range good. If you find that you are getting disconnected make sure that the Booster is near the grill and not inside next to your phone. The temperature is within 2°-3° of any of my other thermometers, I’ll take that. Now for the negatives… I have 4 of these. I bought the first 2 and 2 are replacements from the manufacturer. (I forgot to put that above on the positives…. The customer service was outstanding. But it does not outweigh my negatives.) The first issue I had was #1 would not make the Bluetooth connection. I tried several times eventually with the help of customer service, which led the them sending a new complete unit. Thank You for that! It now connects and I am happy. Now to #2. It connected just fine and seemed to be working properly. The issue came in when the probe battery died about 3 hours into a brisket. Not good. So, again, another call to Customer service and working with them again, they sent a replacement unit. Thanks again! So, now I have 4 TempSpikes, one of which is useless because of the non connecting booster, although the probe still works, kind of. So, following the written instructions and customer supports recommendations on usage and placement of the probe and booster I can not get any more than 5 hours max on any of the probes. I have tried on several styles of grills and smokers, I tried in the oven and lastly I have placed each on the counter not inserted to anything and still the probes are dying at or before the 5 hour mark. Per the specifications the probes are supposed the be good for “48 hours or more”. I would gladly settle for half of that. I don't understand how with over 8000 positive reviews I cant get one to work as advertised. I do a lot of Butts and Briskets and as much as I like the TempSpike and want it to work, I think I’ll have to move on. Anyway, I know this was long winded but I wanted to make sure that I explained myself without just leaving a bad review. Thanks for Reading

review_title: Internal temp accurate, external not so much
review_text: I’ve had rotten luck with leave-in wireless probes but I gave this one a try. Unlike others I’ve tried, this one accurately measured the inside temp, but the ambient temp is at least 50 degrees low consistently. Also, the probe loses its sync with the base station every time I take it off. This is all when fully charged. However, I really like the app, it works good although the alarm is the exact same sound as my smoke detectors which is incredibly disconcerting. I’ll keep this one, it’s works. At the end of the day, accurately telling me the internal temperature is all that truely matters anyway, I can handle the rest.

review_title: The item works very well….. for a while.
review_text: This is my second one. What I have found is that these items last until a short time after the 1 year warranty expires. Then the “spike” stops communicating with the base. And then it is useless. The first one I thought was an anomaly, the second one leads me to believe it’s a trend. I think I will try another brand to see if I get more service out of it. Too bad, because, in the short time these worked, they delivered. Good design on unit and app. Just too wasteful to continue replacing year after year.

Maybe I'm doing something wrong. I doubt it. I will stand by my words that thermoworks crap has always been overrated. I bought this temp spike in July 2023 and have used it a dozen times, none of them satisfactorily. After initial charging I smoked a pork loin and realized the ambient temp was incorrect with no means of calibration. Within a week I tried to utilize this junk again only to find that the probe battery was weak, after only four hours of use? Reverted to my wired thermometers and charged the temp spike. Next use within a week on poultry with several issues of connectivity between the spike and the base, also probe battery was weak. Now it's late October, charged all night only to find the probe battery weak after a couple hours into beef short ribs. I have used this worthless junk at least a dozen times and have never been happy with it even once. It's always something. My advice to any friend of mine would be to run away from thermoworks products and don't look back. I've had a letdown over energy product that I've ever purchased from them and will end the suffering right now. ******UPDATE!******* Although my initial assessment that Thermoworks products are overrated still stands, I would like to commend the customer service I have received from Intek. After my initial review they contacted me and we have come to an amicable agreement regarding this matter. My advice to friends at this point would be to go ahead and give it a try with full confidence that if it isn't right, they will make it right.

I have the Thermopro T20, and I love it. When I started investigating purely wireless meat thermometers, I decided I would go with the Thermopro instead of trying the Meater or Meatstick. I loved my prior Thermopro and thought, stick with what you know. I've only used the Tempspike a couple of times, and I thought it worked great. I actually bought two (for those asking if you can get more than one). It was easy to add both to the app. I think I read somewhere that there may be a limit of three you can add, but I can't confirm. In any case, worked great on the steak I was cooking. No more wires, which made it easy to flip and just coordinate. Easy to clean. Only had it a short time, so will see long term. HOWEVER, the one thing that really annoys me is that you MUST insert the probe up to a line towards the end, which is a few inches. I called up customer service to ask how that would work with hamburgers or small meats like a filet, for example. They told me you can't. It must go up to the line at the end. I was actually extremely annoyed and contemplated returning them. However, I didn't. Because of laziness? Maybe. Too excited to use them? Probably. I rationalized keeping them, but if I was planning again, I probably would have purchased a different product for this reason alone. I just don't want to have to worry about what I can use it with or not, and if not, etc. With that said, worked great for the meats you can use them for, which will be most meats for me anyway.

It worked great for a couple of months, and then it stopped working. The company was kind enough to send me a replacement which worked great for a couple of months, and then stopped working. I didn't go back for a third one.
It was good until the probe stopped working. But I must say the company immediately replace with with no questions asked.

review_title: Expect to replace every couple years.
review_text: It’s okay. It worked fine for the first two years I used it, great range. After that battery life degraded quickly, sucks and almost unusable other than instant read or cooking a quick steak. No longer good for smoking or slow cook.

review_title: Charge them the day before you need them!
review_text: They are never ready when I need them. I've had temp spikes for several years now and they always leave me hanging. I can never reliably go to where I store them, pick them up and use them. I cleaned them, I charge them fully, and I store them in their containers in the box that they came in and when I go to use them they're dead. They're dead. They work great when they're fully charged, but you better prepare them day before you need them. When I was preparing Thanksgiving, I went to the cabinet that I store them in. Pulled them out, opened the app and removed every one of them. Every last one was dead as a doornail.
I use mostly thermpro timers and thermometers. This wireless one lasted only 2 months with daily use.

Ive had this for about a year and a half it worked great ive used it several times but this morning I got a brisket ready to smoke for Easter dinner and the probe wont stay charged. Kind of disappointing id hoped a 60 dollar meat probe would last longer.
Still trying to set it up. When I finally get it I will update

review_title: Easy to use, terribly long time constant makes it useless for smaller/shorter cooks
review_text: I really wanted to like this device. Good price, reputable company, relatively simple/uncomplicated app that doesn't require BS like an account signup and has the basic features like a temp graph one would expect for this kind of product. Unfortunately, I tried it on multiple occasions with smaller cuts of meat that required relatively short (6-12 minutes) cooking time, and every time the thermometer was woefully inaccurate. In each case it was so far off what I expected based on cook time that I used my instant-read thermometer to check things, and in each case it was reading about 25-35ºF lower than the instant-read at the same point. Since I bought this to bolster my confidence cooking smaller cuts in my kitchen, this makes it pretty useless. I think the problem is that it has either an intrinsic or software-imposed thermal time constant that is too long for small cuts and short cooks. I did a quick experiment, where I took this and its replacement (Chef IQ spike) and observed their response times when placed in actively boiling water. This thermometer took over 2 minutes to read over 200ºF, and never read above 203ºF over 3 minutes of observation. The other thermometer took about 15s to read 210ºF. I don't love the other unit's app, and would have preferred for this to work, but accuracy has to come first.

review_title: I really had high hopes for this
review_text: I really had high hopes for this. In the beginning it sort of worked but it had trouble pairing with our phones and the alarm would go off when the meat wasn’t even close. Eventually I just got tired of trying to use it and tossed it in a drawer for a while going back to my accurate wired old school thermometer. I decided to try to give it another try but this time it was completely useless. Updated it but then it was impossible to connect, it kept giving error readings and absolutely would not hold a charge and was just overall frustrating to use. Gave up and tossed it. This was a while ago so hopefully they can work out whatever bugs are going on.
We’ve had this for 2 years now but after 3 uses it quit working. The probe never charges. Wished we could’ve enjoyed it longer.

It worked well for the short time it worked. I rarely used it and it stopped charging after less than 2 years. I see other mentions of this now and wish I'd seen them when I bought it. I probably used it 15 find before it quit working. Invest a couple bucks more and get one that lasts.

Why 5 stars on the details and only 3 for a general review??? PROS: The thermometer is accurate.. at least enough for my purposes. I double check with a good instant read in multiple places while this probe can only check one spot. I also like the fact that this probe checks both the meat and the ambient temp inside the smoker. No wires connected to an outside reader. CONS: Only one probe whereas my other can take up to 6 probes at one time. It would be cost prohibitive to buy even four probes, IMO. I may cook a few meats at once and I often like to have two probes in a product. I don't even know if one could use multiple probes with this product. The only real con I have is the Bluetooth. When set up in my Cookshack or Traeger smokers and my phone is close to the smoker (less than 10') it seemed to work well. However, when I walked to my office which is only about 30' away.. it would work for about an hour or less and then the alarms would go off due to lost connection. Sadly, I ultimately I returned it.
I really enjoyed mine.... but the probe stopped charging after 2hr.

I used this to smoke a brisket over the weekend on an offset smoker. The probe was working as expected, range and battery life wise. However, the app experience was pretty lousy. I used the Android version on Samsung Note 10. App connected fine, and it requires several permissions, which I gave. The app starts fine, sets up alerts, and recording etc. However, it stops even though I had given permissions for it to not be killed by Android to save power. I ended up having to restart it and reconnect it 4 times for a 8 hour cook, and the longest I got without the app stopping was about 4 hours. I figured that was okay since I had the individual sessions recorded, with may be 30 mins or so missed overall, so I could still analyze my progress in the history. But to add to my pain, the app ended up deleting all my recordings abruptly. In the end, I had no record of my brisket cook at all! I am still debating with myself if I should return the thermometer. It's a shame since the hardware seems to work just fine out of the box and I had no accuracy, connectivity or range issues.

review_title: Good probe for the meats but some issues
review_text: Temperature *Internal temperature is accurate within a degree or 2 *Ambient temperature - I have tried to position the spike in many different ways and the ambient temperature is useless. Had it sitting next to 2 different old school grate thermometers and this thing is always 100 or more degrees off even by end of cook. *The app is ok. It does display what is needed although I wish it would keep better logging. There is no way to close the app without going into phone settings and force closing it. It always stays open. There were some complaints about this in app store with absolutely no responses. This is for iphone and several different Android brands. This is an annoying issue. *Range is decent but definitely not 500ft in real world usage. This 500ft must have been measured in an open field with no other devices. 50-75 ft more accurate of you live in a house with walls or use other devices. For the price it is the least complicated probe on the market if all you wanna do is monitor internal temp and get an alarm on your phone when the meat is done and you don't get to far away from it . Fix the app, fix the ambient and allow for WiFi connection and this would be a great device.

I have the MEATER probe but I was hoping that the TempSpike would provide the ability to see the ambient temp all the time. On the MEATER it only displays above 150 which is higher than for sous vide. Well the Tempspike DOES show the ambient temp as long as it is above 122 but everything else about the app is not so great. For example on the MEATER you can pull up an interactive line graph to see the internal and ambient temp over time, you cannot do this with the Tempspike. Additionally, the Tempspike's preset temps do not account for passive cooking after you pull your item from the heat source, so everything WILL be overdone unless you adjust this. The MEATER probe accounts for passive cooking and tells you when yo pull your item based on what it is.... and there might be some sort of algorithm that also determines when to pull based on how long it took the time to rise. I am saying this because the time to pull is not the same for different items. Anyway - Tempspike is good. I like that it alerts from the base (although it does sound like a fire alarm) when stuff is ready but that is probably the only benefit over the MEATER.

review_title: Probe tend to not hold a charge…
review_text: Just sharing my experience after having this for a year.  It worked great the first time I charged it up.  Problem is, and you can surf Reddit to see that its just not me, the probe tends to either not charge, or discharge in the base.  I leave it on the base and charge the base up monthly.  When I go to do a cook, the base is fully charged but the probe is dead.  So if you want to dick around the night before and make sure the probe is charged, this works fine.  But, forget to do that and you will be disappointed when it comes time to cook.

I've had this temp probe a little over two years now. I'm done with it. It's pretty consistent with the meat temperature. The ambient temperature has never been right. I thought I would live with it since my smoker has an electronic temp gauge and mechanical. The battery life is not good for long cooks(the only time I use it). To the trash it goes.

I wrote an 'indifferent' review on this TempSpike. Which involved original purchasing this device. It works great but I'm not sure it has a unobstructed 500 ft range. I haven't had a chance to test it And it doesn't matter. It's not needed, from my perspective. So I made this comment on a FB post and I was almost immediately, contacted concerning this issue. That's an absolute A+ and that goes a very long way with me. They explained a few things and sent me out of replacement. Again, I haven't really tested the 500 ft range. Aside from that, this device incredible. It's fairly cheaper than it's apparent competition. It's worth buying. I got a deal on it. Love this thing. So I was having issue with the replacement when I got it. And that's my fault because I assumed I didn't need to read the directions. My mistake. If you're in the market for a meat probe, this is your choice. They will take care of you if you have an issue. You're in good hands.

I’ve used it in my Ninja woodfire and my regular oven. Makes it easier to monitor cooking. Update: 8/2026. it stopped working on the app. The app no longer shows ambient or food temp. I disconnected; deleted and downloaded app again, paired it and still nothing.

Bought twice. Worked great for about a year then stopped, contacted thermopro and they sent out a replacement that has worked off and on after about 2 months. App is very easy and great to use, but I cannot justify purchasing for a 3rd time.

I had high hopes for this wireless cooking thermometer but it is so inaccurate that it is completely useless. I tested it with two different NIST calibrated thermometers roasting a chicken in a 350° F oven and discovered the new thermometer was reading 100 degrees low on the ambient temperature, and 10 degrees low on the meat side. And yes I did insert the probe into the meat past the line on the probe per instructions. The thermometer was fully charged and inserted correctly, not touching bone and in the thickest part of the breast. I make my living using accurate thermometers so trust me when I say this one is a complete waste of money.

I bought this thinking that it would be money well spent for cooking barbecue instead of getting a popular brand more expensive. However, what I found is that it's hard to get it to work sometimes and the interface is kind of glitchy at least from what I found. So maybe it needs an update? I don't know but having to do it all over again. I probably would have got the name brand popular meat thermometer

review_title: Great but bluetooth distance srinks fast
review_text: At first the Bluetooth from thermometer to booster was standard 30 to 50 ft and then the same from booster to phone and I absolutely loved this thing and would say it was perfect. Well 3 months down the road and the Bluetooth to booster distance is down to 5 to 10 ft and the same as before for the booster to phone with no change in my smoker or its location. Other than that its great. I wish the app would give the running in the background alert everytime u minimize the app or turn the screen off and u have to drag the alert down onethe screen and push it back up on my Samsung phone to get it off the top of ur screen. Just let it run in the background and sound the alarm when its set

review_title: Good concept, needs to be better.
review_text: Pros: Easy to use App functionality is great Alarming function works great Internal temp is accurate Battery life is good, 12+ hours on a full charge Cons: Bluetooth connectivity is rough, if you are more than 15 feet away and on the other side of a wall, you will lose connection. Ambient temperature is wildly inaccurate. It takes hours for the ambient temperature to read anywhere near where it should be. Usually settles out 20-40 degrees lower than other sensing devices. Overall this device works well for the cost and I'm glad I bought it. If you can get over the fact that you can't be more than 20 feet away from the device without losing connection, and the ambient temperature not working, it is a good wireless thermometer. Hopefully the next version has wifi capability.

I bought two of these. One has worked okay most of the time, but the second one barely worked at all. It only connected a few times before having charging issues, and now it won’t connect at all. I’m reviewing now because it showed up again while I was searching for a new thermometer, and I won’t be buying this one again. I did email TempSpike about the problem but never heard back.

I had a great experience with this product and wanted to love it, except for one thing. The app worked really well, the temperature seemed accurate, and the battery was great. The 500' range is simply deceptive. I felt trapped within a 10'-20' radius of my smoker for the whole day. It's one thing to be able to check from anywhere, but really was just looking to be able to stay connected while moving around the house doing other things. It turns out the range is only achievable with the lid open and 0 obstructions, and even then, I doubt it would get anywhere close to 500'. Had it been advertised as something more realistic like 40', I probably would not be upset, but also would not have bought it in the first place. I returned the product and bought something that is Bluetooth and wi-fi compatible, since I have learned that Bluetooth-alone ranges cannot be trusted.
Off by 30-40 deg F (probe and ambient) . And batteries don't last that long. Not happy after about 4 times using two probes. Both are off on temp accuracy. Disappointing product.
It's honestly really nice, but the app is crap. And if ANYTHING happens, your phone will scream, and it's really annoying.

Definitely helpful but has a few flaws. It's good for using to track progress of the cook and helping maintain cooking temperature. Downside is that the temps may be off slightly and the spike itself will discharge in the charging base so you have to reconnect it the night before your cook. Make sure too double check your temperatures with an insta-probe as you get closer to your target.

I am totally doing over my review. I have had the TempSpike for a while now. This model the TempSpike 500 the original one is NOT accurate; it is off by at least 10 degrees sometimes 13 degrees. I was sent another and same issue. I will say the customer service is outstanding and the people are super nice. With this said, they have a new model the Plus. This is the one that goes up to 600 feet. That I cannot confirm or deny if that is accurate, but I can say the temp is accurate. I have tested with a reliable external Thermometer on 3 separate occasions comparing the two different ones in the same cut of meat in the same thickness. I then used the external to make sure was accurate and was either dead on or off by 1 degree every time. It is worth getting the newer one. Always double check with an external if you want to make sure

review_title: Ok for low and slow smoking and roasting
review_text: Useful for low and slow in the smoker or oven roasts. Fat thermometer is too slow to respond to use for fast cooking things like steaks or pork chops; 500 degree limit also means it can’t really be used in anything on a grill. Also, probe died after a year, now won’t connect at all.

review_title: Won't charge anymore and did not send signal to phone once 20-30 feet away from the base.
review_text: Definitely does not work "500 feet" as my grill is about 50 feet from my kitchen. The base has to be very close to the grille and I got coverage on the phone from about 20 feet away inside (it's a wood frame wall there, not even CBS) or I lose reception. And ... the thermometer will not charge or connect to app anymore. Reset everything, followed instructions repeatedly.

review_title: Not the easiest to use - uncertain about accuracy
review_text: I still am not certain if this works or not. I have had many failures and it seems to be where the probe sits in the meat. You have to insert it up to a line on the probe, about 3-4 inches up, or the instructions say the probe could get damaged in the oven. However, if you have a smaller cut of meat, like a pork loin, that can be a challenge if you want it to read the temperature in the center. Also, either my oven temp is very off, or the external temperature is not correct. I still need to determine that. I bought an instant read at the same time as this one, as I felt like my current thermometer may not be accurate. I put all 3 in a glass of hot water and got 3 different temperatures. It is anyone's guess which is correct, if any are.

I have used it four times and it worked great for thick cut large meat! But there are some issues: 1) I find the lights confusing. Blink slow, blink fast, etc. 2) you have to make sure the connectors on the proble are in full contact and clean with the case. My last usage the probe wasn't charged and the blue tooth connection light was blinking red. I thought it wasn't connected to the phone but it was the probe. It would be nice the app indicated the probe wasn't connected. 3) the app is OK but it would be nice to have complete battery and connection status 4) the length of the probe is long for proper insert into the meat. So items like chicken breast cannot be read since the probe will not be properly inserted. This also holds true for thin cut meat.
They seem to work overall but the probe itself hasnt seemed to actually hold a charge well.

review_title: Great product, but only worked about a year.
review_text: Worked great right up to the warranty expiration.

When the Bluetooth connects this thermometer works great. We've successfully used it in a smoker and in the oven and it is surprisingly easy to clean. However, getting it to connect to my wife's iPhone or my android is a nightmare. Make sure you have a full battery because if you don't it definitely won't connect. As it is I'm usually ready to give up and use an old candy thermometer when it finally connects. Makes me wonder if the connectivity issue is part of the reason why the newer models have digital readouts on them.

review_title: Very good tool for shorter cook times
review_text: This product has been helpful in my meat smoking journey. It is accurate and the features are so helpful—especially Bluetooth connectivity. One complaint makes it only a fair to good product—the probes don’t hold a long enough charge for cook times of over six hours. Brisket and Pork butt both were longer, and even some smaller cuts were as well, and my probe simply ran out of juice.
