You might have to have 2 probes so when one runs out of power, you out in the other one. I purchased this one year ago, and 3 months later it failed to work. I called the company and they sent a replacement which has worked well.

review_title: Great idea, not accurate or calbratable.
review_text: Great packaging, app not bad but inaccurate. Mine was about 25-40 degrees F off from internal Temps when tested against 3 other digital thermometers which all were within 2 degrees of each other. Ambient was 40-50 d F different again with 3+ digital and analog thermometers which were all within 5 d F of each other. I can accept some difference but > 5-10 degrees consistently is not okay by me. These are gadgets, imo, for people who are grilling/ smoking/ cooking even as a hobby but want to produce best possible product/ easiest way but I'm not risking over or under cooking something due to faulty thermometers when I have other known good ones in my pantry. I did order the chef iq as I like the wireless capabilities of this unit. My others are older cabled models and a taylor quick read thermometer.

While the internal temperature portion of the probe works great (Within 2-3 degrees of other probes) the ambient temp is off by a lot. I have it in the smoker right now and the smokers built in probe, a 3rd party probe and and analog probe all show 245-250 deg. The ambient temp on the probe shows 175. I have also noticed that it slowly increases with the internal temp. My thought is that there is no thermal break between the two halves of the probe and the meat is keeping the ambient temp probe from accurately ready. Before anyone comments its in to far I have the probe in just beyond the small line where you must install the probe at least to avoid damage to the probe. the app is also a little janky, but that can easily change over time.

I love the idea of what this is! I love having the wireless temp probe and being able to check on my smokes so I don't have to open the smoker as frequently. Only downfall is my probe battery doesn't last the time of the cook... when I used it this last weekend, the probe only lasted about 3-4 hrs... not long enough for a brisket cook. I also sometimes have trouble with the probe fully charging. Because of the time limits on the probe, I am limited to what I can use this with when I cook.
Worked great for about a year. Nice app and easy to use. It stopped charging the probe and became useless. I probably got 20 long cooks out of it before it decided to RIP.

review_title: Thought it was good until the second cook
review_text: The first time I tried the product on my rotisserie I had nothing bad to say other than it didn’t live up to the 500 ft promise. I was getting disconnected at less than 150Ft. Then the second cook happened. Spatchcock chicken in the oven set at 350. The ambient temp never registered more than 270 and when the meter said 165 internal, the chicken still looked raw and after verification with a probe thermometer, thermpro was off by 25 degrees. I verified with two probe thermometers one happens to be thermpro probe thermometer, and it was way off internal. UPDATE: Seller reached out and provided full refund. I also own another Thermpro Model TP27 that I am very happy with and I am glad to know the company stands by their product.
Probe battery only charges to 50%
Nice app, like the graph function Downside: probe battery failed after 1 year (just outside the warranty). Range of booster to smartphone poor. Go for WiFi instead.
Not as accurate as my other ones

review_title: Great except for battery life issues
review_text: I am on the fence. Right out of the box, I loved this thing. I use it with my offset smoker to gove me freedom to do things around the house without sitting and babysitting the fire (as much) all day. The app is great and user friendly. I love the options to have various settings and custom cooks. I love that the docking station beeps very loudly and your phone notifies you if the ambient temp (that you can customize to your preferences!) gets too low or too high. I love that it alerts me when the customizable temp of the food is getting close and when it hits the target. The cook time estimates are never very accurate but I don’t care about that. I have enough experience smoking meat to know what’s going on. Using this just gives me some freedom and peace of mind, especially during a long smoke. So, like I said - right out the box - great product. 5 stars. After about 3 months of use I noticed the probe’s battery life went from being about 18 hours to fully dying in 4-6 hours. Within another 1-2 months it wasn’t even lasting 1-2 hours. I contacted the company via email asking if perhaps I was doing something wrong or if this was a known defect. I really didn’t expect anything in return. I loved the product and had planned to buy another but wanted to know how to protect the next one. They said that shouldn’t be happening and very generously sent me their newest model free of charge. I was blown away and so grateful. 10/10 customer service. That’s something that will make a person keep coming back! Unfortunately, the new product they sent was much worse than the original. The functionality was the same but right out of the box the probe battery only lasted about 6 hours from a full charge. After 3 uses, the battery didn’t even make it an hour before it died. I didn’t want to contact customer service again because I didn’t want to seem like I was just trying to get free products. I also don’t want to risk spending more money on a product that may only last a few uses. Honestly I would pay for it again if it lasted 6 months+ with a decent battery life like the first one I purchased but I can’t justify the cost for 3-5 uses like the one I was given as a replacement. I’m giving this 3 stars because the first device I had was fantastic when it worked well and customer service is top notch. If I was judging solely based on the second device I received (and if I paid for it), it would onlu be one star. So balance, I guess. Sadly, I am still on the hunt for a better option. I bought the Ninja Pro and while it technically works it doesn’t even come close to the functionality and convenience of the TempPro app. I may be back at some point to try them out again because I really loved the first device. I hope they can fix their battery life issues.
This probe thermometer works ok. We use it for smoking meat and it does not hold a charge long enough to use for the whole smoke. It also takes forever to charge.
The range on this is not great. I used it once.
The probe battery life does not last very long. Recharge after every use.  You’d be better off just leaving it on the charger at all times, because it will die when not in use, as well.

review_title: Charging process can be hit or miss.
review_text: I've had mine for about 2 years. ThermPro replaced the original once as it would not hold a charge. The replacement has degraded too. If you are doing a cook, plan ahead and put the unit on a charger well ahead of time. Don't be fooled if the charging light is not blinking. Slightly spin the probe in the base and the charging will likely resume. This routine is necessary even if you charge the unit after the previous cook. While proper use of the probe will greatly improve your results, the question of whether the unit will be sufficiently charged is always a source of anxiety. Planning is critical as when the unit works, the cook is nearly foolproof.
Loved the product while it lasted. It worked for about a year and then stopped. Won't even hold a charge. Very disappointed.
Alarm goes off long before food reaches set internal temperature

This model worked ok for me but just after the warranty period it would not hold a charge for more than three hours, which is of little help when doing something like a brisket. Then about a month later it would not pair with the base. Not really that impressed with the app either, it had a tendency to glitch all the time. I won't be buying this one again, but instead am going to buy the one that has a stand alone screen and better reviews. I don't need to be able to see it on my phone if the screen is portable and has better range.
Was working great for a 5 uses on long smokes, accurate Temp control. It ran out of battery mid smoke, and now I can't get it to reconnect to Bluetooth on my phone.

review_title: Works well, but limited battery life
review_text: If you're smoking something that doesn't take all day, this works very well. Its weakness is that its battery, at fully charged, never lasts longer than five hours, and as it ages, the battery life gets less and less. I've had mine about a year, and it never lasts longer than three hours now, after having been charged overnight. It is useless if you're smoking a brisket, for example.

review_title: Great to start but failed before two years of service
review_text: I would have given this thermometer 5 stars for the first 1.5 years of usage. Unfortunately, the thermometer has failed before hitting the two year mark.
Was great when it was working but didn’t even last 2 years. Had it for 14 months and now the device won’t charge
Worked pretty good for 3 cooks. Then I pulled it out of the drawer months later and it was dead. So I charged it up and it never worked again.

review_title: You get what you pay for
review_text: For the money, this probe is OK at best. First off it’s a large probe compared to the competitors, so if you’re cooking a relatively thin steak, around 1” or so, it’s difficult to fit the probe in the side of the steak. The range is advertised to be 500 feet. I lose signal around 200 feet with minimal obstructions. That’s with the base next to the grill. The app is OK. Fairly user friendly. The predictive cooking time estimate is fairly accurate but takes a while to establish. The max safe temp is 625° so you can’t really sear a steak over charcoal or run the risk of damaging the probe. You will get a high temp warning. The battery life is not great. I have to charge it frequently. I went with this probe hoping the range would be better than the MEATER. Unfortunately I believe I was wrong. I wish I bought the MEATER due to the thinner probe and better app interface. I will continue to use this probe for smoking large meats on my pellet smoker, but I am looking into other probes like the Thermoworks RFX.

The meat temp was good, the alarm went off when we hit the preset temp and when I was supposedly out of range. The bluetooth range wasn't as advertised and the ambient temperature was low with a range of 40-50 degrees low. For these reasons, I returned the item.

review_title: Short life! Not for Brisket! Only lasts 2-3 hours
review_text: Short life! Not for Brisket! Only lasts 2-3 hours then it’s dead! So I use it only to measure through the stall!
It works well with the app, but base station connection to phone drops at about 75 feet even with clear line of sight.

review_title: Battery is dead a year and a half later
review_text: Can’t get base or spike to hold a charge a year later.

review_title: Wireless thermometer must be placed into food item 2.5" in and is rather thick
review_text: I want to take off 2 stars because I didn't realize it was so thick and you had to stick it in pretty far (compared to the wired thermometers, which are much thinner, and you can just stick the tip in). However, not having to deal with the wires, and not having to worry the weather will destroy the base unit, almost makes up for these issues. For chicken drumsticks and fish, it's almost too big to use. Chicken drumsticks, I use the skin to cover up to the line, and it usually works; have to be careful the tip isn't too close to the surface either. The one time I wasn't careful (it was still covered by the meat), it read as being 180 degrees, but the chicken was probably closer to 130, given how raw it looked (which I only noticed too late, after the kids had eaten it... the kids didn't even notice how raw it was... kids...) Fish I sometimes just use a wired thermometer rather than try to jam the thing in all the way and stay in the center of the thin filet. I do like that it lets you know ambient temperature, so sometimes I've noticed my gas grill has gone out because I see the temperature dropping. Definitely with rain or the hot sun, wireless is a plus because trying to fiddle with a makeshift cover for the base is no fun. If they had different colored sticks, that would make it worth buying other ones, but trying to keep track of multiple sticks without a convenient way of identifying them has deterred me from buying more. Also, if most of the things you grill are small, then it's not worth buying. (If you're doing chicken nuggets or cheese sticks on the grill.) Update December 2024: I'm taking off a star because the end has got a little bit of patina from being in the barbecue, so it doesn't connect very well anymore to charge. I have to keep turning it so it eventually gets a contact to charge but just moving the base unit can disconnect it, so basically the probe runs out of battery if you don't check it regularly. The battery life has been affected now, and I only bought this is April. There are other wireless probes on the market where the protected portion connects to charge so it shouldn't have this issue. Unfortunately you can't just buy a new probe so once the probe battery dies, you'll have to buy the entire unit again, even though the base is still usable

review_title: Worked with phone app right out of box
review_text: Once charged complete, it hooks up to app in phone and works. With very few steps. I bought several others like this, but always could not get heat probe to synce with phone app and work. I haven't done a 3 to 4lb roast yet, but using it so far I think it's gonna be a game changer in my future large meat cooks. Recommend this unit , at least it worked right out of box.

review_title: Great temp sensor don’t trust the ambient sensor
review_text: I like the app and the accuracy of the internal temp but the ambient temp sensor is off as much as 40F. I confirmed this with 3 different readings. Oven thermometer, analog grill thermometer, the temp sensor on my grill all reading around 240-245F while the ambient sensor on the probe reads 195-205. Otherwise it’s a great product

This is a nice product. I don't use it often but when i do it is very simple to connect to and it seems to work well.. My biggest complaints are that the spike is rather thick so probably not the best option for smaller cuts of meat like drumsticks or even something like salmon. the other issue is the Bluetooth, I would almost rather have it come with its owned screened interface than hook to my phone. all of the comments you read about the Bluetooth is true. from one end of my house to to the next it will disconnect. with that said, its not a huge inconvenience for the Bluetooth to cut out as it auto reconnects when it is within range and I really dont need to have a constant reading on what i am cooking. i can simply just walk back into range and check on it. My honest opinion is that I WOULD recommend this device to others if they are interested in something like this. Personally, I will probably never buy another one. do not get me wrong, its a really cool product but there are much cheaper options that do just as well of a job if not better.

review_title: Works great, but a couple things..
review_text: After the first time I used this, I stored it in a drawer unplugged with the spike in the cradle. When I went to use it after sitting for about a month or so, the spike battery was dead. I recharged it and was back up to 100% after about an hour or so…..I guess you have to leave it plugged into the USB charger or remember to take it out well in advance to recharge the spike, I have used this a couple of times now with excellent results, 17lb turkey came out perfect and was set for 165……The ambient temp however appears to be reporting low. I had the oven at 450 for the first hour and it never went over 375. Then turned the oven down to 325 and it reported 285. Sent an email to customer support about the spike battery and have not heard back. Update: Received a response about a week later and they offered some support and a full replacement if needed,

Several months back I received my wireless thermometer from Thermopro and it worked well for several grilling sessions. It developed a problem wherein the probe wouldn’t sync with the booster base. I took a chance that I could get some customer support and get things working again. Less than 24 hours after I sent the email, I was told by the customer service representative that a replacement was in the mail! I assumed it would be a new probe, but they sent me an entirely new replacement. It’s companies like this that earn my repeat business and not to mention this review. Having products arrive defective or break months later is regrettable, but it’s even more regrettable to do business with folks who don’t stand behind their product like Thermopro The TempSpike works as advertised and the reason I only give 4 stars is due to the short battery life of the booster. I have to make sure I charge it prior to using it or els the battery will likely die halfway through your cook.

Works quite well and really great that it does not require wires. The challenge is that I have not been able to turn it off but I did figure out that once I use it, if you then charge the device, it eventually shuts off on its own once it is fully charged.

Something is off, either with the ambient temperature probe or the thermostat/thermometer on our oven. I had to try it out after getting it. We opted for a pork tenderloin. Preheated the oven to 350°. Placed the Tempspike in the meat (past the notch) and placed it in the oven. According to the app, the oven's ambient temperature never exceeded 318°. The oven was brand new when we purchased the house a year ago. I have cooked many dishes in it. Baking, broiling, proofing bread (it has that function), braising, roasting, etc. I never had any reason to believe the oven's thermostat was off. I believe my only option is to order a replacement and test the ambient temperature again. The internal temperature appeared to be accurate. The tenderloin was cooked perfectly so there is that. UPDATE: The company reached out to me and replaced the defective device. Replacement was acceptably accurate. 2nd UPDATE: While smoking my previous brisket, with about an hour of cooking left, the app kept telling me I needed an update to the app. I couldn't find one. The probe kept disconnecting after about 5 minutes. I had used a hand held to make sure the brisket was done. I tried them again this 4th of July. Same thing. Would not maintain a connection. Never got a stable connection nor could I get a reading. I went to the store and bought another thermometer. I can say now that the temp spike is nothing more than an ugly paperweight. It's going in the trash.

The product worked good for few times I used it but after leaving it in drawer I was dead after a month .charged it up and worked for about 1 hr then wouldn't connect with probe I repaired it cleaned it charged and reset it,I would drop everytime I used it won't hold charge I did this as a update I reached out to customer support 2cweeks ago explained they sent me a new one but the "new one" appears to be a used replacement it had a crack on the side the type c port was dirty and the top of the case was all scratched up like some one stored it in a drawer rubbing against the bottom and had lint on it but the box was taped up .feel they sent me someone else not working product

review_title: Great probe, but needs more battery life
review_text: This thing is great for my smoker. I no longer have to try and pass 2 probe wires through the grommet in the side. The only issue I have is that the battery doesn't last long enough. Sure, it lasts the length of time the brisket is in the smoker, but it goes dead during the cooler rest. It needs maybe 2-4 more hours of battery life. The app is nice, but needs work better integrating with Android. The probe reached its setpoint while I was sleeping, and the app didn't notify me. Yes, I've put it on the list of apps allowed to send notifications during do not disturb. The app was open when I went to sleep... Android closed it out. I got lucky that I woke up at 4am and got a notification when I opened the app back up. Surprise, it past the set point probably 30 minutes ago. The other complaint I have is that it's Bluetooth instead of WiFi. Need to run to the store during a cook? Prepare for the app to scream at you that it's lost connection.

I've been using this Temp Spike for a couple of months now and find it pretty good, except the probe is quite large and it's required to insert it several inches to have it operate properly. The battery usually needs to be recharged prior to use...remember to do that. Also, and a bummer, it won't work in my new Traeger smoker...the Traeger apparently has too thick of a steel surrounding for the Bluetooth signal to penetrate. The Temp Spike works great in the kitchen oven and the app is fairly straightforward. Maybe the newer, more expensive, model is better??? OK, now that I've read the manual I see that you're supposed to place the booster near the TempSpike to increase the Bluetooth signal. I fully charged the spike and booster and it now works in my Traeger. RTFM!

review_title: Works well with some slight connectivity to app issues
review_text: This works well and the temps match pretty closely with those from a digital quick read thermometer. The app works well and allows for customizable target temp settings, (and also has several presets) for different meats. Everything is easy to charge (place the spike into the receiver unit and charge it all at once, with a simple micro USB charger) and it seems to hold the charges very well. The issue I have is that it tends to lose connection with the app pretty easily. This is with the repeater unit placed less than 15 feet from the spike, and the phone with app being within 30 feet of the repeater unit, just from one room to another. Seems this unit has trouble with signal getting through the older walls, in my home. I read a review, after the fact, that mentions the same thing, so, this appears to be an issue in older homes/suburban areas with brick and thick plaster walls. This may not necessarily be a fault of the unit but, as part of an honest review, I decided to include it. Other than this one issue, I like this thermometer and have used it a few times so far, with pretty good results.

Overall this is a nice product from ThermoPro and will replace my older wireless ThermoPro that I have had for a few years. The fact it can monitor both meat and pit temperature is nice, however, the fact that you have to insert 3 inches of the probe into the meat can be a challenge in some circumstances. Also, since you cannot put the probe on the pit without it being in meat, you will still need the older wireless one to bring you pit up to temperature. Once that happens, and provided you have a large enough piece of meat you are cooking, this works well. The app is straightforward and has alarms for when you are approaching target temp, etc. For cleaning, I let it cool and then wipe it down with an alcohol wipe before storing it away. The Booster does not have an on/off switch or battery indicator (maybe it's in the app but I did not see it?), so I make sure to charge it overnight before a cook, or in a pinch have attached a portable battery bank to it via the USB-C port. A clear power off switch would be nice because otherwise it doesn't seem to know when a cook is done and it's been removed from the meat, and will blink various LEDs to indicate status, even when just sitting in a drawer.

I had problems getting the probe to take a full charge, so I emailed Tempspike. Without the slightest hesitation, they asked for my address to send me a new one. Well, they didn't just replace the probe, they sent a complete new unit, base and probe. At least if you run into issues, Tempspike is VERY quick to resolve them. Kudos to them. I'd only take a half star off if I could. Yes I had a problem with their unit, but they took care of it quickly and without question.

I own a Meater+ which has been rife with issues. The probe won't hold a charge and eats AAA batteries, connecting their probe is problematic every single time, and I was fed up with it enough that I bought a Thermopro wireless. Right out of the box, it's not a pretty as the Meater, but I love that it has an internal rechargeable battery. The app setup is easy and seamless, connecting the probe is super easy and once paired, the probe connects without issue. The probe stays connected throughout the cook, which the meater never did. The only thing the Meater does that I can't find yet on the thermopro is factor in resting times to the desired temps. That's easily corrected by taking whatever you're cooking off the heat source a few minutes early. Not a big deal. Overall, I like this device a lot and I can't wait to use it more now that grilling season is coming!

Had this for about a year now, and I would love to give this five stars - it's neat (no wires!), fairly accurate (ish), and the app is pretty simple to use. My primary issue is the battery life for the probe. There's no way I can use this for a long, all-day smoke; the probe battery conks out after only a few hours. Only way to charge it is to put it back in the booster, and needless to say, you're not really monitoring your meats while it's recharging. I've learned to only use this for the second half of the smoke (e.g. after the stall on pork butts), and check the meats earlier in the session via a Therma Pop or Pen. Also, the ambient temp is sometimes off quite a bit. But besides that, it's a great little tool.
I didn’t expect 500 ft but it’s more like 30 . Still does what I need . Nothing special just does the job .

After reading the reviews like everyone else it leaves you questioning your choice. I work as a calibration tech and so naturally I had to perform a calibration for everyone. This is a wet bath calibrator so what your seeing is me testing the probe insert side and ambient side with another calibrated probe. Well........ yes the insertion side for your food was accurate to within a half a degree which is pretty standard in the commercial industry. But....... the ambient side was 10-12 degrees off. I did suspect this might happen and the reason is I believe the heat from the insertion to your food side is radiating over to the ambient side. When laying the probe out entirely to ambient it is accurate. As long as you factor this in while cooking you'll be fine. Obviously we all are buying this for wireless food side accuracy. For $50 some dollars I'd say it's just fine and no buyers remorse. I did not test the range to my phone yet.

This thermometer is awesome to say the least. Temps are spot on, the ambient temp probe makes for charcoal smoking a breeze since I can monitor the temps and not trust the dome thermometer. Only issue I have had is charging- when the probe sits in the dock, it makes contact on two different places to charge the probe. The probe on the back where the ambient temp is read would not sit firmly against contact on the back of the dock, thus causing it to die instead of not charge. Found this out in the middle of a brisket cook. The ambient probe can get dirty just from smoke and heat, which will also cause it to not make contact and not charge. I scrubbed it with a copper brush and it removed it fairly easily.

review_title: More Convenient than Wired Versions but with Temp Lag
review_text: Used this on a turkey and a rib roast. Temperature pretty accurate overall and easy to use. No issues with connectivity. I’ve noticed that there is a bit of a lag time between the read temperature on the meat and the actual temperature. I’ve adjusted by pulling the meat from the oven/roaster earlier to allow the rest period for the thermometer to catch up. For example on a recent rib roast (which I like rare (125F) to medium rare (130F)). I pulled the roast at 118F and tented it with foil. As it sat on the counter, I watched the temperature coast up to 133F. A 25 degree rise during resting seems a bit much, so I believe it’s due to a lag time in the temperature readings. Otherwise, I found the thermometer to be very useful. Have yet to try on a brisket in the smoker which will take a longer time to cook.

review_title: Great product, once you find the instructions....
review_text: Strangely, the device didn't ship with ANY instructions. Had to look up online the name of the brand and then go to their site to find instructions as to what app to use to download to my phone....fortunately it IS in the play store and verified but you'd think they would put that in the box somewhere...Reminds me of the first printers that advertised themselves as being USB but didn't include an actual USB cable...um ok... but that aside, i used it a couple times for some simple foods (chicken, a small roast, turkey burgers) and they turned out very well using the alarming function to tell me once the inside temp had reached a specific temp...normally we err on the side of safety and and up over cooking the heck out of our food but with this little gadget we get perfectly cooked meat without it drying out from being over cooked.

Waffled for quite awhile on buying a ambient and internal probe in one as I felt they were all overpriced, considering most had mediocre reviews and cons that outweigh the pros, when compared to other wired probes with a wifi connection. My biggest concerns are range and accuracy and the TempSpike is pretty good at both. I don’t lose the connection throughout my 3200sf home, which is a pleasant surprise and it was within degree of my thermapen when checking a steak during a reverse sear. Price during their promo was also close to 50% off which made this worth a try. The downsides IMO are the lack of wifi and the ambient part of the probe which is slow to respond compared to my wired wifi therm. It also doesn’t graph the ambient, which would be a nice feature if it can be added. Overall, solid version of this concept that seems to address some of the concerns of its competitors.

I've used it a few times, but you have to remember to keep it charged before you want to use it. It's relatively accurate, close enough more or less. The default alert to let you know it's reached the desired temperature sounds like a home fire alarm, so you'll want to change it to something more appropriate to avoid the confusion of trying to silence your fire alarms when it goes off. A simple instant read thermometer would be much more sensible and accurate, but not as fun.

review_title: First one - dead on arrival. Replacement worked perfectly
review_text: Might end up being a 5 star rating, but I haven't actually cooked with it yet. The first order I received for this item was dead on arrival. Could not get the temp spike paired with it's booster (the base). The replacement they sent worked immediately as expected. I tested it out on my hot tub and temp reading was spot on. Hopefully, it will do as well with meats. ;-)

I have been using wireless thermometers for years, but wanted something that would report directly to my smartphone instead of having wires running out the smoker to a transmitter with a receiver setup somewhere in range. Being able to check on the temperature working in either the living room or kitchen (both of which are well within the BlueTooth range) was a solid plus. The setup was very simple, internal temps were verified with a Thermapen thermometer and were dead on cooking large chicken thighs. The "estimated time to finish" was close and a nice feature. I'll see how it does with a long smoke in a chunk of meat that stalls. For a first use, it went very well. I'm looking forward to more and heavier uses before summer ends.

EDIT: they sent me a replacement thermometer and I have had no further problems! Works great every time. So convenient for grilling or even in the oven! Worked great….twice….now the thermometer no longer connects to the booster rendering it absolutely useless. I should have heeded the other reviews and gone with a different product

As a probe thermometer, this is a great value. The internal temp is accurate which is pretty much all I care about. However, there are a couple things that could be better. The first would be the ambient temperature. I’ve found it to just be completely inaccurate. I’ve used multiple different kinds of thermometers to monitor the ambient temperature and the TempSpike is always between 10-20 degrees off. The other thing is charging. There have been multiple times when I plugged in the case and put the spike in it and I’ll come back and the spike will still be dead. The indicator light is also not particularly intuitive so I find myself looking at the manual pretty often.

review_title: Not worth it! Maybe that’s not true.
review_text: Worked two times wonderful. After that never connected again. A paper weight. Probe fail every time. Even when it says charged. Updated: they sent out a replacement.

I was torn between Meater, Meat Stick, and this model. A deal came up so I bought this one. I am pleased with it so far for its accuracy and ease of use, but I do have some complaints. First off I don't think it ever turns off. Maybe, I need to search the instructions more but so far I have not seen any way to turn it off. The probe is really thick so it is going to leave a large hole in your meat and you can't use it in a smaller/thinner piece of meat. I'm not sure if this is a negative but be warned the alarm that goes off when the meat is done on both your phone and the base is LOUD and sounds like a smoke alarm.

review_title: Great at close Blue Tooth range!
review_text: I love that this has no wires! It is accurate. Love that you can put it in the dishwasher, though I have not and probably will not. The charge seems to last long. I used to have a wifi temp gage for smoking/bbqing and I liked it but the probes were always out of calibration; so, that defeated the purpose. but what I liked about them when the were in calibration was the range. I could even go to the store or to work and be able to monitor the smoking process. This probe has advantages if you are sticking by your BBQ or smoker. It seemed to be out of range when I went to the bedroom and could not be sure if monitoring was occurring even with the out of range alarm on which sometimes did not work. Thanksgiving turkeys turned out great though.

review_title: As long as it charges… it is very helpful!
review_text: I bought this to take the guesswork out of a long cooking process. To be clear - I didn’t buy this to take the “easy way out” but instead have a better idea throughout slow cooks such as smoking meats. This thermometer is incredibly useful when smoking meats because you will see internal temperature and ambient temperature on your app. Typically smoking requires specific temperatures and this helps you know exactly where everything is at. The “estimated time left” doesn’t register well on hour long cooks and the box sometimes has trouble recognizing the probe to charge. I’ve had to reset the device a few times but when it’s charged and running, it’s hard to cook without it.

review_title: Returned the first one, kept the second one
review_text: The first one of these I got was totally mis-calibrated on both the internal temperature and the ambient. It was hopeless. I'm glad I went for "replacement" instead of "return" because the 2nd one is very good. Not quite as accurate as my wired thermometer, but it is within a few degrees, and the wireless option makes these very flexible. I use this and then double check with my trusty javelin Con: The advertised range (I think the ad said 500 feet when I bought mine) is wildly optimistic. I get about 70 feet out of mine.... maybe 100 on a good day. Still: I feel I got good value for money and I continue to use and enjoy this.

review_title: Great product, but missing one feature.
review_text: I love this temperature probe. It works exactly as advertised. I've used it in a smoker, charcoal grill and even on the stove top. The one feature that's missing, and I only realized it now that I just receive my second probe, is there is no way to differentiate the probes. In the app, the probes are enumerated 1,2,3 etc. But there is no way to know which probe is number 1 or 2. They need to make the ambient temperature part of the probe in different colors, then, instead of identifying by number in the app, they identify them by color. Having this feature would make them a 5 start all the way.

I really like how simple and easy it is to use this thermometer. I Purchased a year ago to date and I am now experiencing connectivity issues with the probe to the booster. The booster connects to my phone but no connection to probe I have tried 3 different chargers and shows that it charges but stops after about 30 minutes. Little disappointed because I rely on it so much it works great, For 100 dollars a year later need another one and used it maybe about 15 times give or take.

The overall data you receive from the temp spike is fine the battery on the probe and case are terrible I have plugged in the case to use the next day and the probe is totally dead every time I use this thing I can find any way to contact temp spike to see how to fix the issue. I think my one year warranty is about to expire if I didn't have the battery issues this would be a 5 star product.....Update got a number to temp-spike spoke with a rep and they're sending me a replacement unit

review_title: Updated to 4 stars from 1 after replacement probe worked perfectly
review_text: Ok, time for an update. I was sent a replacement probe and have now used that probe 8 times over the last several months with great results! I must have just gotten a bad unit initially. This wireless temperature probe works great, except the instructions do not give a clear suggestion on how to use the ambient temp with the internal temp. Otherwise it works great!!

review_text: This product with its app works great and can allow you to set alarms for certain temps and many other functions. Only negative I have is sometimes using the app and checking on temp. It will show disconnected for a minute or two but always connects back.

review_title: Wireless Meat Thermometer that Works well
review_text: I used this wireless thermometer one time on some chicken thighs and it worked well. It notified me both on the unit and on the app when the chicken reached the desired temperature (with a little hiccup explained below). The set up was pretty easy. There are some decent instructions for connecting the temperature probe to the base and connecting the base to my phone. The app was relatively simple, but only had basic information on temperatures for various meats. I think there is opportunity for the app to have recipes, tips etc. I don't like adding apps to my phone, so they need to be worth the space they take up. I also didn't love that I had to re-pair the unit after I had turned it off overnight. The reason I rated it 4 stars instead of 5 is because of the difficulty checking the temp on chicken thighs. The probe is pretty big (4.5 inches long and pretty thick). When I first put it in, I didn't insert it correctly. The alarm went off for 174 degrees, but the check-in was definitely NOT cooked. I looked through instructions and didn't see any for inserting. However, there was information in the app on properly inserting the probe. Apparently, a tiny notch on the probe needs to be covered. It was difficult on a small chicken thigh, but I was able to get it to work. For thicker cuts of meat, there shouldn't be issues. Just make sure you insert the probe like the picture in the app.

I love this for BBQing pork chops and steaks, it is very easy to use. After a year of use it stopped pairing to the base unit, I tried all of the recommended steps but couldn't get it going. Went to the web site and contacted support, it took less than 10 minutes to get a response. After a few more test it still would not work, they didn't hesitate or give me the run around, before the end of the day they have sent a new one free of charge.

review_title: Wow, talk about a great Wireless meat thermometer.
review_text: Wow, talk about a great Wireless meat thermometer. The.ThermoPro TempSpike 500 worked so well and it's very very accurate. I use it in my air fryer it was Little worried about how it would work, but I have to say I was very pleased. Now keep in mind. I am not a chef nor am I very good at cooking but my air fryer definitely makes me look that way, and this thermometer ensure I'd never overcook anything. The 500 foot range is great. It allows me to move around a house or go outside and so I have a connection to the thermometer so I don't have to worry about my food. Very easy to set up and a charge less for quite a while so if I were you, I'd buy this. It's well worth the money as I said before it's a great tool to have in the kitchen.

I’ve been using this for over three months and it works great. It makes grilling much easier since I don’t have to keep checking the meat, and the temperature has been accurate. Connecting to my phone was easy too. The probe gets pretty hot when taking it out, so just be careful. Overall, I really like it.

**Update 16 months after purchase.** Have used the device regularly, and love it, especially for larger, longer-cooking meats. However, the last two times I used it the probe appeared to not be holding its charge and would not last for the duration of the cook. I reached out to ThermoPro, and they sent me a new unit within a couple of days, direct to my home in Mexico. So, couple great customer service with a great product - awesome! Exceptional design, easy to use, mobile app is very good, hopefully it will stand the test of time (I think it will based on apparent manufacturing quality). Have used it three times in a week since I got it - whole chicken, tri-tip, turkey breast. Knowing both meat and ambient temperatures really minimizes trips out to the grill - this is huge during football game BBQs and inclement weather. My BBQ is at the back of the yard - zero issues with signal strength or communication from probe to booster to mobile app. 100% wireless design is far superior to others with wires that will inevitably lead to failure. Price point, function and quality combine for a 5 star solution.

I was impressed with the ThermoPro TempSpike right out of the box. This is an attractive and solidly engineered product. The app is easy to set up and pairing was flawless. The charging station took less than an hour to reach full charge, and the probe took a little over 5 hrs. The app is straightforward and seems to do everything that I could possibly need. Though, I wish the app used a numeric display for the battery levels, rather than two tiny icons. I’ve had no issues with the range, although I live in an apartment so I’ve never tested this beyond 50-100 feet. The critical test for me was accuracy. I recently bought, and returned, the ThermoPro TP902 because of accuracy issues, even though I really liked everything else about this unit. I did limited testing of the TempSpike by placing it in my tabletop Wolf convection oven alongside a trusted thermometer. I checked temperatures in 5 degree increments from 140 to 200F, and found good agreement between the two TempSpike sensors and my other thermometer. I’ll eventually test the ambient sensor at higher temperatures, but I bought this mainly to use in a smoker operating at 225-250F. A couple of things to consider. I found that when I ran my temperature test the ambient sensor response time lagged the internal sensor and it often took 5-10 minutes for the two sensors to stabilize and reach agreement. I really didn’t expect insta-read performance, so this shouldn’t be an issue for long, slow cooks. The downside to the internal sensor is that it can only be used for thick items due to the large diameter of the probe. Though, I’m not certain this is a valid criticism. Thin meats, vegetables, etc. cook very fast, so if you know your grill/oven temperatures you probably don’t need a constant-read thermometer and would be better off with insta-read. The only possible issue I can think of with this thermometer is the longevity of the two internal lithium batteries. Namely, how long before the batteries can no longer be reliably charged? What happens then - can the unit be serviced or is it necessary to buy a new one? So far I’ve never seen this issue addressed. This is a very cool product so I only hope that it will withstand many years of use. Bottom line - so far I’m very impressed with this product from ThermoPro and would enthusiastically recommend it to others.
Great product. Works as it should

review_title: my first try at a wi-fi probe
review_text: It was a bit expensive I thought and the old metal probe I have had for years still works so I read all the reviews and finally decided what the heck This is Amazon who has been top notch for taking care of me and if I didn't like it-- Kaboom back to my old stick it in the meat thermometer that is nearly a collector's item now. It took a little time for this old man to get it setup on my phone (easy but all this new tech you know) MY trial run -- cooked a meat loaf and what a hoot, a total new fun addition to the joy of cooking. I was able to set a temp alert at 150 and watch it climb while I did other things. No opening the oven door or running back to the kitchen-- At 150 which was one hour that usually I watch the clock for and was impressed. I started at 350 and when it hit my goal of 150 I increased the temp to 400F for 10 min and finished at 160F internal temp It gives you the freedom of getting out of the kitchen and do other things. I keep the cellphone with me but should I set it down, the external alarm would go off and it's loud thanks goodness Its is wonderful not to be chained to the stove and know exactly how your meal is progressing I am very glad I brought my cooking into the modern age-- It's wonderful and I deserve such a delightful tool. It is new so how its weathers time I can not comment on. I will be cooking homemade bread this weekend and excited to see the inside story happing with an alarm to remind me to take the bread out just incase.

Update: I was over the moon with this right out the gate. However, after about 3 uses the probe no longer connects with the app. I have tried everything that was listed on the ThermoPro website for problem solving, and called the ThermoPro helpline. I tried to contact them through their online forum, but it appears to be broken. I am at a loss and out $70. Original Review: I was honestly thinking that this was going to be too good to be true. It arrived yesterday and I let it charge overnight. Today I set it up, which couldn't have been easier. The directions have a QR code you scan that takes you right to the APP store. Once downloaded the probe paired with the APP immediately and I was off to the races. You insert the probe into your meat up to the indicated line, and then select a meat type from the menu, which sets the target finish temp. You should note that these appear to be USDA recommended temperatures, and not what our OXO thermometer refers to as "Chef Temperatures." We prefer more rare meat, so you also have the option of adding your own profiles with your own finish temperatures, which fixes this problem. The probe was spot on temperature wise (we double checked with an instant read thermometer). The coolest feature was the ambient temperature reading. It helped us better understand how warm our smoker actually was, as the temperature gauge on our smoker isn't very accurate. I also really appreciate how easy it was to clean, and that I didn't have to worry about getting any part of it wet. We were pleased to find that the booster makes noise, as well as your phone, when the meat reaches temperature. We are often going in and out while grilling, and it's nice to have double insurance that we hear the alarm when things are ready to be removed from the grill. The only thing I wasn't thrilled with was the estimated finish temp. It doesn't seem very accurate. Granted, we have only used this once, but we were only cooking simple chicken breast, and without opening the grill the estimated finish time jumped all over the place. By no means a deal breaker, but I just wouldn't count on it. Overall, we were super impressed with this and I can't wait to cook with it again. I would highly recommend!

Love this addition to cooking. Use it constantly when cooking chicken in the oven as temp is quite important. Can easily put it in the oven and walk away... it will surely tell you when it hits your temperature both on your device and on the unit itself. Have not found a way to turn the unit off from alarming when your temp is reached, which would save a lot of stress hearing the loud noise it makes. After using it and washing many of times, it hasn't degraded at all from when it first was used. Very easy to use as well both the unit and the app. Compared to other similar brands, very pleased with the construction of this ThermoPro TempSpike as I have been with all of their other products. Would highly recommend for anyone that is into cooking as a valuable tool to get temperatures spot on every time without having to constantly check.

Will upgrade to their newer high performance spikes, because this one worked really well when I was a beginner. It helped me understand how to navigate times and temps. Pretty accurate. You get what you pay for though. Good value for someone getting into the science of meats.

What a great company I got one of these thermometers over 2 years ago and never used it till just recently. It worked one time and I couldn’t get it to work again. I contacted the company and they help me trouble shoot it but still could get it to work. So they sent me a new one just like that. Amazing. Pride and ownership. They have a costumer for life.

So, let me tell you, I've had my ThermoPro for 2-3 years. I love it! I've used it for turkeys, brisket, ribs, chicken, steak, everything. The connectivity is great. Keep in mind it uses Bluetooth so you're not going to get a ton of range just like any other Bluetooth device. The app works really well and is very intuitive. Now, the probe suddenly stopped working on Thanksgiving of all days. I was so upset. The base would only connect if in "boost" but the probe would never connect. I did everything to fix it based off the ThermoPro site. I also contacted their customer service. We were unable to fix it so they sent me a replacement. Their customer service is OUTSTANDING. I have several other ThermoPro products and after their amazing service, I won't get any other product. Well done guys!

***EDIT*** The company reached out to me and sent me a new device. I was able to use it My last brisket, and was happy to see it had no battery issues for all 12 hour of the process. I have changed it to 5 stars as I believe the first one I received was just faulty and an outlier as to what the company produces. Customer service was great. ---------------------------------------------------My friend highly suggested this temp-probe to me, and as we both enjoy smoking meats I took his advice. It gives a lot more accurate ambient reading than the built in temp-gauge for most pellet grills and also gives a very accurate internal temp reading as well. I really like the device and the user friendly app, but the the battery life on my probe is so disappointing. Anybody who smokes meat will tell you it's not a short process, so I'd expect my probe to last longer than just 4 hours in the meat. It only allows me to make it though the first leg of my brisket. The battery of the probe survives just long enough to finish out the first target temp. Once it hits that temp I have to pull out the probe and try to get another quick charge on it before spiking it again to monitor the next target temp. Id like to think that my temp-spike might be faulty as my friend said he never had any issues with his battery life. Though, for me it makes the overall smoking process a little bit of a hassle cause I'm so reliant on knowong the temperature of the grill and the meat at all times. With the short battery life, it makes that very difficult. ***And yes I fully charge my device to 100% the night before I start my brisket process

After some research, I ended up buying this one seeing all the reviews. I immediately charged it and used it on Thanksgiving for a turducken. I I set the probe to about 165 and inserted it the way the instruction said. The alarm is really loud and went off at the correct time. It did not tell me how much time I had left, but I think that I need to look at that a little more. Overall, I’m really impressed with the item considering how much I paid. All the other ones seem to be really expensive. I really was looking for some thing a little moderately priced seeing as how I am a casual cook. It is also extremely easy to use, just follow the directions inside. You do have to download the app that goes with it, but it’s super easy to navigate. I also did notice that both times I’ve used it, I have to recharge it immediately. But then again I don’t know of a circumstance where you would use a probe twice in a row. But anyway, overall, I’m super impressed and I really do like it. I would definitely recommend this for anyone.
This one is so much better than the Chinese crap I first purchased. Holds a charge for a long time.

review_title: Good device with superb customer support
review_text: Purchased in Nov 24, used a couple of times, then not during the rest of winter. Recharged yesterday and I found the spike only registered if the booster was plugged in to power. Called their support line. The person I spoke with was a native English speaker who answered with no hold time. He almost immediately identified that the booster battery had failed. "I'll send you another one". No hassle. I did not have to repeat anything. Just the Amazon order number was all I needed. Wow! That's impressive customer support. The probe works well and is accurate compared with my instant read. Works in my airfryer. 6/22/25 Cooked a rolled turkey breast in our airfryer. The Tempspike worked perfectly, cooked the turkey at 350 degrees in 45 minutes instead of the two hours we usually use in our oven. It's a great product. We would have had no clue how long to cook without it.

review_title: If you use it in a smoker be aware of this.....
review_text: I've been using this great little tool for over a year now and I love it. It's convenient and accurate. Having said that I've just discovered something imprortant to know. I've been using it on the grill with good results but yestereday I used it in the smoker to smoke a pork shoulder for pulled pork. The smoking took 16 hours yet the probe battery survived the journey (barely). I am impressed. I did make sure it was fully charged before starting the cooking. However when I tried to recharge the probe and booster batteries I noticed that the bluetooth connection LED kept blinking. According to the instructions that meant the booster couldn't connect to the probe. This was despite the fact that the probe was inserted into the booster case for recharging. In that case the connection LED should NOT be blinking. Looking at the probe's top cap I noticed a significant buildup of smoke residue. The residue was thick enough to prevent a good contact with the charger terminal thus the probe's battery never got charged and the booster was looking for a device with a drained battery. A good scrubbing of the top cap terminal on the probe (with a light touch from an emery board) cleaned the top cap enough to allow the booster to charge the probe properly. If you use it in a smoker, make sure to clean the smoke residue off of the top of the probe when finished or the battery won't charge properly.

Been wanting to get one of these, and finally grabbed one on a pretty good sale ThermoPro had. Used it for the first time on some tuna steaks last weekend. Was nice to have an extra point of measurement so I could have 2 steaks being monitored internally, one on the edge, one in the center of the smoker. I've learned very quickly there is a notable cooking gradient from the edges of the smoker to the center (center is cooler). This is somewhat of a flaw based on how electric pellet smokers work. With this probe I was able to quantify this, noting about a 20*F difference between the smoker's stated temp on the PID, and the actual measured ambient temp in the middle of the chamber. The internal temp correlated perfectly with the smoker's built in wired probe at the start, and you could easily see the temp increasing faster in the steak closest to the edge of the rack over the course of the cook. This allowed me to shuffle the meat around to even things out. Definitely glad I picked this up!

We have used this thermometer every time we have a big group of people where we need to cook a big slice of meat. Turkey, pork butt, ham, prime rib, you name it and this thermometer has got the job done. It is great value for your money and very durable. We love it so much that we have gifted one to my mother as well as my father-in-law and they can’t stress enough how easy it is to detect the temperature of food. We all love that we can hook it up to our phone and that it beeps every time the temperature reaches its limit. It is very convenient and easy to read.
I used it on beef brisket loved it. It gave me temperature inside the meat and temperature in the grill. It also gave me an alarm when the temperature in the grill was too high.
It registered the temperature accurately and is easy to use.

review_title: Excellent customer service and effective device
review_text: I love this device. The app allows me to easily set temp thresholds that are equally easy to read. You can chart the entire cook. I don't use the magnet much but it does hold well. I have some issues cleaning the device, especially on the black end. It's been great for 3 years but it stopped charging to 100%, only to 50% and would discharge in minutes. I wrote TempSpike about the issue and they offered suggestions. When those did not work, they sent me a brand new device at no cost. I had an issue with a wired probe about 5 years ago, wrote them about the issue, and they sent me a new probe then too. The support and customer service is EXCELLENT!!! I have several friends that smoke too and if I haven't already told them about these devices, I sent them as gifts.

This thing is awesome. I got it because my old one had a cord and the probe was so long that it would usually read on the high end. This thing is nice and short. Also one thing I didn't know it did when I got it was that it gives you an estimated done time based off how quickly the temps going on. Was a nice surprise with testing it out on the Thanksgiving turkey. Also, the alarm for when it hits the done temperature sounds like, and is as loud as a smoke alarm. Scared the crap out of me when it went off on my phone lol.

My probe stopped working, however, still giving this 5 stars because their customer service is excellent, and because I did love it while it was working! They were able to replace mine at no cost to me. No fuss at all. Thanks!

review_title: I am totally blown away by the TempSpike!
review_text: My TempSpike arrived yesterday and I immediately tried it with a smoked chicken using a Pit Barrel Junior. To my surprise and skepticism, it worked perfectly! I would have thought that the all-metal construction of the Pit Barrel would have blocked the Bluetooth signal from the TempSpike to my phone, but that wasn't the case at all. As instructed, I did place the booster a couple feet away from the smoker, but never needed to plug it into a power outlet. I then went inside, about 30 feet away and on the other side of an impact glass door, and had no trouble following the temperature of both the pit and the food. When I removed the chicken from the smoker, I checked the reported temperature of the food with a ThermaPen and found the chicken to be within 1 degree of the TempSpike! Surprisingly, this is also very easy to clean. After it's cooled, simply run it under warm water with a little soap and rinse it clean. Electronics able to survive soap and water? Amazing!! The only thing it doesn't do is regulate the pit temperature like a BBQ Guru, but I suppose the people at ThermoPro are working on that as I write this! In addition to BBQing and smoking food, this probe is perfect for the oven or even sous vide. I haven't tried either yet, but truly, the TempSpike is a real game changer for the home cook. For the price, this is a great addition to my kitchen and I look forward to using it often!

review_title: A must have for cooking meat
review_text: This thermometer is a game changer for cooking meat. I got tired of jamming a thermometer into my turkey periodically to see the temperature but never really knowing when it would be done. This handy little device can not only stay in the meat in the oven, you also get continuous readings presented graphically right on your phone. The app accurately predicted when my turkey would hit my target temperature so I could let it rest out of the oven. More importantly, this thermometer and app allowed us to time the prep of all our sides so we could eat on time.
Pleased with product - exactly as advertised - easier to use than I expected.

review_title: To put it simply, I would buy this again.
review_text: I have used the TempSpike on at least a few dozen cooks now. Grilling Steak and Chicken, I have also done a low and slow Pork Butt on the smoker. The app is pretty easy to use, if you can use your smart phone, you will figure it out. The range is good, no issues going from the deck to around the house. I have compared the temperature accuracy to another brand thermometer (costs about $30 more) with very similar results. I have not had any issues grilling at 550deg and the battery life held up fine for a 16hour smoke at 225deg. Good device, I've had it for 6 months and now that Summer is here, it's been getting a good bit of use.

This is probably the very best purchase I’ve ever made through Amazon! If you check my other reviews you’ll see I don’t give out five stars very often. I would seriously give this ten stars. It’s perfect! With the recent holidays I’ve used it more frequently than usual and remain amazed at how easy it is to use, how accurate it is, it’s well built, holds a charge forever, looks great, and more. I originally bought this because I bought a new Weber grill with a wired remote temp probe and I have never gotten the Weber probe to work remotely to my phone. My orange temp spike not only actually works great but it is truly wireless. My only regret is that I haven’t purchased a two-pack (yet). Serious - this is great. I wish they made more of the products that Amazon sells!

review_title: Exceptional performance in the Oven or the Smoker
review_text: I was getting weary of the vague temperature indications from my smoker, and who the heck knows what the real weight of that roast going in the oven? "Cook for xx minutes per pound and ..." Who has patience for that? Not me. Enter this wireless temperature probe. Great performance. The probe goes in the meat inside the smoker. The booster/charger goes on the window sill closest to the smoker. Data is streaming live within the reasonable distances from the booster. Love it. Ditto for that roast in the oven, though the booster doesn't need to be on the window sill, as the kitchen counter works fine. Still love it. I've tested accuracy between several mechanical and electronic thermometers and they all read within a couple degrees (F) of each other. None of them are traceable to NIST, but don't give me any flak about that. Not everything needs to be traceable and precise to 4 significant digits. Cooking isn't rocket surgery, and as a foodie with a love for cooking, especially sous vide steaks, roasts and brisket; this thing is more than accurate enough. Highly recommended.

This is a top notch product all the way around. The App was easy to load and has many interesting features including useful, easy-to-understand graphics. The feature I liked the best is the "ambient" temperature information, including high and low setpoints. This is probably available on similar wireless models but this is the first time I've had one with this feature. This info (ambient temp) allowed me to verify my built in thermometer was correct and the high alarm feature allowed me to stay inside and not constantly check the BGE temperature during the cook. The graphics of the internal temperature (with alarms also) was very good and informative with just a glance (good Human-Factors graphics engineering) using both colors, digital readout and graphs to display information. The holding/charging box for the thermometer is sturdy with an eclectic design. The thermometer itself is sturdy and long (which is very useful for thicker meats). The only mistake I made was not charging it before use. Nonetheless, it charged in about 30 minutes which allowed me to use it shortly after putting the meat on the grill. I would recommend this product to anyone who roasts meat, particularly on an outdoor grill.

review_title: Accurate and took the guesswork out of cooking
review_text: I used the TempSpike wireless Bluetooth thermometer to make a mini pan roast, and it came out beautifully. The temperature readings and timing were accurate, which really mattered because not all ovens heat evenly; and mine definitely needed extra time to reach the doneness I wanted. Because of this thermometer, I was able to monitor the internal temperature closely and pull the roast out at exactly the right moment. It completely took the guesswork out of cooking and gave me confidence that the meat was cooked perfectly. I’d definitely recommend this for anyone who wants more precise results when cooking or roasting.

review_title: Ambient Temperature is not close to accurate.  I HAVE UPDATED MY REVIEW.
review_text: This is supposed to have two temperature readings, the internal and the ambient. The ambient was not even close to accurate. I'm now cross-testing the internal with 2 other thermometers. It appears to be close, but still off by a few degrees. UPDATE: After my initial review, I was contacted by the folks at ThermoPro. After receiving the best customer care I've experienced in a VERY long time, I have changed my rating to FIVE stars due to the level of authentic care and concern the folks at ThermoPro exhibited in resolving my concerns. Furthermore, I would recommend anyone in the market for a wireless thermometer to consider ThermoPro simply because the folks at ThermoPro stand TALL behind their product in a manner that is relatively rare these days. THANK YOU THERMOPRO! AMBIENT AND INTERNAL TEMPS WERE SPOT ON SINCE YOU TOOK CARE OF MY ISSUE. I look forward to referring you and your product to all my friends and family seeking a wireless system for indoor and outdoor cooking.

I am very particular about kitchen thermometers. A few years ago I switched over all of my thermometers to Thermoworks models as they are the industry standard in precision and accuracy. But Thermoworks doesn’t make a wireless Bluetooth probe. At least not yet. So I researched the available options and landed on this model. The app that is necessary to use the probe is a bit simplistic with pre-set target temperatures that are way to high (pork at 160*? What is this, 1965?). But there is an edit function that allows you to reset your target temperatures to your liking. (Pork is now set at 145* which still leaves room for some carryover.) But most importantly the probe is accurate. I have used it three times so far on three different cook—Sea Bass at 140*, Ribeyes at 125* and Meatloaf at 168* and each time when the target temperature was reached I immediately double-checked the internal temperature with my trusty Thermo-Pen and all three times the temperature readings were within 0-2 degrees of one another. That’s all anyone can ever ask of a kitchen thermometer.

review_title: Great product, exceptional customer service with a real phone number.
review_text: I have used my tempspike for over 2 years and love it. However, recently it developed a problem and when I contacted customer service I experienced an unusual throwback experience. Unlike many companies today they: 1. Publish their phone number and 2. The person that answers is competent not only with the product but also with the English language. In summary, they stand behind their product and replaced the entire unit which I received within a week. If you are currently comparing products, this is the one to go with.

review_title: Good addition to the kitchen, great customer service
review_text: Been using instant reed thermometers for a while, and it's really the way you should cook. You can never tell just by looking. Nothing looks done and you wait until it does and it's burned. This is a less expensive alternative to another brand that is very heavily marketed. I got this for about 1/2 the price of the other. My only complaint is they tout that the range to you cell phone is advertised as 500 ft..... Im getting maybe 100, and that's a stretch. You walk to the front of the house, and all of a sudden there's an alarm from you phone that you're disconnected. I've used this about 1/2 dozen times. Im happy. I should add a wired thermometer, to compare accuracy. We'll see Edit: The first unit I had died about 3 months out. I called and spoke with an American in customer service. After trying a few things with no joy, he admitted that some of the first ones had a flaw and he shipped a new one, no real questions asked. I called recently to make note of the advertised vs real range of connection (its really standard Bluetooth, nowhere near 500 ft. Boom... another new one sent out. Absolutely unbelievable customer service. Unbeliveable. Have no fear in buying this.
Works great! No more guessing or stabbing the meat to see if it is done!

I loved how it was signaling from Traeger at outside corner of my garage on a 2700 sq.ft. home and retained connection through the walls at opposite end of home then throughout all rooms even on the opposite side midway point of the home in my kitchen all without a single disruption. I was smoking a Pork Butt for 11 hours and monitored it for the last 8 hours of smoking and surprised it was so great. Now the bad part, I went until the reading shown 190 degrees and pulled the meat then immediately probed with a ThermoPro quick probe and it was reading 196 degrees. This is quite a temperature difference but will work for me as I will just know to take if out a little early and do a quick probe to see where the temperature really is at. The worse scenerio would be to have a slightly better accuracy but have continued connection drops like i see in reviews of other remote thermometers and having to end up walking outside to see the reading as it would defeat the purpose for buying for remote readability.

Originally I was not happy with this purchase. The way it works is the "spike" connects with its "booster" (which doubles as its charger and storage box) and the booster, via an ap, connects with your phone. It's supposed to come from the factory with the spike and booster already paired. Mine were not. I could connect my phone to the booster, but despite repeated attempts following the directions precisely the spike and booster would not connect. I contacted customer service via chat and explained the issue. The customer service rep asked me a couple of questions *click/click/click* "Please give me your address. I'll send you a new one." That easily, handled. No BS, no pushback, just took care of it. And when I received the replacement, it was an upgraded unit. Smokin' some ribs right now, it's working flawlessly. Thank you Thermo Pro. A definite recommend!

review_title: Excellent customer service and a company that stands behind its products.
review_text: My TempPro TempSpike TP961 thermometer developed a connection issue that I could not resolve despite going through the recommended troubleshooting steps. I contacted TempPro support, explained the problem, and provided the information they requested. They were responsive, professional, and quickly approved a replacement at no cost. Any electronic product can occasionally have a problem. What matters to me is how the company responds when something goes wrong, and TempPro handled this very well. Their willingness to stand behind their product says a lot about the company and gives me confidence in buying from them again. I really appreciate the support.
Grateful that I purchased this item , I tried it and it does exactly what it says it does .
What a great idea. My hubby loved it for the smoker.
